WASSA-2017 Shared Task on Emotion Intensity
The WASSA-2017 Shared Task on Emotion Intensity is a competitive evaluation workshop in natural language processing focused on measuring the intensity of emotions in text, where competitors tested their predictive models.

Popović

Machine Translation
**Machine Translation (MT)** is a major subfield of computational linguistics, artificial intelligence, and natural language processing (NLP) dedicated to investigating and deploying software to automatically convert text or speech from one natural human language into another while preserving semantic meaning. As both a foundational technological domain and an advanced natural language generation task, it encompasses language pairs ranging from high-resource languages to pairs such as English to Setswana.

Technologically, Machine Translation encompasses both statistical and neural approaches, commonly leveraging neural language models, sequence-to-sequence frameworks, and neural encoder-decoder architectures. The field has continually evolved through the availability of large-scale datasets as well as innovations such as character-based and character-enhanced embeddings and adversarial training techniques. Operating within this domain presents several core computational challenges, including linguistic ambiguity, out-of-vocabulary entities, and non-standard speech, making the task highly receptive to techniques like word sense disambiguation.

Beyond its primary translation objectives, Machine Translation has significantly influenced broader NLP applications. Its architectures inspired developments in sequence-to-sequence dialogue systems and neural sentence simplification, while its evaluation methodologies—most notably metrics like BLEU and perplexity, as well as semantic textual similarity measures—have been widely adopted across dialogue evaluation and utilized as hand-crafted similarity features in semantic textual similarity (STS) models.

DBpedia
A crowd-sourced community project and structured knowledge base that extracts data from Wikipedia, utilized for cross-lingual knowledge graph tasks.<SEP>A structured knowledge base and community project extracting information from Wikipedia, used as a knowledge source and infobox property repository for training the QA model.<SEP>DBpedia is a community and knowledge repository project that extracts structured infobox properties and n-triples from Wikipedia for training models.<SEP>DBpedia is a community project and open-domain knowledge base repository that extracts structured factual data from Wikipedia.<SEP>DBpedia is a community project that extracts structured knowledge and n-triples from the Wikipedia repository to enable semantic querying.<SEP>DBpedia is an open knowledge base project that extracts structured semantic information and triples from Wikipedia.<SEP>DBpedia is an open-knowledge base and Semantic Web resource accessible via SPARQL queries to support entity disambiguation.<SEP>The project and organization maintaining the structured knowledge base from which resources were selected for the verbalization experiment.

Named Entity Recognition and Disambiguation
Named Entity Recognition and Disambiguation is a computational task that identifies proper names in text and links them to knowledge base entries.

Topic Modelling
A text processing category of techniques suggested as a potential method to alleviate the influence of high-frequency words across different thematic contexts.<SEP>An advanced text-mining method proposed as future work to improve user matching and account tracking across social networks.<SEP>Topic modelling is a text-processing technique proposed to analyze context across small segments of source text prior to translation to guide disambiguation.

Syntactic Disambiguation
Syntactic disambiguation is the challenge of identifying the correct grammatical structure and verbal tense of sentences in natural language processing and translation.

Semantic Disambiguation
Semantic disambiguation is the process of distinguishing between the different senses of polysemous and homonymous words within a specific context.

Ontology
A formal conceptualization of a knowledge domain defining classes, subclasses, and relations between entities, commonly specified using OWL.<SEP>An ontology is a formal representation of knowledge and relations among concepts and properties, used within Semantic Web frameworks to support translation and reasoning.

SPARQL
A semantic query language designed to retrieve and manipulate data stored in RDF format.<SEP>A semantic query language used to retrieve and manipulate data stored in Resource Description Framework (RDF) triple format within Linked Data.<SEP>SPARQL is a semantic query language designed to retrieve and manipulate data stored in Resource Description Framework (RDF) format and Semantic Web knowledge bases.<SEP>SPARQL is a semantic query language designed to retrieve and manipulate data stored in Resource Description Framework (RDF) format.<SEP>SPARQL is a standard query language and protocol designed for querying Semantic Web data stored in RDF format.

Reasoners
Reasoners are algorithmic inference engines used in the Semantic Web to deduce logical relationships and rules, notable for run-time performance limitations in real-time MT.

Pre-Editing
Pre-editing is a translation workflow technique where ambiguous words are identified and annotated in the source text prior to running machine translation.

Post-Editing
Post-editing is a translation workflow technique where Semantic Web tools or human reviewers refine and correct the target language translation output.

Named Entities
Named entities are proper nouns, names, and cultural references that often overlap with common nouns across languages and cause translation errors.<SEP>Named entities are real-world entities identified in natural language texts, frequently appearing as informal name variants in social media posts.<SEP>Named entities are structured real-world referents, such as persons or locations, whose identification is challenged by informal variations.

Ristoski

and world facts for dialogue models.<SEP>A free online encyclopedia whose text corpus was utilized to train both fastText and the Baroni semantic embedding models.<SEP>A multilingual online A country referenced in connection with online trolls identified on Twitter.<SEP>A country whose Russian language dataset was analyzed in comparison with annotator agreement.<SEP>Russia is a country exhibiting false-positive language occurrences in both web-crawled and Twitter datasets.<SEP>Russia is a country referenced as an example geographic location of a user reading foreign language web content.<SEP>Russia is a nation mentioned as an illustrative example of the nationality-adjective morphological transformation rule.<SEP>Russia is identified as being over-represented in Twitter data relative to its population size.<SEP>Russia is the country associated with the state-linked Internet Research Agency (IRA) troll accounts that mimicked US users.<SEP>Russia is the country of origin for the Internet Research Agency and its coordinated troll operations on social media.<SEP>Russia is the country where the IRA social media influence campaign originated.

WMT English-German Translation Task
The WMT English-German translation task is a shared machine translation evaluation benchmark on which entity linking models achieved significant evaluation metric improvements.

Non-Standard Speech
Non-standard speech is a linguistic category encompassing colloquial expressions, slang, multi-word expressions, abbreviations, and idioms that challenge MT systems.

Entity Linking
A natural language processing task that identifies and links named entity mentions in text to corresponding nodes in a knowledge base.<SEP>Entity Linking is a technique that identifies entity mentions in text and connects them to corresponding entries in reference knowledge bases or graphs.<SEP>Entity linking is a subfield of information processing and knowledge representation concerned with connecting named mentions to specific entities in a knowledge graph.

Knowledge Graph Embeddings
Knowledge Graph Embeddings are vector representations of entities and relations from a knowledge graph, used in neural models to preserve semantic structure and contextual information.

RDF
A foundational framework and data specification for representing information in the Semantic Web.<SEP>Resource Description Framework (RDF) is a key foundational Semantic Web data representation language and standard data model.<SEP>Resource Description Framework (RDF) is a standard data model and language of the Semantic Web used to represent information and triples in knowledge bases.<SEP>Resource Description Framework, a foundational semantic web standard used for representing structured data via subject-predicate-object triples.<SEP>Resource Description Framework, a standard model for data interchange and knowledge representation structured as subject-predicate-object triples.

FOAF
Friend of a Friend (FOAF) is a Semantic Web ontology and vocabulary that describes persons, their activities, interests, and relations to other people and objects.

SIOC
Semantically-Interlinked Online Communities (SIOC) is an ontology used to describe online community information, including topics and user forum interactions.

Word2vec
Word2vec is a family of model architectures used to generate word and concept vector representations based on linguistic contexts.<SEP>Word2vec is a foundational family of model architectures and software implementations used to learn distributed vector representations of words.<SEP>Word2vec is a natural language processing model and tool used to learn continuous vector representations of words from Twitter data.<SEP>Word2vec is a neural word embedding approach used to generate vector representations carrying semantic meaning.

Out-of-Vocabulary
Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) refers to words, names, or phrases encountered during inference that were not present in the system's training dataset.

Multi-Word Expressions
Multi-Word Expressions (MWE) are lexical items composed of multiple words whose collective meaning cannot always be inferred directly from the individual words.

Evaluation Metrics
Evaluation Metrics in machine translation, including BLEU, METEOR, and CHRF3, quantify the lexical and semantic quality of generated translations against reference texts.<SEP>Evaluation metrics are performance criteria used to score classification systems, including macroaveraged recall, positive and negative averaged F1 score, and accuracy.<SEP>Evaluation metrics represent quantitative and qualitative criteria—such as BLEU, perplexity, and embedding-based measures—used to evaluate dialogue systems.<SEP>Evaluation metrics, including BLEU, METEOR, and chrF, are quantitative evaluation methods used to assess the quality and correctness of generated text against gold-standard references.

Newstest Datasets
The Newstest Datasets (2014–2018) are benchmark evaluation sets used in the annual WMT shared translation tasks to assess translation model performance.

Brazilian National Council for Scientific and Technological Development
A Brazilian government agency (CNPq) dedicated to the promotion of scientific and technological research, which supported the research.

Knowledge Graphs
A structural representation of entities and relations used to augment conversational agents with factual and contextual common sense.<SEP>Structured representations of real-world knowledge used in multilingual tasks, entity linking, and fact checking.

Natural Language Processing
**Natural Language Processing (NLP)** is a comprehensive domain and subfield of

Model Compression
A broad field of techniques aimed at reducing the parameter size, memory footprint, and latency of deep learning models.<SEP>A category of machine learning techniques, such as weight pruning, matrix factorization, and knowledge distillation, designed to reduce model size and latency.<SEP>A category of techniques in machine learning aimed at reducing model size, memory footprint, and computational overhead while retaining performance.<SEP>A collection of deep learning techniques designed to reduce memory consumption and computational cost of neural networks, particularly in low-resource environments.<SEP>A machine learning paradigm aimed at reducing model parameter sizes and latency for memory-intensive or latency-critical deployment scenarios.<SEP>Model compression refers to techniques used to reduce the size, memory footprint, and latency of deep learning models.

Knowledge Distillation
A compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large teacher model to a smaller student model by minimizing loss functions.<SEP>A compression technique where a compact student model learns to replicate the behaviors and representations of a larger teacher model.<SEP>A machine learning technique where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behaviors and representations of a larger teacher model.<SEP>A model compression technique where a compact student model is trained to approximate the function of a larger teacher model.<SEP>A model compression technique where a compact student model is trained to reproduce the behavior and representations of a larger teacher model.<SEP>A model compression technique where a smaller, compact student model is trained to approximate the representations and functions of a larger model.<SEP>Knowledge distillation is a compression and training technique where a compact student model learns to reproduce the behavior of a larger teacher model.

Germany
A European country whose German language tweet dataset was evaluated across multiple annotators.<SEP>A European country whose parliamentary proceedings have been analyzed in computational political science and ideology prediction studies.<SEP>A country in Central Europe whose language, institutions, and government ministry are referenced in the context of translation research and funding.<SEP>Germany is a European country whose obituary traditions, visual elements, and textual norms were examined in comparative cultural research.<SEP>Germany is a country whose obituaries were analyzed by Barth2013 for visual and textual elements.<SEP>Germany is the European nation associated with the German language texts, corpora, and transcripts gathered from public domain sources.

Brazil
A South American nation whose national research council provided grant funding for scientific and technological development.<SEP>Brazil is a country cited as an example where the UN language ground-truth dataset has no available language demographic information.

LIMBO
A research project supported and funded by the German Federal Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure.

OPAL
A research project funded by the German Federal Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure.

Weight Pruning
A model compression baseline method that iteratively removes non-essential weights from neural network matrices.<SEP>A model compression technique that eliminates non-essential or low-magnitude parameters to reduce memory footprint and latency in neural networks.<SEP>A model compression technique that eliminates redundant or unimportant parameters to introduce sparsity into neural network matrices.<SEP>A model compression technique that induces sparsity by eliminating redundant parameters or weights within neural network matrices.<SEP>A model compression technique that removes connections, neurons, or filters from deep neural networks to produce sparse architectures without significant loss in accuracy.<SEP>An unstructured compression method that induces sparsity in a neural network by setting small weights to zero via a binary mask.<SEP>Weight pruning is a model compression method that removes redundant or low-importance weights to decrease model size and computational complexity.

Matrix Factorization
A mathematical compression technique that decomposes a parameter matrix into the product of two lower-rank matrices.<SEP>A mathematical decomposition technique applied in model compression to factorize parameter matrices into lower ranks, saving memory and compute.<SEP>A mathematical decomposition technique used as a model compression baseline, often utilizing SVD.<SEP>A mathematical decomposition technique, such as Singular Value Decomposition, used to approximate parameter matrices with lower-rank representations.<SEP>A model compression approach that decomposes weight matrices into products of lower-dimensional matrices using techniques like Singular Value Decomposition.<SEP>Matrix Factorization is a mathematical technique category used in prior works to derive latent continuous representations for textual similarity.<SEP>Matrix factorization is a mathematical and compression technique used in LadaBERT to decompose weight matrices and reduce model parameters.

Fact Checking
An automated information verification task in natural language processing that evaluates factual claims against external knowledge bases.

Word Alignment
A subtask in machine translation that determines translational correspondences between words in parallel text corpora.<SEP>Word alignment is a natural language processing technique that maps corresponding words between source and target language sentence pairs.

Weight Quantization
A model compression method that reduces the bit-precision of weights within neural networks, ranging from 32-bit floating point down to 8-bit or binary representations.

Han
A researcher who proposed reducing neural network storage and computation by eliminating unimportant connections to create sparse networks.

Li
A researcher who introduced an acceleration method for convolutional neural networks by pruning filters together with their connecting filter maps.

Ye
A researcher who argued that small weights are critical for maintaining the overall performance of deep neural network models.

Hu
A researcher who introduced a data-driven approach to prune zero-activation neurons iteratively based on intermediate feature maps.<SEP>Hu is a computer science researcher and co-creator of the Hu-Liu opinion lexicon used for sentiment analysis.<SEP>Hu is a researcher who proposed hierarchical LSTM models to predict events by generating descriptive word sequences.

Zhu
A researcher who empirically compared large sparse neural models with smaller dense models of similar parameter sizes.

Gupta
A researcher who co-authored an empirical comparison between large sparse models and smaller dense models alongside Zhu.<SEP>Gupta is a researcher who proposed the GIRNet multitask recurrent neural network architecture.

Wen
A researcher who utilized group lasso as a regularization technique during training to produce sparse neural network models.

Louizos
A researcher who investigated learning sparse neural networks through L0 regularization.

Sainath
A researcher who studied low-rank matrix factorization of deep neural network layers for acoustic modeling.

Xu
A researcher who applied singular value decomposition to deep neural network acoustic models for parameter reduction.<SEP>A researcher who developed a specialized dataset incorporating geolocation and external restaurant information to facilitate food recognition tasks.

Acharya
A researcher who compressed word embedding layers using matrix factorization for text classification tasks.

Winata
A researcher who evaluated low-rank matrix factorization across multiple natural language processing tasks.

Zhou
A researcher who demonstrated that quantizing neural network weights to 8-bits maintains model performance.<SEP>Researcher who, along with colleagues in 2017, provided benchmark test sets and evaluations for headline generation.<SEP>Zhou is a researcher who, with colleagues in 2017, provided benchmark test sets and baseline scores for headline generation.

Choi
A researcher who developed methods to identify controversial topics and sub-topics within news articles.<SEP>A researcher who proposed a Hessian-weighted k-means clustering algorithm to improve weight quantization in neural networks.

Deep Neural Networks (DNNs)
A class of machine learning models with high architectural complexity whose memory consumption and computational demands necessitate model compression.

Natural Language Understanding (NLU)
A subfield of artificial intelligence and NLP encompassing benchmark tasks and public datasets used to evaluate language model performance.

Convolution Neural Network (CNN)
A class of deep neural networks accelerated by pruning entire filters and filter maps.

BERT
A bidirectional transformer language model trained on large-scale unsupervised corpora that achieves state-of-the-art performance across various natural language processing tasks.<SEP>A class of large pre-trained transformer language models targeted by various model compression and acceleration techniques.<SEP>A language representation model built on the Transformer architecture designed to leverage unlabeled text data.<SEP>A pre-trained contextualized language representation model category utilized for joint utterance-table schema encoding.<SEP>A pre-trained neural language model architecture utilized within the utterance-table encoder to jointly encode user utterances and database column headers.<SEP>A pre-trained transformer-based language model architecture consisting of embedding, encoder, and classification layers.<SEP>A pre-trained transformer-based language model architecture that serves as the foundation and baseline for various downstream models and compression techniques.<SEP>A pre-trained transformer-based language model whose architecture and parameters serve as the foundation for the STR-encoder.<SEP>A pre-trained transformer-based language representation model employed as a baseline and an arbitrator in the experimental framework.<SEP>A prominent category of transformer-based pre-trained language models adapted in the study as a shared parameter layer for joint learning.<SEP>A transformer-based language representation model architecture category used as a structural basis for the arbitrator module.<SEP>BERT is a category of pre-trained transformer language model known for its strong feature extraction capabilities, utilized as a base structure for downstream NLP tasks.<SEP>BERT is a category of pretrained contextualized language representation models utilized to encode concatenated sequences of user utterances and database column headers.<SEP>BERT is a pre-trained bidirectional transformer language representation model whose parameters and feature extraction capabilities are leveraged in the proposed architecture.<SEP>BERT is a pre-trained language model architecture whose self-attention encoder and structure serve as the foundation for the proposed shared task representation encoder.<SEP>BERT is a pre-trained masked language model used both as a target text classifier and as a generator for token replacements and insertions in adversarial attacks.<SEP>BERT is a pre-trained transformer masked language model and classifier used both to generate adversarial mask perturbations and as a target classification model.<SEP>BERT is a pre-trained transformer-based language model architecture widely used in natural language processing.<SEP>Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, a deep language model utilizing the Transformer encoder for self-supervised representation learning.

LadaBERT
A BERT-oriented model compression approach that achieves superior performance and faster training speed across multiple compression ratios.<SEP>A lightweight BERT model compression framework and model family that combines SVD-based matrix factorization, weight pruning, and knowledge distillation.<SEP>A lightweight adaptation framework for BERT that applies hybrid compression and knowledge distillation to create compact models.<SEP>A model compression framework that combines SVD-based matrix factorization, weight pruning, and multi-level knowledge distillation to achieve varying parameter reduction ratios.<SEP>LadaBERT is a lightweight model compression pipeline that creates adaptive BERT models using matrix factorization, weight pruning, and knowledge distillation.

BERT-PKD
A BERT compression baseline model outperformed by LadaBERT-1 under a 2.5x compression ratio.<SEP>A BERT compression baseline that initializes a student model by selecting specific layers from a pre-trained BERT-Base teacher model.<SEP>Patient Knowledge Distillation, a model compression baseline extracting knowledge from intermediate Transformer layers into a 3-layer student model.

TinyBERT
A compact student Transformer model comprising 14.5M parameters across 4 layers, utilized as a baseline and as the basis for multi-level distillation constraints.<SEP>A compressed BERT baseline model that relies on pure knowledge distillation from scratch and data augmentation.<SEP>A compressed BERT model framework that employs knowledge distillation constraints on embedding and intermediate layers.<SEP>A state-of-the-art BERT compression baseline outperformed by LadaBERT-3 under a 7.5x compression ratio.

Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
A widely used matrix factorization method that generalizes eigendecomposition to provide the optimal low-rank matrix approximation under the Frobenius norm.

Acoustic Modeling
A discipline within speech processing that models relationships between audio signals and phonetic units using deep neural networks.<SEP>A domain in speech processing where deep neural network layers are compressed using low-rank matrix factorization and singular value decomposition.

Text Classification
A fundamental Natural Language Processing task that involves assigning predefined categories or labels to input text sequences or documents.<SEP>A fundamental natural language processing task category focused on assigning predefined labels or categories to text sequences.<SEP>A fundamental natural language processing task that involves assigning predefined categories or labels to open-ended text.<SEP>A machine learning task formulation involving predicting discrete labels from input text sequences, used as a baseline framing for dialogue action prediction.<SEP>A natural language processing task aimed at categorizing text sequences into discrete predicted class distributions.<SEP>A natural language processing task that categorizes text, applied within dialogue systems for tasks such as emotion recognition and turn-taking arbitration.<SEP>A natural language processing task where word embedding layers are compressed using low-rank matrix factorization.<SEP>Text Classification is a general category of NLP tasks that involves categorizing text into predefined classes or labels.<SEP>Text Classification is a natural language processing task focused on categorizing text inputs, serving as the primary evaluation target for adversarial attacks.<SEP>Text classification is a core natural language processing task category focused on assigning predefined labels or categories to text sequences.<SEP>Text classification is a foundational natural language processing category focused on assigning predefined labels or categories to text documents.<SEP>Text classification is an NLP task performed directly from raw character sequences using convolutional neural networks by Zhang et al.<SEP>Text classification is an automated natural language processing task that assigns predefined labels or categories to text documents.

Sparsity-Induced Models
A class of neural network models that encourage zero-valued parameters during training using regularizers like group lasso and L0 regularization.

Binarized Neural Networks
An extreme class of quantized neural networks containing 1-bit binary weights and activations.

Incremental Network Quantization
A weight quantization technique that converts full-precision models into low-precision networks via weight partitioning, groupwise quantization, and retraining.

Variational Network Quantization
A weight quantization approach that formulates neural network parameter precision reduction as a variational inference problem.

GroupReduce
A neural language model compression technique that applies low-rank matrix approximation to vocabulary partitions.

Choi et al.
Researchers who investigated the drawbacks of conventional k-means quantization methods and proposed a Hessian-weighted k-means clustering algorithm.

Chen et al.
Chen et al. refers to researchers who proposed a method for generating sense embeddings utilized to represent words and contexts in a shared vector space.<SEP>Researchers who applied knowledge distillation to object detection tasks using modified loss functions and adaptation layers.

Li et al.
A research team that in 2017 introduced adversarial training for open-domain dialogue generation combining reinforcement learning and generative adversarial networks.<SEP>Researchers who developed frameworks leveraging knowledge distillation for learning from noisy labels and compressed DNN-based acoustic models using distillation and pruning.

Anil et al.
Researchers who proposed online distillation to enable extra parallelism when training large-scale data.

Han et al.
Researchers who combined quantization, hamming coding, and weight pruning for model compression on image classification tasks.

Yu et al.
Researchers who proposed a unified framework for low-rank and sparse decomposition of weight matrices.

Polino et al.
Researchers who advocated combining distillation and quantization, introducing quantified distillation and differentiable quantization.

Network Quantization
A neural network compression technique that reduces the bit-width and precision of weights or activations.

Hybrid Model Compression
An approach that integrates multiple distinct compression techniques, such as pruning, quantization, and distillation, for enhanced efficiency.

Variational Inference
A statistical and machine learning framework that approximates complex probability densities, applied to network quantization.

K-Means Clustering
An unsupervised clustering algorithm used in conventional quantization methods to group neural network weights.

Object Detection
A computer vision task focused on identifying and locating instances of semantic objects within digital images.

Online Distillation
A variant of knowledge distillation that trains multiple models simultaneously, enabling enhanced parallelism for large-scale data.

Image Classification
A core computer vision category involving the categorization of whole images into predefined classes.

Sparse Decomposition
A mathematical decomposition technique that breaks down matrices into sparse components to reduce computational complexity.

AutoML
Automated Machine Learning, a field focused on automating the process of applying machine learning, including search for optimal model compression pipelines.

Reinforcement Learning
A category of machine learning paradigms focused on training decision-making agents through interactions within simulated environments.<SEP>A machine learning paradigm explored in dialogue systems to optimize conversational policies and agent interactions.<SEP>A machine learning paradigm referenced as a baseline optimization technique alongside reward rescaling in coreference resolution tasks.<SEP>A machine learning paradigm where an agent learns decision-making strategies through reward feedback, applied in compression pipelines to search configurations.<SEP>A machine learning paradigm where an agent learns to make decisions by receiving rewards, applied in open-domain dialogue generation.<SEP>Reinforcement Learning is a machine learning paradigm used to directly optimize non-differentiable evaluation metrics, compared against differentiable relaxations.<SEP>Reinforcement learning is a machine learning paradigm utilizing action-value functions and critic networks to optimize policy decisions.<SEP>Reinforcement learning is an area of machine learning centered on trial-and-error strategy optimization, which is supported by the HoME platform.

Patient Knowledge Distillation
A specialized knowledge distillation methodology that extracts rich feature representations across intermediate hidden layers of teacher networks.

Singular Value Decomposition
A linear algebra factorization method that decomposes a parameter matrix into constituent singular vectors and values for low-rank compression.<SEP>A mathematical decomposition method, commonly known as SVD, used to perform low-rank matrix approximation for model parameter compression.

Data Augmentation
A machine learning technique used to expand training data and mitigate model bias in neural relation extraction.<SEP>A technique for expanding training samples, utilized in distillation pipelines such as TinyBERT.<SEP>A technique used during distillation by models like TinyBERT to artificially expand training data in order to mimic teacher behavior.<SEP>A technique used to increase the diversity of training data by creating modified copies of existing data, employed in two-stage distillation pipelines.

Hybrid Compression
A model compression technique that integrates weight pruning directly onto low-rank decomposed matrices produced by SVD.

Low-Rank Matrix Approximation
A mathematical approximation technique that models a high-dimensional matrix by decomposing it into lower-rank representations via truncated singular value decomposition.

BERT Encoder
A core structural component of the BERT model consisting of multiple transformer encoder layers subjected to hybrid compression in LadaBERT.

Embedding Layer
Embedding layer converts input word sequences into initial vector representations (H_0) prior to processing by attention layers.<SEP>The input representation layer of neural language models such as BERT, which is compressed using specified compression ratios.

Classification Layer
A downstream task layer in BERT architectures, typically structured as a Multilayer Perceptron with Softmax activation.

Teacher Model
A full-sized or high-capacity neural network model used to guide and supervise smaller networks during knowledge distillation.

Student Model
A compact or compressed neural network model trained to mimic the intermediate outputs and representations of a teacher model.

Multilayer Perceptron
A Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) is a category of feedforward artificial neural network employed in the RC downstream task layer to map sequence representations to relation probability distributions.<SEP>A feedforward artificial neural network architecture commonly employed with Softmax activation in classification layers.<SEP>A feedforward artificial neural network class used as part of the classifier architecture with a sigmoid activation function.<SEP>Multilayer Perceptron is a feedforward artificial neural network model used to predict event spans and event attributes from learned features.

Random Search
A hyper-parameter search method applied to determine optimal fine-grained compression ratios.<SEP>An optimization algorithm used to explore and identify optimal fine-grained compression ratios across model layers using validation data.

Embedding-Layer Distillation
A specific knowledge distillation constraint applied to align the embedding layer representations between student and teacher models.

Attention-Layer Distillation
A knowledge distillation technique that constrains the self-attention matrices of a student model to match those of a teacher model.

Hidden-Layer Distillation
A knowledge distillation constraint enforcing alignment across intermediate fully-connected sub-layers in Transformer models.

Prediction-Layer Distillation
The standard form of knowledge distillation using soft cross-entropy loss over output logits.

Hybrid Pruning
A model compression approach combining SVD-based matrix factorization and iterative weight pruning.<SEP>A model compression technique that performs weight pruning on SVD-decomposed matrices, combining low-rank factorization and sparsity.

Sentiment Classification
A machine learning task and methodology used to detect and predict sentiment from labeled and unlabeled social media texts across domains and languages.<SEP>A natural language understanding task category evaluating text sentiment, exemplified by the SST-2 benchmark.<SEP>Sentiment Classification is a machine learning and natural language processing task aimed at categorizing text units into discrete sentiment classes such as negative, neutral, or positive.<SEP>Sentiment Classification is a machine learning task aimed at categorizing text into sentiment classes such as positive, negative, and neutral.<SEP>Sentiment Classification is an automated text classification category focusing on identifying the emotional polarity or subjective tone of texts such as Twitter posts.<SEP>Sentiment classification is a broad natural language processing category focused on analyzing and predicting affective states or polarities expressed in text.<SEP>Sentiment classification is a natural language processing task category focused on classifying the sentiment polarity of texts.<SEP>Sentiment classification is a subcategory of text classification focused on determining subjective attitudes or opinions in texts, evaluated on benchmarks like SST, IMDB, and MDSD.<SEP>The natural language processing task of categorizing text into sentiment classes, specifically ordered categories such as negative, neutral, and positive.

Natural Language Inference
A classification task category determining inferential relationships between sentence pairs, such as MNLI and QNLI.

Pairwise Semantic Equivalence
A category of natural language tasks that assesses whether two sentences share identical meaning, such as QQP.

Transformer Architectures
A class of deep learning neural network architectures relying on self-attention mechanisms.

GLUE-Benchmark Evaluation Platform
An evaluation benchmark platform and service used by the NLP community to assess and rank language models across diverse understanding tasks.

BERT-Base
A 12-layer pre-trained transformer model serving as the teacher model for distillation and compression baselines.<SEP>The pre-trained base Transformer checkpoint with 12 layers, 12 heads, 768 hidden units, and 110M parameters used as the initial model for compression.

BERT-FT
A baseline approach that directly fine-tunes BERT via supervision task labels.

BERT-KD
A baseline compression approach implementing vanilla knowledge distillation on BERT.

BERT-SMALL
A baseline Transformer model with the same architecture as TinyBERT, pre-trained directly via the official BERT pipeline.<SEP>A small-scale BERT model pre-trained from scratch on a smaller architecture using the official BERT pipeline.

Distilled-BiLSTM
A baseline model that distills knowledge into a single-layer bidirectional LSTM achieving a 10.8x compression ratio.<SEP>A distilled bidirectional LSTM recurrent model used as a baseline for model compression on natural language processing tasks.

SST-2
A benchmark dataset used for evaluating sentiment classification in natural language understanding.<SEP>A binary sentiment classification benchmark dataset of movie reviews evaluated in the multi-cardinality multi-task scenario.<SEP>The Stanford Sentiment Treebank dataset used to evaluate sentiment classification performance in natural language processing.

MNLI
The Multi-Genre Natural Language Inference dataset, evaluated across matched and mismatched settings (MNLI-m and MNLI-mm).

QNLI
A public question natural language inference dataset evaluated within natural language understanding benchmarks.<SEP>The Question-answering Natural Language Inference benchmark dataset used for language understanding evaluation.

QQP
The Quora Question Pairs benchmark dataset used to evaluate semantic equivalence and sentence-pair classification.<SEP>The Quora Question Pairs dataset, used to evaluate models on pairwise semantic equivalence.

SVD-Based Matrix Factorization
A low-rank matrix approximation method based on Singular Value Decomposition used to factorize weight matrices.<SEP>A low-rank matrix decomposition technique used to reduce parameters in neural network weight matrices.

Mean Squared Error
A loss function adopted to compute distillation loss at the embedding, self-attention, and hidden representation layers.<SEP>A statistical metric used to measure agreement on polarity ratings by penalizing larger numerical discrepancies between annotators.

Soft Cross-Entropy Loss
A loss function applied in prediction-layer distillation between the predictive logits of teacher and student models.

BertAdam
An optimization algorithm configured with default settings to optimize LadaBERT models.

LadaBERT-1
A compressed variant of LadaBERT with a 2.5x parameter reduction ratio, evaluated against BERT-PKD.

LadaBERT-3
A compressed variant of LadaBERT with a 7.5x compression ratio, evaluated against TinyBERT and BERT-SMALL.

LadaBERT-4
A highly compressed variant of LadaBERT with high compression ratio, evaluated against Distilled-BiLSTM.

MNLI-m
A matched natural language inference benchmark dataset used to evaluate model accuracy and convergence speed.

MNLI-mm
A mismatched natural language inference benchmark dataset used for evaluating cross-domain model generalization.

Transformer
A category of neural network architecture implemented with multi-head attention and stacked layers in the seq2seq automation experiments.<SEP>A neural network architecture based entirely on self-attention mechanisms, used across various NLP tasks.<SEP>A neural network architecture based on self-attention mechanisms, serving as the foundational building block for language models like BERT.<SEP>A neural network architecture based solely on attention mechanisms that achieves strong performance across numerous natural language processing tasks.<SEP>A neural network architecture category based on self-attention mechanisms, used as a foundation for context-aware machine translation models.<SEP>A neural network architecture using self-attention mechanisms, exhibiting faster inference than recurrent models of similar size.<SEP>A neural network model architecture category utilizing self-attention mechanisms that outperformed ConvS2S across evaluated translation tasks.<SEP>A self-attention-based neural network architecture category evaluated for its superior performance and inference stability in speech act identification.<SEP>A state-of-the-art neural network architecture relying on self-attention mechanisms, trained and evaluated for translating English into South African languages.<SEP>The Transformer is a neural network architecture based on self-attention mechanisms, evaluated in context-aware translation experiments for its performance on intra-segmental and source-context pronoun translation.<SEP>Transformer is a neural machine translation architecture implemented using Tensor2Tensor that outperformed ConvS2S across all tested languages.<SEP>Transformer is a neural network architecture based on self-attention mechanisms, used in machine translation and language representations like BERT.

BiLSTM
A bidirectional long short-term memory recurrent neural network architecture implemented for sentence segmentation in obituaries.<SEP>A bidirectional recurrent neural network architecture comprising forward and backward LSTM components, used to learn sentence representations of event intents.<SEP>A bidirectional recurrent neural network architecture whose inference speed is typically slower than transformer-based architectures.<SEP>Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network, a type of recurrent neural network architecture used to determine the importance of segments in text inputs.

SVD Pruning
A model reduction technique using Singular Value Decomposition matrix factorization to compress neural network weights.

Computer Vision
A field of artificial intelligence where complementary benefits of low-rank factorization and sparsity were previously demonstrated.<SEP>A subfield of artificial intelligence used to analyze meal images, identify ingredients, estimate volume, and assess nutritional content.<SEP>Computer Vision is a domain of artificial intelligence focused on extracting meaningful information from digital images and visual inputs.<SEP>Computer Vision is a domain of artificial intelligence that extracts insights, patterns, and features from digital images.<SEP>Computer Vision is a domain of artificial intelligence where adversarial attacks were historically easier due to continuous input spaces compared to NLP.<SEP>Computer vision is a field of artificial intelligence focused on enabling computers to derive meaningful information from digital images, videos, and visual inputs.

European Central Bank
The European Central Bank is an international financial institution cited as an antecedent example in sentence translation tasks.

Context-Aware Translation
Context-aware translation is a paradigm in machine translation that leverages inter-sentential context beyond single-sentence boundaries to improve translation coherence and accuracy.

Pronoun Translation
A linguistic phenomenon and evaluation focus in machine translation that often requires inter-sentential context to resolve correctly.<SEP>A specialized subfield and challenge within machine translation focusing on correctly resolving and translating anaphora across languages.<SEP>Pronoun translation is a machine translation challenge involving mapping pronouns such as English 'it' into gender-marked pronouns like German 'er', 'sie', or 'es'.<SEP>Pronoun translation is a specialized task and challenge in machine translation that frequently requires cross-sentence context to resolve gender, number, and antecedent ambiguities.<SEP>Pronoun translation is a specific linguistic challenge and evaluation task in machine translation concerning the correct translation of pronouns such as English 'it' into target language gendered forms like German 'er', 'sie', and 'es'.

MNLI-m Dataset
MNLI-m is a natural language inference benchmark dataset used to evaluate the accuracy and learning performance of language models like LadaBERT.

QQP Dataset
QQP (Quora Question Pairs) is a benchmark dataset used to evaluate the learning curve and performance of compressed language models.

BLEU
A category of standard evaluation metric for translation and text generation tasks, noted for potentially penalizing expressive diversity.<SEP>A standard automated evaluation metric used to calculate the linguistic quality and overlap of machine translation outputs against reference translations.<SEP>A standard evaluation metric that calculates n-gram precision to evaluate machine translation quality against reference translations.<SEP>A standardized automatic evaluation metric used in machine translation to assess the quality of translated text against reference translations.<SEP>An automated evaluation metric category used in natural language processing to assess the quality of machine translations.<SEP>An automated metric used to evaluate machine translation quality across test sets like newstest2017 and newstest2018.<SEP>BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) is an automatic evaluation metric that measures n-gram precision overlap between generated text segments and gold-standard references.<SEP>BLEU is a quantitative evaluation metric used to benchmark and compare the translation accuracy of the machine translation models.<SEP>BLEU is a standard automated evaluation metric used in machine translation to assess document- and sentence-level translation quality against reference translations.<SEP>BLEU is a standard automated evaluation metric used in machine translation to assess overall translation quality, showing moderate improvements for context-aware models.<SEP>BLEU is a standard evaluation metric in natural language processing used to measure the quality of machine-translated text against reference translations.<SEP>BLEU is a standard evaluation metric used in natural language processing and machine translation to assess text generation quality.<SEP>BLEU is a standard evaluation metric used to score machine translation accuracy.<SEP>BLEU is an evaluation metric commonly used to assess the quality of machine translation outputs.<SEP>Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU), an evaluation metric used to benchmark and measure translation quality in machine translation experiments.<SEP>Bilingual Evaluation Understudy, an automated evaluation metric used to assess the generation quality of the imaginator models.

RIBES
RIBES is an automated evaluation metric for machine translation designed to measure translation quality, particularly rank correlation of words.

Sequence-to-Sequence Models
A baseline class of neural network architectures commonly used for conversational agents and dialogue modeling.<SEP>An encoder-decoder neural network framework used to process variable-length input sequences into target sequences, widely used in translation, dialogue, and simplification.<SEP>Neural network architectures designed to map input sequences to output sequences, utilized in direct speech translation and speech recognition.<SEP>Sequence-to-sequence models are a class of neural network architectures commonly applied to tasks such as machine translation, summarization, and question answering.<SEP>Sequence-to-sequence models are an encoder-decoder neural network framework used to map input sequences to output sequences for generation tasks.<SEP>Sequence-to-sequence models are deep learning architectures designed to map an input sequence to an output sequence, commonly used in neural machine translation.

Parameter Tying
Parameter tying is a technique in neural architecture design where weights are shared across components, such as multi-encoder networks in context-aware translation.

DiscoMT
DiscoMT is an academic workshop series focusing on discourse in machine translation that hosts shared tasks such as pronoun prediction.

WMT
WMT is a premier machine translation conference and shared task competition that has co-hosted cross-lingual pronoun prediction tasks.

Cross-Lingual Pronoun Prediction Task
A shared evaluation task held at DiscoMT and WMT challenging participants to predict missing pronouns in target language translations.

Context-Aware NMT
A category of neural machine translation systems and architectures designed to incorporate information beyond single-sentence boundaries.

Contrastive Evaluation
An evaluation methodology assessing model accuracy based on whether the model scores correct reference translations higher than contrastive erroneous translations.<SEP>An evaluation methodology using targeted contrastive pairs to assess how accurately translation models handle specific linguistic phenomena like pronoun disambiguation.<SEP>Contrastive evaluation is an evaluation methodology in machine translation that tests a model's ability to discriminate between correct reference translations and contrastive incorrect variants by comparing model scores.

AutoPRF
An automated reference-based evaluation metric that scores pronoun translation using word alignment between source, MT output, and reference translations.

APT
An automated reference-based pronoun translation evaluation metric based on word alignment and pronoun identification.

OpenSubtitles Corpus
A large-scale multi-language subtitle dataset used to automatically extract contrastive examples for pronoun translation evaluation.

Encoder-Decoder Model
A standard sequence-to-sequence neural network architecture extended with additional context encoders and attention mechanisms for discourse modeling.<SEP>Encoder-Decoder Model is a neural network architecture category that underpins sequence generation frameworks such as CopyRNN.

Attention Mechanism
A deep learning mechanism enabling models to dynamically focus on different parts of an input sequence, serving as the sole foundation of the Transformer architecture.<SEP>A deep learning technique that allows models to focus on specific parts of input sequences, foundational to modern dialogue models and Transformers.<SEP>A neural network mechanism in the G-SAT classifier that weights the hidden states of input tokens to generate a slot-specific context vector.<SEP>A neural network mechanism modified in context-aware architectures to allow models to attend to preceding context sentences.<SEP>A neural network mechanism within the encoder-decoder architecture that allows the decoder to access encoder states during translation.<SEP>An algorithmic component that allows the decoder in an NMT model to selectively focus on specific source representations from the encoder.<SEP>An attention mechanism is a neural network technique that dynamically assigns weights to relevant tokens or facts during inference and reasoning.<SEP>An iterative neural scoring mechanism that computes attention weights over document tokens across multiple inference steps to guide answer prediction.<SEP>Attention Mechanism is a deep learning technique that dynamically weights representations of different input segments to allow models to focus on relevant context and targets.<SEP>Attention Mechanism is a neural network component that dynamically weights and focuses on relevant features and token relationships within distributed representations.

Hierarchical Architecture
A multi-level neural network structure that uses cascaded RNNs to encode words into sentence vectors and combine them into document-level summaries.

Inter-Sentential Anaphora
A linguistic discourse phenomenon where a pronoun refers to an antecedent located in a preceding sentence, requiring cross-sentence context to resolve.<SEP>Inter-sentential anaphora is a discourse-level linguistic phenomenon where a pronoun refers to an antecedent noun located across sentence boundaries in previous sentences.

Intra-Sentential Anaphora
A linguistic phenomenon where a pronoun and its antecedent exist within the same sentence.

Concatenation Technique
A context-aware translation method that prepends preceding sentences directly to the current sentence without modifying model architecture.

German
A West Germanic language used in vector interpolation and cross-entropy evaluation alongside English.<SEP>A language category referenced in the context of the WMT 2014 translation benchmark for subword token optimization.<SEP>A major language possessing an aspect-annotated sentiment corpus, mentioned as an example of an adequately resourced language.<SEP>A parent language evaluated in transfer experiments for the Spanish-English child language pair, yielding lower Bleu scores than French.<SEP>German is a European language appearing as a false-positive language prediction within digital data sets for Russia.<SEP>German is a West Germanic language evaluated in cross-entropy interpolation experiments alongside English.<SEP>German is a language present in existing BLI evaluation dictionaries paired with English.<SEP>German is a natural language referenced as possessing rich morphological structures compared to English.<SEP>German is a natural language used in a German–English parent model to compare transfer performance against a French–English parent model.<SEP>One of the languages evaluated in the multilingual WOZ2.0 benchmark to measure the accuracy and prediction latency of dialogue state trackers.<SEP>One of the professional translation target languages evaluated in the multilingual WOZ2.0 dataset experiments.<SEP>The target language chosen for evaluating difficult pronoun translation cases extracted from corpora.<SEP>The target language into which the WOZ2.0 dialogue benchmark was translated by professional translators for multilingual evaluation.

French
A Romance language analyzed in the study, noted for paradigm syncretism and large verbal paradigms.<SEP>A Romance language included in the bilingual dictionaries and extensively compared against MUSE baselines.<SEP>A high-resource language paired with English to train the parent neural machine translation model.<SEP>A language category referenced in the context of the WMT 2014 subword token count benchmarks.<SEP>A parent language evaluated in transfer experiments, proving to be more effective than German for Spanish due to language similarity.<SEP>French is a Romance language evaluated in the study as part of the French–Spanish language pair.<SEP>French is a high-resource language used to train parent bilingual models for transfer learning into child models.<SEP>French is a major European language identified as an over-predicted false-positive language within digital datasets in Russia.<SEP>The high-resource natural language utilized as the source language for training the parent NMT model in the study.<SEP>The target language evaluated in the first edition of the cross-lingual pronoun prediction task.

OpenSubtitles
An online subtitle repository and project providing movie dialogue data used for question-answering sentence pairs to train neural models.<SEP>OpenSubtitles is an online platform for movie and television subtitles used as a data source mimicking informal speech for language identification training.<SEP>OpenSubtitles is an online subtitle platform and database from which a 12,000-instance contrastive test suite for pronoun translation was extracted.<SEP>OpenSubtitles is an online subtitle repository and project whose text corpus is used to extract English-German translation pairs.<SEP>OpenSubtitles is an organization and resource provider whose subtitle corpus is used to extract dialogue question-answer pairs for natural language generation.

Coreference Resolution
A natural language processing task aimed at identifying when different mentions or expressions in a text refer to the same real-world entity.<SEP>A natural language processing task whose absence in the model causes classification errors in obituary sentences.<SEP>Coreference Resolution is a natural language processing task and clustering problem that identifies all mentions in a document referring to the same real-world entity.<SEP>Coreference Resolution is a natural language processing task referenced as an area where gender bias evaluation and datasets have previously been developed.<SEP>Coreference Resolution is a natural language processing task that involves determining whether different mentions or expressions in a text refer to the same entity.<SEP>Coreference resolution is a natural language processing task aimed at identifying when different expressions in a text refer to the same entity.<SEP>Coreference resolution is a natural language processing task that links pronouns to their corresponding antecedents within and across sentences.<SEP>Coreference resolution is an NLP task and category focused on identifying mentions that refer to the same real-world entities in text.

Moses Tokenizer
The Moses tokenizer is a natural language processing tool used to tokenize text prior to alignment and parsing.

Fast_align
Fast_align is an unsupervised word alignment tool used to generate symmetric word-level alignments between parallel texts.<SEP>Fast_align is an unsupervised word alignment tool used to generate token and pronoun alignments in the machine translation training dataset.

CoreNLP
CoreNLP is a natural language processing toolkit used to parse English sentences and perform neural coreference resolution.

ParZu
ParZu is a dependency parsing tool used for syntactic analysis of German text.

CorZu
CorZu is a coreference resolution system designed for German text.

Parsing
A computational linguistic task involving analyzing the syntactic structure of sentences according to a formal grammar.<SEP>Parsing is a natural language processing task involving syntactic structural analysis, addressed by Ballesteros et al. using a character-level model.<SEP>Parsing is the computational syntactic analysis of sentence structures, providing part-of-speech and dependency information.

Contrastive Translation
A contrastive translation is an artificially modified translation variant where a correct pronoun is replaced by an incorrect one to test system discrimination.

Nominal Antecedent
A nominal antecedent is a noun or noun phrase in a coreference chain that provides the gender and referential context for a pronoun.

Grammatical Gender Disambiguation
Grammatical gender disambiguation is the process of selecting the correct gendered pronoun in the target language based on the antecedent's gender.

data.entity_name: WMT 2017 English-to-German News Translation Shared Task
data.content:
WMT 2017 English-to-German News Translation Shared Task
The WMT 2017 English-to-German news translation shared task is a competitive benchmark event providing training data of approximately 5.8 million sentence pairs for evaluating machine translation models.

Recurrent Models
A class of neural machine translation architectures based on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with attention, tested with various context-aware and concatenation configurations.

Transformer Models
A class of neural machine translation architectures that eschew recurrence in favor of stacked self-attention and fully connected feedforward layers.

Context-Aware Models
Context-aware models are specialized neural machine translation architectures that incorporate inter-sentential context to improve coreference resolution and pronoun accuracy.<SEP>Neural machine translation architectures designed to incorporate preceding source or target sentence context to better resolve discourse phenomena.

Sentence-Level NMT
Standard baseline neural machine translation systems that translate sentences in isolation without access to surrounding cross-sentence context.

Nematus
A neural machine translation toolkit used to implement and train bidirectional recurrent neural network baselines and context-aware recurrent models.

SacreBLEU
A standard evaluation tool used to compute BLEU scores to measure overall translation quality in machine translation experiments.

Adam
An optimization algorithm used to train recurrent neural network models with an initial learning rate of 0.0001.

Byte Pair Encoding
A data compression algorithm adapted to learn subword translation units based on statistical properties and frequent character sequences in text.<SEP>A data-driven subword segmentation algorithm that iteratively merges the most frequent character bigrams.<SEP>A subword segmentation algorithm and representation unit evaluated for machine translation efficiency against words, morphemes, and syllables.<SEP>A subword segmentation algorithm applied to source and target texts to handle open vocabulary in both RNN and Transformer models.<SEP>A subword segmentation method and translation unit representation evaluated for machine translation between related languages.<SEP>A subword tokenization algorithm (BPE) analyzed in relation to machine translation performance and BLEU scores.<SEP>A subword tokenization technique (BPE) analyzed through an ablation study to find optimal token vocabularies across different language dataset sizes.<SEP>Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) is a data compression and subword segmentation technique used to address vocabulary limitations in neural language models.<SEP>Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) is a substitution dictionary-based subword segmentation algorithm widely used as a standard preprocessing method in neural machine translation.<SEP>Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) is a subword tokenization and representation technique that provides writing system independence and improves translation accuracy across various languages.

S-Hier-To-2
A context-aware recurrent model that uses an additional encoder for source context and concatenates target context, achieving top performance in pronoun translation.

S-Hier
A multi-encoder recurrent architecture with hierarchical attention that incorporates the previous source sentence as context.

S-T-Hier
A multi-encoder recurrent model with hierarchical attention that reads both the previous source sentence and previous target sentence.

Concat22
A contextual translation approach that concatenates each sentence with one preceding sentence on both the source and target sides.

Concat21
A contextual translation architecture where the preceding sentence is concatenated to the current sentence only on the source side.

Newstest2017
A standard benchmark evaluation test set from the WMT 2017 news translation shared task used to measure BLEU scores.

Newstest2018
A standard benchmark evaluation test set from WMT 2018 used to measure BLEU scores.

Weight Tying
A parameter-sharing method where embedding matrices between encoders reading the same side of text share parameters.

Swiss National Science Foundation
The Swiss National Science Foundation (SNF) is a research funding agency that provided financial support for the CoNTra research project under grant number 105212_169888.

WMT 2017
The 2017 Conference on Machine Translation (WMT 2017) news translation task, which provided training data and test sets for machine translation models.<SEP>The WMT 2017 news translation task is a machine translation benchmark and shared task whose dataset was used to train the translation systems.

CoNTra
CoNTra is a funded scientific research project focused on contrastive evaluation and machine translation, supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation.

Multi-Encoder Architecture
Multi-encoder architecture is a neural model design strategy in context-aware translation that utilizes separate encoders for context and source sentences, outperforming simple concatenation approaches.

Parameter Sharing
A joint learning mechanism that shares a feature extraction layer between named entity recognition and relation classification models.<SEP>Parameter sharing is a machine learning optimization technique where weights are tied between contextual and primary encoders or decoders, significantly boosting model accuracy.

Coreference Chain
A coreference chain is a sequence of referring expressions in discourse that refer to the same nominal entity across multiple sentences, providing contextual signals for translation models.

Contrastive Test Suite
The contrastive test suite is a specialized machine translation benchmark comprising 12,000 test cases designed to evaluate whether neural models can correctly translate pronouns.

German Language
The German language is the target language in the translation experiments, presenting morphological gender distinctions in pronouns such as 'er', 'sie', and 'es'.

English Language
A natural language used to present demonstrative example sentences and annotation schemes in the text.<SEP>A widely researched Germanic language used as a baseline and comparison point for directive analysis.<SEP>The English language is the source language in the experiments, characterized by gender-neutral third-person pronouns such as 'it'.

FreeFollowers
An online blackmarket service that allows users to gain inorganic appraisals and artificial engagement on social media platforms.

Like4Like
A blackmarket service platform that facilitates artificial engagement and appraisals on social media.<SEP>Like4Like is an underground credit-based freemium blackmarket website crawled to collect data on collusive retweeting behavior.

YouLikeHits
An online service that enables users to generate inorganic appraisals and engagement metrics for social media content.<SEP>YouLikeHits is an underground credit-based freemium blackmarket website used to gain retweets and other social media appraisals.

JustRetweet
A blackmarket service allowing users to submit tweets to obtain artificial retweets and endorsements.

Blackmarket Tweets
A category of tweets submitted to blackmarket engagement services to gain artificially inflated retweets, likes, and reach.

Social Spam
A category of fraudulent or unsolicited content and activity on social media platforms.

NTra
A funding agency or project responsible for awarding grant number 105212_169888.

Bots
Automated accounts on social networks studied in research focused on detecting fraudulent and automated behaviors.

Fake Followers
Inauthentic or fabricated accounts used to artificially inflate user follower counts on social networks.

Collusive Retweeters
Coordinated groups of accounts that collaborate fraudulently to artificially amplify and retweet content.

Spammers
Entities or users who generate unsolicited, repetitive, or deceptive social media content.

Blackmarket Users
Social media users who utilize blackmarket engagement services to gain inorganic appraisals and artificial reach for their posts.

Genuine Tweets
Legitimate, authentic tweets that are posted organically without relying on blackmarket amplification services.

Blackmarket Services
Blackmarket services are underground platforms and mechanisms where users collusively purchase or trade social media appraisals such as retweets.<SEP>Online platforms that offer inorganic social media engagement such as likes, retweets, and followers.

Content-Level Appraisals
Metrics and signals of support on Twitter, specifically including Likes, Retweets, and Quotes.

Yardi
Yardi is a researcher who studied the network structures of spammers and non-spammers and tracked endogenous Twitter content.

Chen
Chen is a researcher who conducted comprehensive evaluations of machine learning algorithms for timely spam detection.

Serrano
Serrano is a researcher who conducted an extensive survey on fake tweet detection.

Motoyama
Motoyama is a researcher who provided detailed analyses of underground forums and social network structures.

Dutta
Dutta is a researcher who investigated customers involved in purchasing fake retweets and analyzed models of blackmarket services.

Chetan
Chetan is a researcher who proposed CoReRank and CoReRank+ to detect collusive users involved in retweeting activities.

Misra
Misra is a researcher who introduced Cross-Stitch units for multitask learning representations.

Zhang
A researcher investigating character-level models for natural language processing tasks.<SEP>A researcher who, with Lapata, framed the encoder-decoder model as an agent using deep reinforcement learning for sentence simplification.<SEP>Zhang is a researcher who classified multitask learning models into five distinct types.<SEP>Zhang is a researcher who, along with colleagues, previously proposed a decoding approach for text simplification that this work contrasts with by implementing greedy and beam-search strategies.<SEP>Zhang is a researcher who, along with colleagues, trained a convolutional neural network to perform text classification directly from characters without using words.

Freemium Services
Freemium services are a category of blackmarket services that provide both paid and unpaid options to earn appraisals.

Premium Services
Premium services are a category of blackmarket services accessible only via monetary payment from customers.

Credit-Based Services
Credit-based services are a sub-category of freemium blackmarket services where users earn credits by appraising others' content to gain appraisals for their own.

Social-Share Services
Social-share services are a sub-category of freemium blackmarket services that require customers to share content on social media.

Auto-Time Retweet Services
Auto-Time retweet services are a sub-category of freemium blackmarket services that use Twitter access tokens to automatically retweet content.

Promotional
A topical category of tweets accounting for 23.29% of the false negatives in the tweet classification model.<SEP>A tweet category identifying tweets that attempt to promote a website, product, or service.<SEP>Promotional is an annotation category of tweets that attempt to market a website, product, or account.

Fake Tweets
Fake tweets represent a category of malicious social media posts designed to spread misinformation, often linked to major events.

Spam
A tweet classification category representing unwanted, deceptive, or automated messages commonly targeted in detection studies.<SEP>A tweet content category examined during classification robustness evaluations.<SEP>Spam refers to malicious, unsolicited, or automated tweets and content detected on social platforms.

IRB
Institutional Review Board, an administrative body that oversees and approves research involving human subjects to ensure ethical standards.<SEP>The Institutional Review Board (IRB) is an administrative body that reviewed and granted ethical approval for the researchers to create dummy accounts on blackmarket platforms.

Multitask Learning
A machine learning paradigm adopted to jointly train the primary binary classification task and secondary engagement regression task.<SEP>Multitask learning is a machine learning paradigm used to simultaneously optimize two or more related tasks through shared representations.

Malicious Activities
Malicious activities encompass harmful behaviors in social networks, specifically including spam, fake content, and blackmarket services.

Major Events
Major events are significant real-world occurrences during which accounts spreading fake tweets and misinformation are frequently created.

Entertainment
A topical category of tweets accounting for 21.92% of the false negatives in the evaluation.<SEP>Entertainment is a topical category of blackmarket tweets comprising 15.89% of the annotated test dataset.

News
A tweet content category for which the proposed model demonstrates robust blackmarket classification performance.<SEP>News is a content category of blackmarket tweets accounting for 7.86% of the annotated test dataset.

Politics
A general news categorization field found in the HTML pages of news articles.<SEP>A societal domain characterized by governance and public affairs, noted for being adversely impacted and polarized by the spread of fake news.<SEP>A topical category of tweets against which the classification model demonstrates robust detection performance.<SEP>Politics is a thematic category of blackmarket tweets accounting for 4.82% of the annotated test dataset.<SEP>Politics is a thematic topic and domain category often represented in fake news research and datasets.

Others
A residual classification category of tweets accounting for 28.77% of false negatives, noted as particularly difficult to distinguish from genuine tweets.<SEP>A tweet category largely encompassing personal tweets without explicit call to action, though potentially functioning as self-promotion.<SEP>Others is a residual annotation category representing 14.11% of blackmarket tweets, primarily consisting of personal and self-promotional posts.

Dhingra Et Al.
Dhingra et al. are researchers who provided the pre-trained Tweet2Vec model trained on a dataset of 2 million tweets.

Wu Et Al.
Wu et al. are researchers who proposed a Twitter spam detection method using Word2Vec and Doc2Vec with an MLP classifier.

Rajdev Et Al.
Rajdev et al. are researchers who proposed flat and hierarchical classification approaches to classify spam, fake, and legitimate tweets.

Blackmarket
A classification category representing tweets associated with blackmarket manipulation services or illicit promotion.<SEP>A target class in the binary classification task representing tweets submitted to blackmarket services for inorganic engagement.

Genuine
A classification category representing legitimate or normal non-manipulated tweets.<SEP>A target class representing legitimate, authentic tweets in the binary classification problem.

Not-Spam
A classification category representing non-spam or authentic social media content used in baseline spam detection frameworks.

Fake
A category used in tweet classification setups to identify fraudulent or counterfeit social media posts.

Legitimate
A category denoting genuine and authentic social media posts within hierarchical and flat classification frameworks.

Binary Classification
The machine learning task category utilized as the primary objective to differentiate tweets between blackmarket and genuine classes.

Regression
A category of predictive modeling used as the secondary task to forecast numerical counts of likes and retweets after five days.

Tweet Content Features

BLSTM

Artificial Intelligence

A deep learning model architecture that uses bilinear tensors to explicitly model relational interactions among event components.<SEP>A neural network architecture that combines arguments multiplicatively to generate dense compositional event representations.<SEP>Neural Tensor Network is a family of baseline models that use tensors to learn interactions between predicates and their arguments.<SEP>Neural tensor network is a deep learning architecture used to perform semantic composition and capture interactions between event arguments.

A baseline class of compositional models, including Comp. NN and EM Comp., compared against tensor-based models.<SEP>Parameterized additive models are vector space modeling methods that pass concatenated or summed word embeddings through parameterized functions.

Character-Level Models
A category of neural network architectures that process text at the level of individual orthographic characters rather than whole words.<SEP>Character-level models are translation representations that use character mappings, effective primarily for closely related languages.<SEP>Translation units and modeling approaches operating at the level of individual characters, effective primarily for highly similar language pairs.

Char2Vec

Recurrent Architecture

Classical Word Embedding Models
Classical word embedding models represent entire words as distinct vectors and capture semantic relations and human word similarity judgments.

Compositional Word Semantics

Bahdanau

Morphology

Word2Vec
