A domain of artificial intelligence and computational linguistics dedicated to the analysis and processing of clinical records and healthcare data.<SEP>A subfield of artificial intelligence and computer science focused on developing computational methods for linguistic analysis and knowledge extraction from free-text clinical records.

Rule-based Method
A class of natural language processing techniques that relies on predefined linguistic rules and lightweight token replacement.

AttnCopy Seq2seq
An attention-based sequence-to-sequence neural model with copying mechanisms serving as a baseline architecture for text generation.

Qualitative Study
An analytical examination conducted to inspect and compare generated sentence outputs across different model variants and test cases.

Clinical Practice
The medical and healthcare field that stands to be transformed through the large-scale computational processing of clinical records.

Data Access Policies
Regulatory, ethical, and institutional governance frameworks that restrict researcher access to sensitive medical data.

Data Privacy
An ethical and regulatory principle focused on safeguarding sensitive patient health information in clinical records.

Biomedical Natural Language Processing
A domain of natural language processing focused on analyzing biomedical research literature, which faces fewer data privacy restrictions than clinical NLP.

HIPAA Privacy Rule
A United States regulatory framework that legally protects confidential patient medical information and clinician encounter records.<SEP>A health data privacy regulation that permits disclosure of health records of deceased individuals under specific conditions without IRB approval.<SEP>A legal framework in the United States that protects the confidentiality of individuals' medical and health data.

General Data Protection Regulation
A European Union legal framework governing the principles and scientific processing of personal and health data.<SEP>European Union regulation governing data protection, privacy principles like data minimization, and the scientific use of sensitive health data.

MIMIC-III
A widely used clinical dataset covering intensive care admissions from a single hospital in the United States, subject to sampling bias.

I2b2 Shared Tasks
Collaborative evaluation events and competitive benchmarks providing annotated clinical datasets for NLP research.

ShARe/CLEF
Shared clinical challenge tasks that produce annotated datasets for research community evaluation.

MiPACQ
A clinical text corpus used in published research that was subsequently restricted, trimmed down, or made unavailable due to legal or access issues.

Blulab
A clinical dataset previously utilized in published research and reproduction efforts that faced subsequent access restrictions.

EMC Dutch Clinical Corpus
A Dutch-language clinical dataset that was utilized in empirical research but later faced distribution limitations or reduced availability.

2010 i2b2/VA Dataset
A clinical benchmark dataset consisting of 841 annotated patient records across three specialty areas used for training named entity recognition models.

Data Science
The broader field of analyzing data and developing computational models, sharing ethical and bias challenges with clinical NLP.

Sampling Bias
A corpus-level bias that arises when the collected dataset does not adequately represent the target population.<SEP>A systemic error where a specific dataset or sample fails to represent the broader population, leading to skewed research conclusions and model invalidity.

EU
The European Union, where the processing and scientific usage of health data are regulated under the General Data Protection Regulation.

Clinical NLP
A specialized subfield of natural language processing focusing on extracting information, concepts, and knowledge from clinical and health-related documents.<SEP>A subfield of natural language processing focusing on the analysis of clinical records and medical text data.<SEP>The domain of applying natural language processing techniques to clinical notes, medical records, and healthcare data.

Sanitization
Data privacy techniques, including anonymization and de-identification, used to remove or alter sensitive identifiers from datasets.

Informed Consent
The legal and ethical process of obtaining explicit authorization from data subjects to collect, use, and process their health data.

Personal Genome Project
An initiative that implements open consent by allowing individuals to make their personal data publicly available for research.

Polonetsky
A researcher cited for work providing overviews on sanitization procedures such as anonymization, pseudonymization, and de-identification.

Dwork
A researcher cited for studies on secure data access, storage, and the trade-off between privacy loss and data utility.

Pottenger
A researcher cited alongside Dwork concerning secure access and storage of sensitive clinical data.

Malin
A researcher cited for contributions to research on secure access and confidentiality of sensitive health data.

Rindfleisch
A researcher cited for literature regarding secure data access, storage, and confidentiality in clinical settings.

Data Minimization
A core data protection principle under GDPR mandating that personal data collection and processing be limited to what is strictly necessary and retained only as long as required, encompassing techniques like sanitization.

Special Categories Of Personal Data
A GDPR regulatory classification for sensitive data, including health data, requiring explicit subject consent or public disclosure by the subject before scientific or technological processing.

Anonymization
A sanitization technique that removes or modifies personal identifying details to prevent identification of individuals in a dataset.

Pseudonymization
A data protection technique that replaces personal identifiers with pseudonyms to reduce linkability while preserving analytical utility.

De-Identification
A process of removing or obscuring personal identifiers from clinical and health datasets to preserve subject confidentiality.

Deductive Disclosure
A re-identification phenomenon where sanitized or de-identified data is re-linked to an individual using external information or inference.

Opt-In Policy
A consent framework where consent is presumed or granted by default, often coupled with a right to withdraw (opt-out), potentially structured in a broad or tiered manner.

Open Consent
A data-sharing paradigm where participants agree to have their sensitive or genomic data made publicly available without guarantees of total anonymity.

Secure Access
Data governance and computational mechanisms designed to provide researchers controlled, secure entry to sensitive clinical data while balancing utility and privacy.

Medical Institutions
Healthcare and clinical organizations that generate, store, and govern patient health records and clinical data.

VetCompass
A repository storing tens of millions of clinical documents from various veterinary clinics in the UK and Australia for research purposes.

Australia
A country whose workers were accepted to provide annotations for the dataset via AMT.<SEP>A nation where veterinary clinics contribute clinical documentation to the centralized VetCompass repository.<SEP>Australia is a country noted for being over-represented in Twitter language data compared to its population size.<SEP>Australia is a country showing over-predicted languages in Twitter data compared to census records.<SEP>Australia is one of the countries from which crowd workers were accepted to carry out annotation tasks.

Clinical NLP 2016 Workshop
An academic workshop where early natural language processing work utilizing veterinary records from VetCompass was presented.

Kramer et al.
Researchers who authored an influential study on emotional contagion via Facebook posts, which faced scrutiny over consent.

Rebholz-Schuhmann et al.
Researchers known for work on ensembling trained models from disparate sources and creating silver standard corpora.

Lipton et al.
Researchers who explored sequential modeling applied to diagnosis classification and imputing missing values in clinical texts.

Reporting Bias
A form of bias found in clinical texts stemming from subjective clinician documentation, selective recall by patients, or suppression of sensitive information.<SEP>A form of bias in clinical documentation where information is selectively omitted, altered, or suppressed due to social stigma, legal fears, or clinician prejudices.

Algorithm Transparency
An ethical and legal principle requiring insight into how automated models make decisions and how training data biases influence outcomes.

Government
Public governing bodies that can facilitate and guarantee researchers' access to relevant health data.

Healthcare Organizations
Medical and clinical institutions that maintain patient records and provide the computational infrastructure for health data research.

Statistical NLP
A computational methodology within natural language processing that relies on statistical methods, requiring significant CPU and GPU power.

Interoperability
The ability to share and combine health data across different medical institutions to improve statistical power and reduce bias in research.

Epidemiology
The study of health and disease distribution in populations, requiring cross-organizational interoperability to attain statistical power.

Surrogate Data
Alternative health-related textual data, such as patient-generated content and social media posts, used to complement or substitute clinical discourse.

Derived Data
Secondary forms of data such as text fragments, statistics, and trained models that reduce privacy risks because they prevent reconstruction of original patient text.

Data Quality
The degree to which clinical notes accurately, completely, and explicitly reflect patient health conditions and treatment contexts.

Health Disparities
Systemic variations in healthcare access and treatment, reflected in clinical text through prejudices, ethnic communication gaps, and societal norms.<SEP>Unequal health outcomes and documentation gaps in clinical notes driven by practitioner prejudices or communication barriers across ethnic groups.

Brady
A researcher who, along with colleagues, found documentation disparities regarding obesity between sexes in weight clinics due to societal norms.

Madhumita
An individual acknowledged by the authors of the clinical NLP paper for providing helpful comments.

data.entity_name: Agency for Innovation by Science and Technology
data.content:
Agency for Innovation by Science and Technology
A government agency (IWT) that funded the research through the Accumulate IWT SBO project.

Duluth
A research team and system that participated in SemEval-2017 Task 6 using N-gram language models for humor detection.

Comedy Central
A television network that aired the show @midnight with Chris Hardwick, which served as the source material for the humor detection task.

Chris Hardwick
The host of the Comedy Central television show @midnight, who provides hashtags that inspire humorous responses.

SemEval-2017 Task 6
An international NLP evaluation workshop task titled '#HashtagWars: Learning a Sense of Humor', focusing on computational humor detection.

Computational Humor
An interdisciplinary research field combining linguistics, psychology, philosophy, and computer science to model, generate, or detect humor.

Observational Bias
A bias occurring when explanatory factors are missing from clinical reports because they fall outside the experimental or clinical observation setting.

Dual Use
The concept and ethical issue where technologies or health information can be applied in both beneficial and harmful ways.

Accumulate IWT SBO Project
A research project framework under which part of the clinical NLP research was carried out, sponsored by the IWT.

@midnight
A Comedy Central television show hosted by Chris Hardwick that inspired audience tweets used as evaluation data for computational humor tasks.

Subtask A
A specific sub-competition within SemEval-2017 Task 6 in which the Duluth system participated.<SEP>A subtask within a natural language processing shared evaluation focused on pair-wise comparison of tweets to determine which is funnier.<SEP>Subtask A is a tweet humor comparison challenge where a system compares pairs of tweets to determine the funnier one.

Streetlight Effect
An observational bias referring to the search for explanatory factors only where it is easy to look, leading to missed social and behavioral determinants in clinical texts.

Privacy in Health
The domain of data protection and patient confidentiality governing access to sensitive clinical notes and health records.

Right to Science
The ethical and legal principle emphasizing the right of individuals and society to participate in and benefit from scientific progress.

Humor Generation
A subfield of computational humor focused on developing systems that synthesize comedic content.

Recall Bias
A systematic error in clinical data caused by differences in how patients remember and report their medical experiences.

N-gram Language Model
An N-gram Language Model is a statistical language modeling approach that estimates the probability of a word sequence using contiguous sequences of N words.

Trigram Language Model
A Trigram Language Model is a specific type of N-gram language model that predicts word probabilities based on sequences of three words or two prior context words.<SEP>A statistical n-gram language modeling technique using sequences of three words, evaluated on tweet and news datasets for humor classification.

Brown Corpus
The Brown Corpus is a text corpus whose newswire sections were used in prior research to build a 'common language' model.

News Commentary Corpus
The News Commentary Corpus is a collection of English news text used alongside the News Crawl Corpus to train unfunny baseline language models.

News Crawl Corpus
The News Crawl Corpus is an English news dataset from 2008, 2010, and 2011 utilized to train common language models.

KenLM Toolkit
The KenLM Toolkit is a language modeling software tool used to train, estimate, and score N-gram models with modified Kneser-Ney smoothing.

Modified Kneser-Ney Smoothing
Modified Kneser-Ney Smoothing is an estimation and smoothing technique applied without pruning in the KenLM tool to handle unseen N-grams.

Statistical Language Model
A statistical language model estimates the probability distribution of a sequence of words or an upcoming word based on linguistic training data.

Unigram
A unigram is a single-word sequence representing the lowest order unit in N-gram language modeling.

Bigram
A bigram is a contiguous two-word sequence utilized in training statistical language models.

Markov Assumption
The Markov assumption posits that the probability of a word depends solely on a small number of preceding words, simplifying sentence probability estimation.

Common Language Model
A common language model represents standard, typical language patterns, serving as a baseline to evaluate distinctiveness, memorability, and humor.

Back-Off Technique
The back-off technique is an estimation method in KenLM that calculates probabilities using lower-order N-grams with back-off weights when higher-order N-grams are absent.

Tokenization
Tokenization is a linguistic data preprocessing step performed via specialized toolkits to segment Twitter messages into filtered word tokens.<SEP>Tokenization is a text pre-processing procedure where input text is segmented into discrete tokens by splitting on whitespace and punctuation.

Filtering
Filtering is a pre-processing method specifically applied to the tweet corpus to remove URLs, user mentions, and hashtag symbols.

Task Organizers
The Task Organizers are the competition committee responsible for providing the tweet datasets and formulating Subtask A and Subtask B.<SEP>The committee or coordinating body responsible for designing the shared ICD-10 coding challenge and providing datasets, dictionaries, and evaluation benchmarks.

Tweet Corpus
The Tweet Corpus is a dataset provided by task organizers consisting of 106 hashtag files and approximately 21,000 tokens divided into development and training partitions.

Bigram Language Model
A statistical n-gram language modeling technique using sequences of two words, analyzed during the development and post-evaluation phases.

#HashtagWars
An online social media competition or trend generating humor-oriented tweets targeted for future corpus collection.

Neural Relation Extraction
A natural language processing methodology aimed at extracting semantic relations between entities using neural networks.<SEP>A natural language processing subfield and machine learning category focused on extracting semantic relations between entities using neural models.<SEP>A subfield and task in natural language processing (NRE) focused on predicting semantic relations between entities from text, evaluated for gender bias.<SEP>Neural Relation Extraction (NRE) is an NLP task and model category focused on predicting semantic relationships between entities in text.<SEP>Neural Relation Extraction (NRE) is an application of neural network architectures to relation extraction, contributing to automated knowledge base construction.

Automated Knowledge Base Construction
A domain in artificial intelligence dedicated to automatically extracting structured facts and knowledge from unstructured text.<SEP>Automated Knowledge Base Construction (AKBC) is the process and domain of automatically building or expanding structured knowledge repositories using extraction models.

WikiGenderBias
A benchmark dataset derived from Wikipedia used to train word embeddings and analyze gender bias in relation extraction models.<SEP>A distantly supervised benchmark dataset featuring a human-annotated test set, created to evaluate gender bias in neural relation extraction systems.<SEP>A large dataset designed for the evaluation and benchmarking of gender bias in relation extraction and other NLP tasks.<SEP>A specialized benchmark dataset created to assess and measure gender bias in neural relation extraction models.<SEP>WikiGenderBias is a dataset created from Wikipedia data to analyze gender bias and train and test neural relation extraction models.<SEP>WikiGenderBias is a distantly supervised dataset containing a human-annotated test set of approximately 45,000 sentences curated to train and evaluate relation extraction systems for gender bias.

Unigram Language Model
A class of statistical language models applied in morphological and subword segmentation comparison methods.<SEP>A statistical language modeling technique based on single-word probabilities, considered for future NLP modeling work.<SEP>A unigram language model is a zero-order memoryless Markov model assuming that sub-word units or morphs occur independently in a word.

Character-Level Language Model
A language modeling method that predicts sequences at the character level rather than word level.<SEP>A statistical model estimating probabilities of character sequences, used to initialize subword candidate probabilities.

Back-Off N-Gram Models
Traditional statistical n-gram language models utilizing smoothing and back-off strategies, against which neural network models are compared.

Social Bias
Social bias encompasses unfairness, disparities, and societal prejudices manifested within natural language processing and machine learning models.<SEP>Systematic prejudice or disparity reflected in automated natural language processing and artificial intelligence systems.

Distant Supervision
A semi-supervised machine learning paradigm used to automatically label training data using existing knowledge bases, utilized in creating WikiGenderBias.<SEP>A weakly supervised machine learning technique used to automatically generate labeled training data for relation extraction by aligning knowledge bases with text.<SEP>Distant Supervision is a machine learning paradigm used to automatically generate training data for relation extraction models by aligning text with knowledge bases.

Evaluation Stage
The formal competition and testing phase of the shared task where system runs were officially evaluated and ranked.

Development Stage
The experimental and trial phase where system parameters, tokenization settings, and n-gram models were optimized on trial data.

#BreakUpIn5Words
A specific viral Twitter hashtag event and dataset file on which the language modeling system achieved exceptionally high performance in Subtask A and B.

Barack Obama
Barack Obama is an individual referenced as an example entity in a relation tuple (Barack Obama, spouse, Michelle Obama) illustrating relation extraction.

Michelle Obama
Michelle Obama is an individual referenced as an example entity in a relation tuple (Barack Obama, spouse, Michelle Obama) illustrating relation extraction.

Relation Extraction
A natural language processing subtask focused on identifying semantic relationships between entity pairs in text.<SEP>An information extraction subdiscipline concerned with detecting and classifying semantic relationships between entities in text.<SEP>Relation Extraction (RE) is a natural language processing task aimed at extracting semantic relations from unstructured text and representing them as succinct tuples to populate knowledge bases.

NYT Dataset
The NYT dataset is an existing relation extraction benchmark derived from the New York Times that lacks reliable gender information for evaluating social bias.

Counterfactual Data Augmentation
Counterfactual Data Augmentation (CDA) is a bias mitigation method that swaps masculine and feminine words to equalize training contexts.<SEP>Counterfactual Data Augmentation is a training set debiasing method involving gender-swapping used to reduce gender bias in predictive models.

Hard Debiasing
A word embedding debiasing method that modifies vector representations to eliminate gender bias while preserving semantic meaning.<SEP>Hard Debiasing is a debiasing technique applied to word embeddings to mitigate gender bias in downstream predictions.

Name Anonymization
A bias mitigation technique where entity names are replaced or masked to prevent models from learning spurious demographic associations.<SEP>A debiasing approach aimed at removing entity names to reduce entity-specific bias in relation extraction models.<SEP>A debiasing technique that replaces entity names to evaluate and reduce entity-level gender bias in relation extraction models.<SEP>Name Anonymization (NA) is a bias mitigation technique that replaces named person entities with placeholders to prevent names from serving as gender proxies.<SEP>Name Anonymization is a data pre-processing and debiasing technique analyzed for its capacity to reduce bias in relation extraction models.

Equality of Opportunity
A fairness metric evaluated to determine whether relation extraction models perform equitably across male and female demographic data points.<SEP>Equality of Opportunity is a fairness metric used to evaluate neural relation extraction models across binary gender attributes.<SEP>Equality of Opportunity is a fairness metric used to evaluate predictors and allocative bias in machine learning models.

OpenNRE
An open-source neural relation extraction toolkit and framework whose models are trained and evaluated on WikiGenderBias.<SEP>An open-source neural relation extraction toolkit and model collection evaluated for Equality of Opportunity and gender bias across relation types.<SEP>An open-source toolkit and framework used for implementing, training, and benchmarking neural relation extraction models.<SEP>OpenNRE is an open-source neural relation extraction system and toolkit evaluated for gender bias and debiasing effects across various models.<SEP>OpenNRE is an open-source neural relation extraction toolkit and code repository providing various encoders and selectors for evaluating models.

Knowledge Bases
Knowledge Bases (KBs) are structured repositories of knowledge built or extended using relation extraction models, which downstream NLP applications rely on.

Task-Based Dialogue Systems
Task-Based Dialogue Systems are downstream natural language processing applications that rely on structured knowledge bases to execute user tasks.

Allocative Bias
Allocative bias refers to unfairness in the distribution of resources, opportunities, or information, such as disparate representation of gender in knowledge bases.

F1 Score
A statistical metric used to measure model performance and quantify the performance gap between male and female datapoints.<SEP>A statistical metric used to quantify the accuracy and performance of the LID model across held-out evaluation samples.<SEP>F1 score is an evaluation metric category measuring the harmonic mean of precision and recall, used to evaluate the AE task.<SEP>The F1 score is a performance metric measuring the harmonic mean of precision and recall, used to evaluate relation extraction models and compute gender performance differences.

DBPedia
A structured knowledge base project that extracts data from Wikipedia, used to retrieve relation sets for the WikiGenderBias dataset.

AMT
Amazon Mechanical Turk, a crowdsourcing platform used to recruit human workers for annotating ground truth labels for the relation extraction test set.

Barack
A prominent individual referenced as an example entity in Wikipedia articles to illustrate the distant supervision relation extraction process.

Michelle
An individual referenced as an example entity linked to Barack through the spouse relation in relation extraction examples.

England
A geographic location whose residents were eligible to participate as AMT annotators for ground truth labeling.<SEP>England is one of the countries from which crowd workers were recruited to perform annotation tasks.

Gender-Swapping
A bias mitigation and counterfactual data augmentation technique that removes contextual gender bias and bolsters relation extraction performance.<SEP>A data-level debiasing and augmentation technique that swaps gendered terms and pronouns to achieve gender parity in training datasets.

Spouse Relation
A semantic relation evaluated in neural relation extraction that frequently exhibits high gender bias and performance disparities.<SEP>A semantic relation in WikiGenderBias connecting married entities, hypothesized to be vulnerable to model gender bias due to lexical patterns in female Wikipedia articles.

Hypernym Relation
A semantic relation in relation extraction that exhibited low initial gender bias but an increased performance gap under name anonymization.<SEP>A semantic relation representing categorical type or occupation, hypothesized to correlate with male entities in Wikipedia articles.

BirthDate Relation
A biographical relation used as an experimental control in WikiGenderBias, expected to show no correlation with entity gender.<SEP>A semantic relation evaluated in relation extraction that showed low Equality of Opportunity satisfaction across multiple architectures.

BirthPlace Relation
A geographic biographical relation used as an experimental control in WikiGenderBias, expected to be unaffected by gender bias.<SEP>A semantic relation evaluated in neural relation extraction that exhibited substantial gender bias comparable to the spouse relation.

Hard-Debiasing
Hard-Debiasing is a bias mitigation technique applied to word embeddings to remove gender components from gender-neutral word vectors.

PCNN
Piecewise Convolutional Neural Network (PCNN) is a neural encoder that applies piecewise max-pooling based on head and tail entity positions.<SEP>Piecewise Convolutional Neural Network architecture evaluated in neural relation extraction alongside average and attention selectors.

RNN
A class of neural network architectures typically trained to recognize temporal patterns across sequential data.<SEP>Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) is a neural network architecture used as an encoder for sequential data in OpenNRE.<SEP>Recurrent Neural Network architecture whose combination with attention exhibited high bias on the spouse relation.<SEP>Recurrent Neural Network, a category of neural model architecture evaluated with an attention mechanism for intent argument inference.

Bi-RNN
Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Network (Bi-RNN) is a sequence encoder in OpenNRE that processes text sequences in both directions.<SEP>Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Network architecture evaluated for gender bias and Equality of Opportunity in relation extraction.

Wikipedia Infoboxes
Wikipedia Infoboxes are structured data boxes on Wikipedia articles that were analyzed for gender-based discrepancies in spouse information.

Hard-Debiased Word Embeddings
A bias mitigation technique utilizing debiased word embeddings to reduce performance disparities across gender categories.

CDA
Counterfactual Data Augmentation, a debiasing technique applied to training text to reduce gender bias in embedding and relation extraction models.

Average Selector
A sentence selector baseline in neural relation extraction that weights training sentences equally and demonstrated superior bias mitigation over attention selectors.

Attention Selector
A sentence selection mechanism in neural relation extraction models that weights sentences according to learned attention scores.

EiTAKA
A research team or system participating in the SemEval-2018 Task 1 competition focused on emotion analysis of tweets.

SiTAKA
A research team or system that participated in the Twitter Sentiment Analysis Track in SemEval 2017.

SemEval-2018 Task 1
An academic evaluation competition focusing on affect and emotion analysis in tweets.

SemEval 2017
An international workshop on semantic evaluation featuring a Twitter Sentiment Analysis Track.<SEP>SemEval 2017 is an international workshop and evaluation campaign on semantic analysis, featuring competitive NLP benchmarks including the Twitter Sentiment Analysis Track.

Gender Swapping
A data pre-processing and debiasing technique that swaps gender indicators to mitigate context and gender bias in models.

Debiased Embeddings
A bias mitigation method that modifies word representation vectors to reduce gender-based stereotyping and performance gaps.

XGBoost Regressors
An ensemble gradient boosting algorithm applied to valence intensity regression and emotion classification.

N-Stream ConvNets
A deep learning convolutional neural network architecture utilized for tweet affect and emotion analysis.

Equality Of Opportunity
A fairness metric measuring whether predictors achieve equal prediction recall across demographic groups, such as male and female entities.

Twitter Sentiment Analysis Track
The Twitter Sentiment Analysis Track is an evaluation track within SemEval 2017 focused on classifying the sentiment and polarity of tweets across multiple languages.

Message Polarity Classification
Message Polarity Classification is Subtask A of the Twitter Sentiment Analysis Track at SemEval 2017, assessing systems on their ability to determine whether a tweet is positive, negative, or neutral.

King Saud University
King Saud University is a higher education and research institution whose Arabic corpus (Ksucorpus) was used to train Arabic word embedding models.

Bing Liu
Bing Liu is a computer science researcher whose opinion lexicons were utilized and translated into Arabic for sentiment analysis evaluation.

Bag Of Words
Bag of Words is an n-gram text feature extraction category representing sequences of tokens to provide contextual information for classification.

Bag Of Negated Words
Bag of Negated Words is a specialized feature representation category capturing sequences of tokens within negated contexts in text.

Part Of Speech Tagging
Part of speech tagging is a grammatical text annotation category used to distinguish subjective, non-neutral terms from objective content.

SiTAKA Team
The SiTAKA research team developed the SiTAKA system and participated in the SemEval 2017 Twitter Sentiment Analysis Track, ranking 8th in English and 2nd in Arabic.

Stanford University
Stanford University is a research institution whose NLP group developed the Stanford Tagger used for tokenization and POS tagging of Arabic tweets.

Arabic Wikipedia
Arabic Wikipedia is an open-collaborative Arabic-language encyclopedia project whose corpus was used to train Arabic word embeddings.

Support Vector Machines
A class of supervised machine learning algorithms that served as the primary foundation for constructing the study's sentiment classification models.<SEP>A traditional machine learning classification algorithm historically applied to sentiment analysis tasks.<SEP>Support Vector Machines (SVM) is a machine learning classifier widely reported and utilized for sentiment analysis classification problems.<SEP>Support Vector Machines (SVM) is a supervised machine learning classification algorithm widely used for large-scale text and sentiment categorization.

Opinion Lexicons
Opinion lexicons are vocabulary resources containing polarity information used to compute sentiment scores and feature representations.

En-SiTAKA
En-SiTAKA is a sentiment analysis system designed to classify English-language tweets using semantic clusters, embeddings, and lexicons.

Ar-SiTAKA
Ar-SiTAKA is a sentiment analysis system designed to evaluate and classify Arabic-language tweets.

Part of Speech
Part of Speech (POS) refers to syntactic word classes—such as nouns, adjectives, adverbs, and verbs—whose frequencies and distributions are used as features to differentiate subjective from objective texts.

Bi-tagged Features
Bi-tagged features are syntactic representation features that combine bigram word tokens with their corresponding part-of-speech tags to capture expressive and subjective phrases.

Ark Tweet NLP
Ark Tweet NLP is a natural language processing toolkit for Twitter that provides pretrained resources, including 1,000 Brown clusters generated from 56 million English-language tweets.

Brown Clustering Algorithm
The Brown clustering algorithm is a hierarchical clustering algorithm used to group words based on syntactic and semantic context from large text corpora.

K-means Algorithm
The K-means algorithm is an unsupervised clustering method applied to group 40-dimensional word embeddings into 4,960 semantic clusters.

Pooling Functions
Pooling functions are element-wise mathematical operations (sum, standard-deviation, minimum, and maximum) used to convert variable-length word embedding vectors into a fixed-length tweet vector representation.

URV
URV (Universitat Rovira i Virgili) is an academic research institution that provided research support funds for the sentiment analysis project.

Martí i Franqués
Martí i Franqués is a historical figure whose namesake PhD grant provided partial funding for the research work.

Subword Segmentation
A natural language processing technique for breaking words down into smaller subword units or morphemes.<SEP>Subword Segmentation is an NLP data preprocessing technique that splits words into subword units to handle vocabulary size, out-of-vocabulary words, and morphological complexity.

Finnish
A natural language used to evaluate subword seed lexicons, pre-pruning, and morphological segmentation accuracy.<SEP>Finnish is a Finno-Ugric language category used in the morphological segmentation experiments and error analysis.<SEP>Finnish is a language used in existing evaluation benchmarks paired with English in prior BLI studies.<SEP>Finnish is a morphologically rich language used in data sets to evaluate subword and morphological segmentation methods.

North Sami
North Sami is a language whose dataset was utilized in evaluating the unigram subword segmentation models.

Morfessor Baseline
A baseline morphological segmentation algorithm initialized with whole words that uses greedy local search and recursive binary splitting.<SEP>A baseline statistical morphological segmentation framework for which the EM+Prune algorithm is introduced.<SEP>Morfessor Baseline is a probabilistic generative morphological segmentation model whose recursive training algorithm and optimization problems are analyzed and improved in the study.<SEP>Morfessor Baseline is an unsupervised generative method within the Morfessor family that uses MAP estimation and greedy local search for morphological segmentation.

Morfessor EM+Prune
A proposed training algorithm for Morfessor Baseline designed to reduce search error during training and lower Morfessor model costs.<SEP>A subword segmentation method combining the unigram language model and priors of Morfessor Baseline with an EM+Prune training algorithm.<SEP>Morfessor EM+Prune is a morphological segmentation and subword tokenization framework combining Expectation-Maximization (EM) training with lexicon pruning strategies.<SEP>Morfessor EM+Prune is a novel unigram subword segmentation algorithm that integrates Expectation Maximization and lexicon pruning to reduce search error and improve segmentation accuracy.<SEP>Morfessor EM+Prune is a proposed morphological segmentation method combining Expectation Maximization with iterative lexicon pruning.

SentencePiece
A subword segmentation method and tool designed for multilingual NLP systems and neural machine translation, using an EM+Prune training algorithm.<SEP>A subword tokenisation tool and variant category of BPE used to address rare words in neural machine translation systems.<SEP>A subword tokenization library and technique mentioned regarding token count choices across source and target data.<SEP>SentencePiece is a subword tokenization algorithm that can be recovered as a special case of Morfessor EM+Prune by omitting the prior and applying specific configuration settings.<SEP>SentencePiece is a subword tokenization and segmentation approach that can be derived from Morfessor EM+Prune using specific hyper-parameters.<SEP>SentencePiece is a widely adopted unigram subword segmentation method and software implementation evaluated and compared against Morfessor EM+Prune.

Greedy Unigram Likelihood
A subword segmentation and pruning strategy based on unigram probability models, designed for speech recognition.<SEP>Greedy Unigram Likelihood is an existing subword segmentation method operating in a generative unigram language modeling framework.

Expectation Maximization
Expectation Maximization (EM) is an iterative statistical optimization algorithm utilized in the training phase of the proposed Morfessor EM+Prune method.<SEP>The Expectation Maximization (EM) algorithm is an iterative technique for finding Maximum Likelihood or Maximum a Posteriori estimates in models with latent variables.

Decision Tree
A Decision Tree is a supervised classification model exemplified in the study's experimental illustrations.<SEP>A supervised learning algorithm evaluated among candidate classifiers for Twitter speech act classification.

Hammarström
Hammarström is an NLP researcher who authored a notable 2011 survey on unsupervised morphological segmentation methods.

Ruokolainen
Ruokolainen is a researcher whose comparative evaluation and morphological error analysis framework is utilized in the study.<SEP>Ruokolainen is an NLP researcher who authored a 2016 comparative survey on semi-supervised morphological segmentation.

Sennrich
A researcher referenced for describing the Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) algorithm in neural machine translation.<SEP>A researcher who first adapted Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) from data compression to neural machine translation to learn subword units.<SEP>Sennrich is a computational linguistics researcher who first adapted the Byte Pair Encoding segmentation algorithm for neural machine translation in 2015.<SEP>Sennrich is a researcher cited for work on Byte Pair Encoding merge operations and joint bilingual vocabulary learning in neural machine translation.

EI-reg Task
EI-reg is an Emotion Intensity regression benchmark task evaluated in the research experiments.

V-reg Task
V-reg is a Valence regression evaluation task benchmarked in the experimental analysis.

EI-oc Task
EI-oc is an Emotion Intensity ordinal classification evaluation task assessed in the experimental results.

V-oc Task
V-oc is a Valence ordinal classification evaluation task evaluated in the sentiment analysis study.

Spitkovsky
Spitkovsky is a researcher who introduced lateen-EM, an alternating optimization method combining Expectation Maximization and Viterbi optimization.

Virpioja
