A low-resource machine translation model initialized with parameters transferred from a parent model and fine-tuned on limited data.<SEP>A neural machine translation model for a low-resource language pair that is regularized or initialized using a parent model.<SEP>A translation model trained on a low-resource language pair that leverages transferred parameters from a pre-trained parent model.

String-to-Tree Statistical MT
A specific syntax-based statistical machine translation formulation that translates source strings directly into target parse trees.

Document Classification
An NLP classification task where deep transfer learning techniques have demonstrated positive results.

Latin Characters
A writing script used as a source or target task domain in transfer learning experiments for character recognition.

Chinese Characters
A writing script domain evaluated in convolutional transfer learning studies alongside Latin characters.

WMT 2015
The 2015 Workshop on Statistical Machine Translation, whose French-English dataset serves as the high-resource training corpus for the parent models.

ACL-IJCNLP
A joint academic conference on natural language processing where foundational work on unknown word replacement was published.

Noise-Contrastive Estimation
A statistical training method used to train the neural language model with a target vocabulary of 100,000 words.<SEP>A statistical training technique applied to train the large-vocabulary LSTM neural language model efficiently.

Transfer NMT
A neural machine translation approach that utilizes transfer learning from a parent model to improve translation performance on low-resource child languages.

SBMT
Syntax-Based Machine Translation, a strong baseline translation system against which transfer models and re-scoring techniques are compared.

French-English
A high-resource parent language pair used across transfer learning experiments to transfer representations to child language pairs.

Spanish-English
A child language pair used in experiments evaluating the impact of different parent languages on transfer learning performance.

Uzbek-English
A low-resource child language pair used to test transfer from parent models such as French-English.

French'
A synthetic child language designed with the exact distributional and relational properties of French but with randomly shuffled vocabulary.

Berkeley Aligner
A statistical alignment tool used to generate word-to-word t-tables between language pairs for dictionary initialization in transfer models.

English-French
A language pair used in conjunction with Uzbek-English to build translation tables via the Berkeley Aligner.

Dictionary Initialization
A transfer technique where child model input embeddings are seeded using parent embeddings guided by word-to-word t-table probabilities.

ARL/ARO
ARL/ARO (Army Research Laboratory / Army Research Office) is a military research organization that provided funding under grant W911NF-10-1-0533.

Sutskever
Sutskever is a researcher cited for the foundational 2014 work on the encoder-decoder framework for neural machine translation.

String-to-Tree Statistical Machine Translation
String-to-tree statistical machine translation (SBMT) is a strong statistical baseline translation system compared against and re-scored by NMT models.

French′
French′ is a synthetic child language identical to French except for modified word spellings, created to test the impact of parent–child language similarity in transfer learning.

Recurrent Neural Network Language Model
A monolingual neural language model (RNN LM) trained on English text, used both as an experimental parent model and for re-scoring SBMT outputs.

Distributed Word Representation
A technique in natural language processing where words are mapped to continuous vectors of real numbers in a low-dimensional space, capturing syntactic and semantic relationships.

Skip-Gram
A neural network model and word embedding method (word2vec) trained to predict context words given an input word, known for capturing morpho-syntactic and semantic properties via linear vector operations.<SEP>Skip-gram is a class of neural network models used to generate word vector embeddings from word contexts.

SubGram
A proposed extension of the Skip-gram model that incorporates character-level substring structure (such as n-grams) into word representations to enhance morpho-syntactic performance without requiring explicit linguistic annotation.<SEP>SubGram is a substring-oriented neural network model architecture extending Skip-gram to learn vector embeddings from character n-grams.<SEP>SubGram is an extension of the Skip-gram model that incorporates substrings of input words to better capture morphosyntactic relations and out-of-vocabulary terms.

Continuous Bag-Of-Words
A neural network word embedding model (CBOW) related to Skip-gram that predicts a target word from surrounding context words, mentioned as a baseline model augmented with morphological knowledge.

Neural Network
A computational architecture inspired by biological neural networks, used in machine learning for tasks such as representation learning, language modeling, and translation.

Hierarchical Softmax
An efficient approximation of the softmax normalization function used in neural networks and word embedding models such as Skip-gram to accelerate training.

Image Annotation
A computer vision and natural language processing task involving generating textual descriptions or tags for images, which benefits from learned word vectors.

Semantic Relations
Semantic relations are a category of linguistic relations dealing with word meanings and analogies, which were tested alongside syntactic relations.<SEP>Semantic relations is a category of word analogies testing conceptual associations such as capitals, currencies, and family terms.

Syntactic Relations
Syntactic relations is a category of grammatical and morphological word analogies testing inflections like plurals, tenses, and degrees of comparison.

Vector Embeddings
Vector embeddings are dense mathematical representations of words in continuous vector space that capture linguistic semantics and syntax.

Rule-Based Baseline
Rule-based baseline is a deterministic heuristic system based on regular English morphological suffix and prefix rules used for comparison.

Morphosyntactic Relations
Morphosyntactic relations refer to linguistic and grammatical transformations situated at the intersection of morphology and syntax.<SEP>Morphosyntactic relations represent a linguistic category focusing on the grammatical and morphological variations of words, tested via question pairs in the evaluation sets.

Czech Republic
A country in Central Europe whose Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports funds the LINDAT/CLARIN project.<SEP>The Czech Republic is a European country whose Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports funded language resources utilized in the research.

data.entity_name: Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports
data.content:
Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports
The Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports is a Czech government ministry overseeing educational and language research initiatives, including the LINDAT/CLARIN project.

LINDAT/CLARIN
A research project that develops, stores, and distributes language resources used in the research.<SEP>LINDAT/CLARIN is a research infrastructure project in the Czech Republic that develops, stores, and distributes language resources.

QT21
QT21 is a research project supported by the European Union's Horizon 2020 programme under grant agreement no. 645452.<SEP>QT21 is an EU-funded research project focused on machine translation and language technologies under the Horizon 2020 programme.

GAUK
GAUK (Grant Agency of Charles University) is a research funding body that supported the study through grant 8502/2016.<SEP>GAUK (Grant Agency of Charles University) is a research funding body that supported the study under grant 8502/2016.

SVV
SVV is a university research support program and funding scheme that provided financial backing for the project.

Skip-gram
Skip-gram is a word embedding architecture that predicts context words given a target word, serving as the baseline model.

Rule-based Approach
Rule-based approach is a deterministic, heuristic-based NLP methodology used as a baseline that outperforms neural network models on morphosyntactic tasks.

Syntactic Questions
Syntactic questions is an analogy test set category evaluating grammatical patterns and morphological transformations between word pairs.

Opposites
Opposites is a question set category expanded in the test set to cover negation and antonymy across adjectives, nouns, and verbs.

Verb Tense
Verb tense is a morphosyntactic category evaluated through pairs of verb forms and their morphological variations.

data.entity_name: Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports of the Czech Republic
data.content:
Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports of the Czech Republic
A government ministry of the Czech Republic that supported the LINDAT/CLARIN language resource project under project LM2015071.

Sociolinguistics
A branch of linguistics that studies the effect of external social, geographic, and socioeconomic factors on language variation and communication norms.<SEP>Sociolinguistics is an academic field and research domain focusing on the relationships between language variation, social factors, and demographic characteristics.<SEP>Sociolinguistics is the field of study examining linguistic variation and features in relation to socioeconomic status, geography, time, and social networks.<SEP>Sociolinguistics is the scientific field analyzing the relationship between language variation, geographic distribution, and socioeconomic factors.

Computational Sociolinguistics
An interdisciplinary research field combining computer science and sociolinguistics to analyze digital interaction patterns and language variation at scale.

Southern France
Southern France is a geographic region whose language use was found to be more standard compared to the North.<SEP>The southern region of France characterized by language closer to standard grammatical conventions and greater vocabulary diversity.<SEP>The southern region of France, identified in the study as exhibiting a spatial pattern with more standard language variants and greater lexical diversity.<SEP>The southern region of France, observed in the sociolinguistic study to have a higher propensity for standard language use compared to the northern region.

Northern France
Northern France is a geographic region whose residents were found to use more non-standard linguistic terms and a smaller vocabulary set compared to the South.<SEP>The northern region of France identified in the study as having lower rates of standard language usage and smaller vocabulary sizes.<SEP>The northern region of France, analyzed in contrast with the southern region in terms of dialectal and standard linguistic usage.

Computational Social Science
An interdisciplinary research domain integrating computer science and social sciences to analyze digital human behavior and communication.

Linguistic Variables
Linguistic variables are quantitative language markers extracted from user timelines, specifically standard negation rate, plural agreement rate, and vocabulary size.<SEP>Structural or phonetic points in language that permit multiple variants conveying identical reference but carrying distinct social significance.

Standard Language Variants
Linguistic forms associated with formality, educational attainment, social prestige, and higher socioeconomic status.<SEP>Standardized linguistic forms whose frequency of use was found to correlate with socioeconomic status, geography, and daily activity cycles.

Non-Standard Language Variants
Vernacular linguistic forms associated with local solidarity, social bonding, and informal communication.

Status Homophily
Status homophily is a sociological principle describing the tendency of individuals with similar socioeconomic status to associate and connect with one another.<SEP>Status homophily is the sociodynamic tendency for individuals with similar socioeconomic status to connect, interact, and form social ties.<SEP>Status homophily is the sociological phenomenon where individuals from similar socioeconomic classes tend to connect with one another in social networks.<SEP>The principle that people associate with others of similar socioeconomic status, evaluated in social network linguistic analyses.

Zillow.com
Zillow.com is an online real estate service utilized in prior research to derive socioeconomic indicators to augment Twitter data.

Socioeconomic Status
A demographic classification based on metrics such as income, education level, and population density, examined for its correlation with language usage.<SEP>A metric and classification reflecting individuals' economic and social standing, measured through indicators such as income and population density.<SEP>Socioeconomic Status is a demographic categorization proxied by income, which strongly correlates with linguistic patterns and temporal Twitter activity.<SEP>Socioeconomic status (SES) is a composite measure of social and economic position, proxied through income, homeownership, and population density.<SEP>Socioeconomic status (SES) is a social classification metric that correlates with linguistic markers, temporal activity patterns, and social network clustering.<SEP>Socioeconomic status (SES) is an economic and sociological measure of an individual or population's standing, proxied in the study by income per capita, homeownership fraction, and population density.<SEP>Socioeconomic status is a demographic classification representing an individual's social and economic standing, inferred through indicators such as census data and location.<SEP>Socioeconomic status is a major demographic variable analyzed in the study to evaluate its relationship with sociolinguistic features.<SEP>Socioeconomic status refers to an individual's social and economic standing, inferred from income and used to partition users into socioeconomic classes.

Standard Occupation Classification
The Standard Occupation Classification (SOC) is an occupational classification system used to assign socioeconomic status based on occupational mentions.

Web Content Analysis
A subfield of computational research focused on evaluating text features, metrics, and language markers across online platforms.

Multivariate Analysis
A statistical methodology employed to analyze multiple variables simultaneously, identifying correlations among linguistic cues, socioeconomic status, and geography.

Linear Regression
A statistical modeling approach used in the study to evaluate relationships between sociolinguistic variables and demographic factors.<SEP>Linear Regression is a fundamental statistical and supervised learning algorithm used for predictive modeling and sentiment analysis tasks.<SEP>Linear regression is a statistical modeling method used to perform regression analysis on the sociolinguistic dataset.

Census Data
Census data provides official French population distributions across administrative units, used to validate inferred Twitter population distributions.<SEP>Official demographic and socioeconomic survey data collected by governments, combined with social media data to overcome user profile inaccuracies.

Geolocation Metadata
Geographic coordinate data embedded within social media posts, used by researchers to infer users' home locations.

Lexical Diversity
A linguistic measure of vocabulary set size known to have a positive relationship with socioeconomic status.<SEP>A measure of vocabulary size and range used to evaluate language patterns across different geographic regions and socioeconomic groups.

Datasift
Datasift is a data provider company that provided access to Twitter PowerTrack API feeds for the research dataset.

Gnip
Gnip is a social data provider company that provided Twitter PowerTrack API feeds for the study.

Social Network Analysis
Social Network Analysis refers to the methodology used to infer social ties, interactions, and user network structures from mutual mentions.

Scikit Learn Toolkit
The Scikit Learn Toolkit is a machine learning software library used in the study to perform linear regression analysis.

Pandas
Pandas is a Python data analysis library utilized for data preprocessing in the study.

NetworkX
NetworkX is a Python software library used for graph analysis and studying social network structures.

MElt
MElt is a part-of-speech (POS) tagger tested during data preprocessing for the detection of French linguistic markers.

French Language
French is the language studied in the research, specifically focusing on the realization of the negative particle and standard versus non-standard variants.<SEP>The French language is the primary linguistic focus of the study, encompassing 170 million tweets analyzed for sociolinguistic variation.

Geographic Location
Geographic location is a spatial variable determined via GPS coordinates and used to study spatial sociolinguistic patterns across France.

GMT
GMT (Greenwich Mean Time) is one of the two timezones defining the geographic and temporal boundaries for user data collection.

GMT+1
GMT+1 is the timezone covering France, used as a filter for selecting Twitter users in the study.

data.entity_name: National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies
data.content:
National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies
The National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE) is France's national statistics bureau, which released a fine-grained sociodemographic dataset in December 2016 based on 2010 tax returns.<SEP>The National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE) is the national statistics bureau of France that released a sociodemographic dataset in December 2016 based on 2010 tax returns.

2010 French Tax Return
The 2010 French tax return is a nationwide administrative tax data collection event used by INSEE to estimate aggregated sociodemographic indicators across France.<SEP>The 2010 nationwide tax return collection in France, which served as the empirical basis for INSEE's sociodemographic patch estimates.

French Regions
The 22 administrative regions of France used as a high-level spatial resolution unit to evaluate correlation between inferred and official population distributions.

Arrondissements of France
The 322 administrative arrondissement units across France used to assess population distribution correlation at an intermediate geographic level.

Cantons of France
The 4,055 canton-level administrative units across France representing a fine-grained spatial resolution in the population analysis.

INSEE Dataset Release
The December 2016 public release by INSEE of aggregated 200m by 200m patch sociodemographic indicators for the whole French territory.

Average Yearly Income Per Capita
A socioeconomic indicator measured in euros representing cumulative household income divided by the total number of inhabitants within a 200m by 200m square patch.

Real Estate Ownership Fraction
A socioeconomic metric defined as the proportion of real estate owners relative to the total population living within a spatial patch.

Population Density
A demographic indicator within the study whose lower values are consistently indicative of higher socioeconomic status.<SEP>A demographic metric defined as the number of individuals residing within a 200m by 200m (4-hectare) square patch.<SEP>A socioeconomic demographic indicator representing the concentration of individuals in a geographic area, transformed logarithmically for regression analysis.

Pareto Principle
An economic distribution principle positing heavy-tailed inequality in wealth and socioeconomic variables, contrasted with the winzorized empirical indicators.

INSEE
INSEE (National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies) is the French statistical agency that provides comprehensive socioeconomic census datasets used as a ground truth and benchmark in the study.<SEP>The French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies, referenced as the source for socioeconomic dataset features and population density metrics.<SEP>The National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies in France, whose socioeconomic maps and indicators were linked to geolocated Twitter data.

French Metropolitan Territory
The geographic territory of metropolitan France across which the study's dataset of geolocated Twitter users and socioeconomic maps were examined.

Standard Negation
A grammatical linguistic variable measuring adherence to standard versus incorrect negation forms in language usage.<SEP>A linguistic metric evaluating the adherence of users to formal grammatical negation rules across time and geographic departments.<SEP>A linguistic variable in French involving bipartite negation particles whose usage frequency correlates with socioeconomic status.<SEP>A specific linguistic variable measured from user timelines indicating the frequency or rate of using standard forms of grammatical negation.

Standard Plural Ending
A written French linguistic variable regarding the use of mute plural markers ('s' or 'x'), studied for omission rates relative to social status.

Spoken French
The oral variety of the French language characterized by features such as the optional omission of the preverbal negative particle 'ne' and the absence of phonetic plural endings on nouns and adjectives.

Written French
The standard orthographic register of French where bipartite negation is obligatory and plural forms of nouns and adjectives are marked with letters such as 's' or 'x'.

SES Indicators
Statistical and demographic metrics, such as income and population density, used to measure and evaluate the socioeconomic status of individuals.

Income
An economic indicator analyzed alongside density and other socioeconomic factors to determine individual socioeconomic status.

Language Acquisition
A scientific field studying the development of language in humans, demonstrating that child lexicon growth depends on the lexical diversity of caretakers.<SEP>The scientific field of linguistics and psychology studying how individuals acquire language, specifically noting that children's vocabulary growth depends on the lexical diversity of caretakers.

Negation Deletion
A sociolinguistic phenomenon in spoken French where the initial particle 'ne' is omitted from negative constructions.

Egocentric Social Network
A network model constructed from users' direct Twitter mentions to map and analyze personal social interactions in relation to language and socioeconomic status.

Vocabulary Set Size
A linguistic marker measuring the breadth and quantity of distinct words utilized in an individual's Twitter timeline.<SEP>A metric representing lexical diversity, defined as the normalized number of unique words used by a user or population.<SEP>A static linguistic metric measuring the diversity and breadth of unique words used by speakers within a given administrative department.

Linguistic Variation
The phenomenon of language differences and standard or non-standard expression usage across socioeconomic levels, geographic locations, and social networks.

Caretakers
Individuals responsible for raising children whose socioeconomic status, educational level, and lexical diversity influence the lexicon growth of children.

Plural Agreement
A linguistic variable measuring the frequency and correctness of plural forms compared to non-standard or incorrect plural expressions.<SEP>A linguistic variable tracking the rate of correct or standard plural grammatical agreements used in user timelines.

Average Income
An economic indicator reflecting individual or group earnings, found to have the highest correlation with vocabulary set size.

Education Level
A socioeconomic status indicator reflecting formal education, influencing lexical diversity and language usage.

Departments Of France
Administrative territorial divisions of France used to categorize geolocated users for studying regional and spatial linguistic variation.

Socioeconomic Variation
The structural differences in language variants and linguistic competence observed across varying socioeconomic groups.

Spatial Variation
The geographic divergence of linguistic variables across regions caused by historical local dialects, socioeconomic factors, or cross-border influences.

Standard Language Usage
Standard Language Usage is a linguistic classification reflecting adherence to formal grammar rules, such as standard negation and pluralization.

Linguistic Variability
Linguistic Variability is a research concept describing differences in vocabulary size, grammar standardization, and language usage across geographic, temporal, and social dimensions.

Suburban Paris
The suburban area of Paris marked by sharp socioeconomic segregation between its Eastern and Western sides, displaying linguistic patterns distinct from central Paris.

Standard Plural Agreement
A linguistic metric assessing the frequency of grammatically standard pluralization across regions, showing notable longitudinal variation.

Temporal Variation
A study dimension examining the periodic hourly and weekly fluctuations in user activity, standard language usage, and socioeconomic demographics.

Social Network
Social network refers to the web of mutual mention ties and social interactions connecting individuals.<SEP>The structural arrangement of connected individuals that influences linguistic patterns through various link-formation dynamics.

Homophily
A general social phenomenon where individuals with similar characteristics such as age, gender, interests, or socioeconomic status are more likely to form social connections.<SEP>A social network principle where individuals with similar characteristics such as age, gender, or interests form ties and influence one another.

Preferential Attachment
A network formation mechanism driving the creation of social ties and community-rich complex structures.<SEP>A network growth mechanism where individuals preferentially form ties with already well-connected nodes, contributing to complex social network structures.

Focal and Cyclic Closure
Structural link-creation mechanisms in social networks that foster the emergence of communities and clustered connections.

North
North refers to the northern region of France, where users were observed to use more non-standard linguistic terms and a smaller vocabulary set.

South
South refers to the southern region of France, where users showed higher usage of standard language variants and larger vocabulary compared to the North.

Social Influence
The social process by which connected individuals induce behavioral, linguistic, or opinion similarities in one another over time.

Twitter Mention Network
A social network structure constructed from mutual mention interactions between geolocated Twitter users in France.<SEP>The empirical graph structure of interactions and mentions among Twitter users utilized to examine peer connectivity and status homophily.

Configuration Model
A reference random network model that preserves structural network degree properties while removing social and structural correlations.

Temporal Activity
The diurnal variation in user activity across day and night, affecting observed linguistic patterns due to population turnover.

Physical Proximity
The geographical closeness of individuals within a spatial area, acting as a contributing factor to social connection and linguistic similarity.

Standard Language
Standard language refers to conventional linguistic variants and vocabulary commonly associated with higher socioeconomic strata and daytime online activity.

Non-Standard Language
Non-standard language refers to informal or vernacular linguistic variants and limited vocabulary sets, observed predominantly at night and among lower socioeconomic strata or regional groups.

Negative Particle in French
A specific grammatical marker in the French language whose variable realization exhibits direct correlations with three distinct indices of socioeconomic status.

Sample Survey of Geolocated Users
An empirical survey conducted on a set of geolocated Twitter users designed to bootstrap socioeconomic data and validate location and status inference models.

Marketing Design
A commercial and strategic domain identified as a direct practical application for inferring individuals' socioeconomic status from online linguistic and network behaviors.

OpenAI
OpenAI is an artificial intelligence research organization that developed OpenAI Gym, with which the HoME platform is compatible.<SEP>OpenAI is an artificial intelligence research organization that developed OpenAI Universe and the OpenAI Gym environment interface referenced for reinforcement learning compatibility.

Household Multimodal Environment (HoME)
HoME is an open-source, simulated 3D household platform designed for artificial agents to learn via multimodal inputs including vision, audio, semantics, and physical interaction.

Virtual Embodiment
Virtual embodiment is a machine learning paradigm in which artificial agents learn through dynamic, interactive, and multimodal sensory experiences within simulated environments.

Socioeconomic Status (SES)
Socioeconomic Status refers to the social and economic indicators, such as income and property ownership, studied for their correlation with linguistic variations.

Linguistic Markers
Linguistic markers are grammatical and lexical variables, such as correct negation, plural usage, and vocabulary size, evaluated across user groups and regions.

SUNCG Dataset
The SUNCG dataset is a collection of over 45,000 3D house layouts integrated into the HoME platform to facilitate large-scale contextual learning.

OpenAI Gym
OpenAI Gym is a standardized toolkit and interface for developing and comparing reinforcement learning algorithms, supported by HoME.

Language Grounding
A category of artificial intelligence tasks involving mapping natural language descriptions to real-world contexts, objects, and spatial relationships.<SEP>Language grounding is an AI task involving the connection of linguistic symbols to multimodal sensory inputs, actions, and physical objects.

Sound-Based Navigation
Sound-based navigation is an embodied agent task supported by HoME that requires agents to orient and navigate environments using acoustic perception.

Robotics
Robotics is a field of artificial intelligence and engineering focused on embodied agents, where contextual simulation environments assist in improving reward quality and control.

Multi-Agent Learning
Multi-agent learning is an artificial intelligence domain focused on training multiple agents simultaneously through interaction in a shared environment.

Visual Question Answering
A multimodal machine learning task requiring models to answer textual questions grounded in visual imagery.<SEP>Visual question answering is a multimodal AI task requiring systems to process both visual imagery and natural language queries.

Atari Benchmark
The Atari benchmark comprises classic video games used in reinforcement learning to train agents on complex strategies via trial and error.

Go
Go is a researcher who investigated keyword-based approaches and machine learning classifiers such as Maximum Entropy and Naive Bayes on Twitter sentiment.<SEP>Go is an abstract board game used in reinforcement learning to push agents to discover complex strategies through trial-and-error.

Mention Network
The mention network is a graph structure derived from Twitter user interactions that reflects socioeconomic correlations and community connectivity.

Cognitive Science
Cognitive science is an interdisciplinary field studying the mind and concept association, serving as inspiration for context-rich multimodal machine learning.

DeepMind
DeepMind is an artificial intelligence research laboratory that created DeepMind Lab, a maze-based 3D environment for training learning algorithms.<SEP>DeepMind is an artificial intelligence research organization that developed DeepMind Lab, an interactive 3D platform benchmarked against HoME.

Stanford
Stanford is a research institution associated with the Stanford Scenes 3D layout dataset referenced in comparison to SUNCG.<SEP>The institution whose typed dependencies framework was extended to formalize realization rules from SPARQL queries.

Household Environments
A category of interactive 3D simulation platforms set within domestic indoor scenes, including HoME, House3D, AI2-THOR, and Matterport3D Simulator, used for embodied AI research.

Visual Navigation
A category of embodied AI tasks focused on enabling autonomous agents to navigate through indoor spaces based on visual inputs.

Object Categories
A semantic classification comprising generic and detailed item classifications present within SUNCG house layouts.

Material Categories
A classification of physical textures and surface materials, such as wood or textile, that dictate visual rendering and acoustic properties.<SEP>Material Categories is a set of 20 surface texture classifications, including wood and textile, determined by object surface area in HoME.

AI Community
The collective global network of researchers and developers working on algorithmic advances, benchmarks, and artificial intelligence simulation environments.

Blind Navigation
A navigational task category where an agent learns to navigate an environment without visual observation, relying on non-visual modalities such as acoustics.

Planning
An artificial intelligence category focusing on deliberative sequence-of-action generation to achieve predefined goals within an environment.

3D Sandboxes
A category of interactive 3D simulation platforms designed to support the development, benchmarking, and training of learning algorithms.

Multimodal Learning
A category of machine learning tasks and algorithms that process and integrate multiple sensory data streams, such as audio, vision, and language.

Embodied Learning
A paradigm of artificial intelligence where virtual agents learn through physical or simulated interaction within realistic spatial environments.

Room Types
A categorical classification of indoor functional spaces, representing 24 distinct room styles found within domestic house datasets.

Color Categories
A semantic category system discretizing object textures into basic, intermediate, and detailed color classifications.

Size Categories
A categorical distribution classifying objects into discrete scales such as small, medium, or large based on 3D mesh volume.<SEP>Size Categories is a qualitative categorization classifying objects into small, medium, or large based on mesh volume histograms.

Simulation-to-Real Transfer
A category of machine learning methods focused on adapting models trained within virtual simulators to real-world applications.

MILA
MILA is an artificial intelligence research institute that provided a collaborative research environment for the HoME project.

CIFAR
CIFAR (Canadian Institute for Advanced Research) is a research organization that provided funding and support for the research.

CHISTERA IGLU
CHISTERA IGLU is a research funding programme/consortium that supported the research project.

Calcul Québec
Calcul Québec is a high-performance computing organization that provided computational resources for the research.

Compute Canada
Compute Canada is an organization providing advanced research computing infrastructure and support for the project.

Acronymcreator.net
Acronymcreator.net is an online service credited for generating the HoME acronym.

Nord-Pas de Calais
Nord-Pas de Calais is a region in France associated with the CPER/FEDER research project funding.

Slavic Languages
A branch of Indo-European languages including Polish and Czech, characterized in the study by high morphological generalization and smaller nominal paradigms.<SEP>A genealogical language family including Polish, Czech, Russian, Slovak, and Ukrainian, examined for morphological mapping and bilingual lexicon induction.<SEP>A major European language family containing Polish and Czech, analyzed through morphologically complete dictionaries in the study.<SEP>Slavic Languages is a linguistic group analyzed in the bilingual lexicon induction experiments to evaluate performance on highly inflectional systems.<SEP>Slavic languages are a branch of Indo-European languages sharing common ancestry, demonstrating linguistic relatedness.<SEP>The Slavic language family consists of genetically-related languages including Polish, Czech, Russian, Slovak, and Ukrainian, selected for evaluating morphological generalization in BLI models.

Indo-Aryan Languages
A branch of the Indo-European language family represented in the study by languages such as Hindi, Bengali, Punjabi, and Urdu.<SEP>Indo-Aryan languages are a language family sharing common ancestry, exemplifying languages with high lexical and structural similarities.

Indian Subcontinent
The Indian subcontinent is a geographic region identified as a linguistic area where prolonged language contact led to convergence of linguistic properties.

Balkan
The Balkan is a geographic region forming a linguistic area characterized by language contact and convergence.

South-East Asia
South-East Asia is a geographic region featuring prominent cultural and communication ties among speakers of related languages.

FEDER
FEDER (European Regional Development Fund) is a European institutional funding body that supported advanced data science and technology research.

CPER
CPER (Contrat de Plan État-Région) is an institutional planning and funding framework in France that supported the research through the Nord-Pas de Calais program.

Standard Average European
Standard Average European is a recognized linguistic area in Europe where sustained contact resulted in convergent linguistic and structural features across multiple languages.

Object Semantic Categories
Object Semantic Categories are the 187 fine-grained object classes derived from SUNCG (such as bathtub, wall, armchair, accordion, and xbox) used for semantic scene representation in HoME.

Related Languages
A linguistic classification of languages sharing high lexical similarity, cognates, and lateral borrowings but often lacking parallel training corpora.<SEP>Related Languages is a linguistic classification of languages that exhibit lexical and structural similarities due to shared genetic ancestry or prolonged contact.

Writing Systems
Writing Systems are graphical systems for representing verbal communication, categorized into vowel-based orthographies and non-vowel systems.

Lingua Franca
Lingua Franca is a category representing bridge languages adopted for common communication between speakers of different native tongues, exemplified by English.

Kunchukuttan
A researcher who described a method for mapping characters across Indic scripts, which was implemented in the Indic NLP Library.<SEP>A researcher who proposed orthographic syllables as a linguistically-motivated variable-length unit for machine translation between related languages.<SEP>Kunchukuttan is a researcher cited for demonstrating that orthographic syllable-level translation models are robust against domain changes.

Orthographic Syllables
A linguistic unit representation previously used in machine translation experiments, compared directly against Byte Pair Encoding.<SEP>A linguistically motivated variable-length subword unit approximating a syllable, used as a benchmark unit in machine translation.<SEP>A rule-based linguistic subword translation unit consisting of consonant-vowel sequences.<SEP>A subword representation unit based on orthographic syllabification rules, compared against Byte Pair Encoding across different writing systems.<SEP>Orthographic Syllables (OS) are subword translation units whose effectiveness is limited to writing systems that explicitly represent vowels.

Subword Units
Basic units of translation below the word level, including morphemes, syllables, character n-grams, and BPE units, designed to exploit lexical similarity.

Transliteration
A technique of converting source language words into target language scripts, used for handling named entities and untranslated words.

Hindi
An Indo-Aryan language examined in translation experiments, sharing high lexical similarity with Urdu.<SEP>An Indo-Aryan language used as an example of lexical similarity in cognate and shared word forms with related languages like Marathi.<SEP>Hindi is an Indo-Aryan language examined in cross-lingual contact and translation pairs with Malayalam.

Marathi
An Indo-Aryan language exhibiting lexical similarity and shared cognates with Hindi.<SEP>Marathi is an Indo-Aryan language evaluated in translation pairs with Konkani.

Parallel Corpora
Text datasets containing aligned source and target language translations, noted as being scarce for most related languages.

Lexical Similarity
A linguistic metric assessing the degree of shared vocabulary and cognates between source and target language pairs.<SEP>An evaluation category reflecting surface-level word and token overlap between model predictions and gold standard references.<SEP>The linguistic property whereby related languages share words with similar orthographic or phonetic forms and meanings.

Cognates
Words in related languages that share a common origin and similar form and meaning, critical for subword-level machine translation.

Character N-gram
A subword unit choice based on fixed-length character sequences, which suffers from data sparsity when applied at higher orders.

Wordpieces
A data-driven subword segmentation unit proposed for neural machine translation architectures.

Huffman Encoding
A data compression method whose principles have been applied to derive subword units for neural machine translation.

Bulgarian-Macedonian
A pair of closely related Slavic languages previously studied in character-level statistical machine translation.

Indonesian-Malay
A pair of closely related Austronesian languages previously evaluated using character-level translation models.

Spanish-Catalan
A pair of closely related Romance languages evaluated in character-level statistical machine translation research.

Character-Level SMT
A statistical machine translation approach using individual characters as basic translation units.

Indo-Aryan
A subgroup of the Indo-European language family examined in the translation experiments.

Slavic
A subgroup of the Indo-European language family examined in the translation experiments.

Germanic
A subgroup of the Indo-European language family examined in the translation experiments.

Altaic
A language family grouping used in the study to denote the relationship between Japanese and Korean.

Japanese
A language evaluated in the translation experiments, noted for lexical and grammatical similarities with Korean.<SEP>Japanese is a language employing the logographic Kanji script, studied in translation tasks with Korean.

Korean
A language evaluated in the translation experiments, noted for lexical and grammatical similarities with Japanese.<SEP>Korean is a language utilizing the syllabic Hangul script, examined in machine translation alongside Japanese.<SEP>Korean is a natural language for which a structured annotation scheme and lexicon ordering were established in the described dataset.<SEP>The Korean linguistic environment and agglutinative language in which diverse argument expressions, phrases, and morphological tokenization were performed.

Malayalam
A language examined in translation experiments and compared with Hindi despite belonging to a different language family.<SEP>Malayalam is a morphologically rich Dravidian language evaluated in translation experiments with Hindi, Telugu, and Tamil.

Macedonian
A Slavic language exhibiting high lexical similarity with Bulgarian.

Bulgarian
A Slavic language exhibiting high lexical similarity with Macedonian.

Phrase-Based Statistical Machine Translation
A statistical machine translation paradigm (PBSMT) trained at subword, morpheme, and orthographic syllable levels.<SEP>A subfield of statistical machine translation that models translations of word sequences rather than single words, evaluated as a baseline system in the study.<SEP>Phrase-Based Statistical Machine Translation is a translation framework combined with unsupervised word segmentation in previous Southern African language studies.

Character N-grams
Variable or fixed-length character sequences compared against BPE and orthographic syllables in machine translation context.

Morpheme
A minimal linguistic unit used as a comparison unit and translation segmentation level in PBSMT models.

Alphabetic Writing System
A category of writing systems where vowels and consonants are represented by distinct letters.<SEP>A type of writing system that explicitly represents vowels, suitable for rule-based orthographic syllabification.

Abugida Writing System
A category of writing systems where consonant-vowel sequences are written as a unit, and vowels are represented.<SEP>A segmental writing system representing vowels, applicable for orthographic syllabification.

Abjad Writing System
A category of writing systems where vowels are largely omitted or optional, as observed in scripts like Urdu.<SEP>A writing system where the representation of vowels is optional, exemplified by scripts like Urdu.

Logographic Writing System
A category of writing systems that represent words or morphemes rather than individual phonetic sounds, lacking explicit vowel representations.<SEP>A type of writing system in which characters do not represent vowels directly.

Longest Common Subsequence Ratio
A metric (LCSR) computed at character level across parallel training sentences to quantify lexical similarity between language pairs.

Indian Language Corpora Initiative
The Indian Language Corpora Initiative (ILCI) is a multilingual initiative that developed parallel corpora for Indian languages, covering Indo-Aryan and Dravidian language families.

Dravidian Languages
A major language family spoken predominantly in South Asia, including morphologically rich languages such as Malayalam, Tamil, and Telugu.

Syllabic Writing System
A category of writing systems in which each symbol represents a syllable, exemplified by the Korean Hangul system where vowels are implicitly embedded in character blocks.

Korean Hangul
A syllabic writing system used for the Korean language in which consonant and vowel elements are combined into syllabic blocks.

Indic Scripts
A family of writing systems used across the Indian subcontinent that share structural characteristics and can be mapped across one another.<SEP>Indic scripts are abugida writing systems that permit one-to-one character mappings for joint bilingual BPE models.

Slavic Script
A script category encompassing writing systems used for Slavic languages, targeted with custom syllabification rules.

Phrase-Based SMT
Phrase-based Statistical Machine Translation (SMT), a translation framework trained using the Moses system to evaluate subword representations.

Moses System
An open-source statistical machine translation system used to train phrase-based SMT models.

Indic NLP Library
A natural language processing software toolkit providing morphological segmentation models, orthographic syllabification rules, and Brahmi-derived script mapping for Indian languages.

OPUS
An open-source collection of parallel corpora from which data such as the OpenSubtitles2016 dataset was retrieved.

Batch MIRA
A margin-infused relaxed algorithm used for parameter tuning in phrase-based statistical machine translation.

LeBLEU
An evaluation metric variant of BLEU that uses edit-distance based soft-matching of words, particularly suited for morphologically rich languages.<SEP>LeBLEU is an evaluation metric reflecting translation quality trends consistent with BLEU scores.

Juman
A morphological analysis and tokenization tool used for processing Japanese text.

Mecab
A morphological analysis tool used for morpheme-level tokenization of Korean text.<SEP>An open-source text segmentation and morphological analysis tool applied to Korean tokenization.

Abjad Writing Systems
Abjad writing systems, such as Arabic and extended Arabic for Urdu, represent consonants and do not consistently represent vowels.

Logographic Writing Systems
Logographic writing systems represent words or morphemes with symbols, exemplified by Japanese Kanji and Chinese.

Syllabic Writing Systems
Syllabic writing systems represent syllables rather than individual vowels and consonants, exemplified by Korean Hangul.

Abugida Writing Systems
Abugida writing systems represent consonant-vowel combinations and fall into the category of scripts that explicitly represent vowels.

Agriculture Domain
A specialized translation domain evaluated in experiments to assess model performance under domain-specific conditions.<SEP>The agriculture domain is a test subject domain consisting of 1,000 sentences used to evaluate the cross-domain robustness of translation models.

Tourism And Health Domains
Tourism and health domains are the training domains utilized for evaluating cross-domain translation performance on unrelated test sets.

Tamil
Tamil is a Dravidian language tested in machine translation experiments utilizing BPE and OS units.

Telugu
Telugu is a Dravidian language evaluated in translation experiments involving Malayalam and subword representation units.

Chinese
Chinese is a language that uses a logographic writing system where vowels are not explicitly represented.

Arabic
Arabic is a language employing an abjad writing system that does not consistently represent vowels.

Hebrew
Hebrew is a language that employs an abjad writing system.

Syriac
Syriac is a language that uses an abjad writing system.

Konkani
Konkani is an Indo-Aryan language evaluated in machine translation experiments alongside Marathi.

Alphabetic Writing Systems
Alphabetic writing systems are scripts that explicitly represent both consonants and vowels, compatible with orthographic syllables.

Word-Level Representation
Word-level representation is a baseline machine translation unit that suffers from data sparsity compared to subword units.

Morpheme-Level Representation
Morpheme-level representation is a linguistic subword unit evaluated against BPE in translation tasks.

Department of Electronics & Information Technology
A department of the Government of India that provided institutional and funding support for the research.

data.entity_name: Technology Development for Indian Languages Programme
data.content:
Technology Development for Indian Languages Programme
A government initiative under the Government of India that supported research in natural language processing and machine translation.

Indian Languages
A collection of related languages spanning diverse families and writing systems used as experimental testbeds for translation units.

Multimodal Attribute Extraction
A proposed information extraction task aimed at extracting entity attributes from mixed-media inputs such as text, images, video, and audio.

Govt. of India
The central government of India, overseeing ministries and technological development initiatives including TDIL and DeitY.

Word-Level Representations
Translation modeling units based on whole words, suffering from data sparsity when limited parallel corpora are available.

Morpheme-Level Representations
Translation units based on morphological segments of words, which show low correlation with lexical similarity.

Pivot Based MT
A machine translation methodology utilizing intermediate pivot languages to facilitate translation between related languages.

Domain Adaptation
A transfer learning technique used in machine translation to adapt models across different subject areas and data distributions.

ITRANS
An Indian language transliteration scheme used to encode Indic scripts into standard ASCII characters.

Weakly Supervised Learning
A machine learning paradigm utilizing partially labeled, noisy, or heuristic supervision, applied to train multimodal attribute extractors.

Mixed-Media Data
Unstructured and semi-structured contextual information comprising combinations of text, images, video, and audio.

Diffbot
Diffbot is a technology company whose Product API is utilized to automatically extract attribute-value pairs from structured web data to build knowledge bases.<SEP>Diffbot is a technology company whose Product API was used to collect commercial product items from e-commerce sites for the Multimodal Attribute Extraction dataset.<SEP>Diffbot is a technology company whose Product API was used to extract mixed-media product data across e-commerce platforms for research.

Mechanical Turk
Mechanical Turk is a crowdsourcing platform and service used by the researchers to conduct human evaluation on attribute detection across modalities.<SEP>Mechanical Turk is a crowdsourcing platform used to conduct human evaluation studies to assess the difficulty of the multimodal attribute extraction task.

Electronic Products
Electronic Products is a commercial merchandise category included in the Multimodal Attribute Extraction dataset.<SEP>Electronic Products is a product category represented within the Multimodal Attribute Extraction dataset.

Jewelry
Jewelry is a merchandise category included in the commercial items collected for the Multimodal Attribute Extraction dataset.<SEP>Jewelry is an e-commerce product category featured among the items in the Multimodal Attribute Extraction dataset.

Clothing
Clothing is an apparel merchandise category represented within the Multimodal Attribute Extraction dataset.<SEP>Clothing is an apparel product category encompassed within the multimodal e-commerce dataset.

Vehicles
Vehicles is a high-value commercial product category present in the dataset.<SEP>Vehicles is a product category covered in the diverse collection of items in the dataset.

Real Estate
Real Estate is a commercial item category featured within the multimodal product dataset.<SEP>Real Estate is a commercial listing category included in the diverse Multimodal Attribute Extraction dataset.

Imagenet
ImageNet is a benchmark computer vision dataset and resource category referenced for revolutionizing object recognition.

Unstructured Text Documents
Unstructured Text Documents represents a category of data sources including job postings, scientific papers, news articles, and emails traditionally utilized in information extraction.

Semi-Structured Web Pages
Semi-Structured Web Pages is a multimodal data type category on the web that contains varied knowledge outside strict tabular schemas.

Attribute Extraction
A machine learning task and research area focused on identifying and extracting attribute-value pairs from unstructured or semi-structured data, extended to multimodal settings involving text and images.

Multimodal Machine Learning
A domain of machine learning research involving models and architectures that process, combine, and reason across multiple modalities of information such as images, text, and metadata.<SEP>A subfield of artificial intelligence that involves unifying, processing, and learning from multiple modalities of information, such as visual and textual data.

Object Recognition
A core computer vision task focused on identifying and classifying objects present within visual images.

Diff
An organization or automated web-data extraction platform used to extract structured attribute-value pairs from product pages to build knowledge bases.

Gated Multimodal Unit
An advanced neural fusion mechanism designed to selectively combine multimodal inputs, such as visual and textual representations, through gating.

Naïve Bayes
A family of probabilistic classifiers based on Bayes' theorem, applied to retail product attribute extraction using seed data.

Hidden Markov Model
A statistical Markov model with unobserved states, utilized in sequence labeling approaches for extracting product attributes.

Maximum Entropy Model
A log-linear probabilistic classification model used in statistical machine learning for sequence tagging and attribute extraction.

Crowdsourcing
A distributed sourcing model involving human workers used to manually verify, filter, and label attribute-value pairs to reduce noise.<SEP>Crowdsourcing is a data collection and annotation methodology that enlists groups of online participants to label data and generate evaluation sets.

Semi-Supervised Learning
A machine learning paradigm that combines a small amount of labeled data with a large amount of unlabeled data, often employing bootstrapping in attribute extraction.

Multimodal Information Extraction
A subfield of artificial intelligence and data mining focused on extracting structured knowledge, such as product attributes, from multiple modes of data including text and images.

E-Commerce
The domain of online commercial trade, serving as the source environment from which multimodal product descriptions, images, and attribute datasets are gathered.

Fake News
Fabricated or misleading information disseminated across online social networks and offline communities, negatively influencing culture and political discourse.<SEP>Fake News is a overarching category of false, deceptive, or misleading information appearing in text, image, or multimodal formats.

Fake News Detection
A research area in machine learning and data science dedicated to building automated systems and classification benchmarks to detect misinformation.<SEP>Fake News Detection is a research domain and task category focused on developing computational models to identify false, misleading, and fabricated news content.

Misinformation
Misinformation refers to false or misleading information spread across digitized communication networks, driving political polarization and social disruption.

Fact-Checking
Fact-checking is the verification process of investigating claims and news stories, often lacking or inadequate in standard social media environments.

Culture
Culture represents social institutions and shared human behaviors, noted as being adversely impacted by the proliferation of fake news.

Celebrity
Celebrity is a domain of popular culture and public figures that frequently forms the subject matter of fake news datasets and stories.

Knowledge Base Construction
Knowledge Base Construction is the machine learning and data extraction process of building structured repositories of information from unstructured and multimodal web data.

Multimodal Reasoning
Multimodal reasoning is an artificial intelligence research discipline focused on drawing joint inferences across multiple diverse modes such as vision, text, and structure.

Pushshift.io
Pushshift.io is a service and API provider used to collect historical submission and comment data from Reddit.

True
True is a classification category representing content that is accurate and in accordance with real-world facts.

Satire/Parody
Satire/Parody is a category of content that presents contemporary information with a satirical or humorous tone, making it false.

Misleading Content
Misleading Content is a category representing information intentionally manipulated to deceive or mislead an audience.<SEP>Misleading Content is a classification category applied to certain online submissions whose text or captions mislead the audience.

Imposter Content
Imposter Content is a category characterized by bot-generated or impersonated material, such as posts from automated simulator accounts.

False Connection
False Connection is a classification category in the fake news dataset wherein submission images do not accurately support or correlate with their accompanying text descriptions.<SEP>False Connection is a multimodal category where images or media do not accurately correspond to or support their text descriptions.

The Onion
The Onion is a prominent satirical digital media and news organization whose content and style are represented in satirical submissions.

Waterford Whispers News
Waterford Whispers News is a satirical news website and media outlet whose content forms part of the satire subreddits.

BuzzFeed News
BuzzFeed News is a digital news organization referenced in relation to image and news verification datasets (BUZZFEEDNEWS, BUZZFACE).

Celebrity Gossip
Celebrity Gossip is a specialized topic category commonly appearing in domain-specific fake news data collections.

2-Way Classification
2-Way Classification is a binary classification framework categorizing submissions simply as fake or true.

3-Way Classification
3-Way Classification is a categorical scheme dividing content into completely true, fake news with true text, and fake news with false text.

5-Way Classification
5-Way Classification is a fine-grained categorization framework that groups content into true and four distinct fake news categories.

Fake News With True Text
Fake News with True Text is a category within the 3-way classification schema denoting misleading samples where the textual component is factually true in the real world.

Fake News With False Text
Fake News with False Text is a category within the 3-way classification schema indicating fake news items containing false textual content.

Completely True
Completely True is a category in the 3-way classification framework designating verified, fully accurate news submissions.

Non-Canonical Directives
A category of conversational utterances, questions, or commands that deviate from standard syntactic forms, complicating automated intent extraction.<SEP>Non-Canonical Directives is a linguistic and conversational category of indirect or non-standard user commands and requests that modern dialogue systems must interpret.<SEP>Non-canonical directives are speech acts that convey requests or commands in indirect or non-standard linguistic forms.

Misleadingthumbnails
Misleadingthumbnails is a Reddit community and content category featuring images whose thumbnails appear to depict something completely different from the actual full image.

Confusing_perspective
Confusing_perspective is a Reddit community and content category dedicated to images displaying confusing optical perspectives or misleading angles.

Pareidolia
Pareidolia is a Reddit community and content category containing images of everyday objects and patterns perceived as faces or recognizable figures.

Fakehistoryporn
Fakehistoryporn is a Reddit community and content category that features humorous or satirical historical posts pairing real or unrelated photos with fake historical captions.

Savedyouaclick
Savedyouaclick is a Reddit community and content category dedicated to debunking and revealing the true contents behind clickbait headlines.

PsBattle
PsBattle (Photoshop Battles) is a Reddit community and content category where users submit images to be humorously or creatively edited by other users.

Subsimulatorgpt2
Subsimulatorgpt2 is an automated Reddit community and content category composed of posts generated by GPT-2 artificial intelligence models simulating various subreddits.

Online Safety Benchmark Award
The Online Safety Benchmark Award is a funding recognition and award program sponsored by Facebook to support research in online safety and content moderation.

Multimodal Classification
Multimodal Classification is a machine learning classification category where predictions are made by jointly learning from multiple input types, such as text and images.

Intent Classification
A classification task in natural language processing aimed at identifying the core objective or intention behind user utterances.

Slot-Filling
A standard natural language understanding task involving the extraction of specific parameters and arguments from user input.

Speech Act
A linguistic and pragmatic category representing the communicative function and intent of an utterance, structured into a multi-class taxonomy on Twitter.<SEP>A pragmatic linguistic category representing the intended communicative action of an utterance, critical for accurate argument inference in the evaluated NLP tasks.<SEP>A pragmatic linguistic concept where utterances perform actions or express conversational intents such as requests, commands, or questions.<SEP>Linguistic pragmatic categories defining utterance types whose correct identification directly affects intent argument inference.<SEP>Speech acts are a linguistic concept framing speech as action, adapted into a multi-class taxonomy for classifying tweets.

Korean Language
A natural language highlighted as the primary language of the corpus and study, noted for real-world non-canonical utterances.<SEP>An agglutinative, head-final language characterized by scrambling, investigated as a low-resource linguistic setting for intent comprehension.

Question Set
A structured semantic representation used to capture the intent arguments of questions in dialog systems.

To-Do-List
A structured semantic representation used to capture the intent arguments of commands and action directives in dialog systems.

Amazon Echo
A brand of smart speaker and conversational agent developed by Amazon that processes user voice commands and questions.

Google Home
A line of voice-enabled smart speakers and virtual assistant devices developed by Google for household interaction.

Poppa Joe
A person addressed in a conversational declarative question example ('poppa joe you want me to go now') used to illustrate machine interpretation difficulties.

Entity Recognition
A natural language processing technique focused on identifying and classifying named entities within unstructured text.

Formal Semantics
A linguistic and mathematical discipline providing theoretical foundations for understanding sentence meaning and utterance representations.

Task-Oriented Systems
Conversational dialogue systems specifically designed to identify intents and execute predefined actions or transactions.

Non-Task-Oriented Dialogues
Open-ended conversational dialogues that do not assume predefined action domains and rely on natural language argument representations.

Directive Utterances
A functional category of speech acts in natural language processing that includes questions and commands, requiring intent extraction and comprehension.

Questions
A subcategory of directive utterances encompassing interrogatives such as yes/no, alternative, and wh- questions, as well as embedded and declarative questions.<SEP>Questions are an utterance category subclassified into yes/no, alternative, and wh- questions for argument extraction.

Commands
A subcategory of directive utterances encompassing imperatives, requests, prohibitions, and conditional directives.<SEP>Commands are an utterance category treated analogously to to-do lists and rewritten into actionable clauses.

SQL Generation
A structured query language generation task in computational linguistics related to semantic parsing and code generation from natural language.

Berant
A researcher whose semantic parsing methodology serves as a reference for re-using extracted natural language terms as building blocks.

Cho
A researcher cited (Cho et al., 2018b) for work establishing a structured annotation scheme for the Korean language.<SEP>A researcher whose speech corpus work is referenced as part of the corpus annotation process.<SEP>Cho is a researcher and lead author of a 2018 study detailing a structured annotation scheme for the Korean language.<SEP>Cho is a researcher referenced in connection with the construction of a Korean single utterance corpus for identifying directives.

Powell
An individual referenced within an illustrative example of an embedded question.

Carney
An individual referenced alongside Powell within an illustrative example of an embedded question.

Robotics Domain
An application domain in artificial intelligence where command extraction has historically been investigated.

Seq2seq Architecture
A sequence-to-sequence neural network model family commonly employed in semantic parsing, SQL generation, and machine translation tasks.

Non-directive Utterances
A classification of speech acts encompassing fragments and declarative statements, contrasted with questions and commands.

Smart Speaker Commands
Real-world conversational spoken inputs given to smart home devices, which frequently exhibit non-canonical syntactic structures.

Imperatives
A grammatical structure featuring covert subjects or modal auxiliaries used primarily to express commands and requests.

Interrogatives
A grammatical class of sentences characterized by features such as do-support, wh-movement, or embedded predicates, used to express questions.

Declarative Questions
A subcategory of questions that have the syntactic structure of a declarative sentence but function pragmatically as questions.

Conditionalized Imperatives
Imperative constructions combined with conditional clauses, categorized as commands based on whether the condition maintains or negates the required action.

Intent Arguments
Extracted semantic units or parameters representing the underlying communicative goal of non-canonical directive utterances.<SEP>Intent arguments are semantic components extracted from utterances to represent the underlying directive or conversational intent.

Hawaii
Hawaii is an island location referenced in an example alternative question comparing temperatures.

Guam
Guam is an island territory referenced in an example alternative question comparing temperatures.

Treadstone
Treadstone is an organization or program referenced within an example wh- question utterance.

Yes/No Questions
A question category whose candidate answers are constrained to yes or no and extracted using an if-clause.

Alternative Questions
A category of utterance type included in the corpus construction alongside wh-questions.<SEP>A question category structured around options, annotated using whether-or clauses and candidate answer lists.

Wh- Questions
A question category that seeks specific information, extracted beginning with lexicons corresponding to wh- particles.

Prohibitions
A negative directive command category representing prohibited actions, rewritten using 'not to' structures.

Coreference
A linguistic phenomenon in conversational utterances involving pronouns and anaphora that require resolution and standardization during annotation.

Spatial Dependencies
Contextual spatial references, such as specific locations or demonstratives like 'there', that must be captured in intent arguments.

Temporal Dependencies
Contextual temporal references, such as timing indicators like 'tomorrow' or 'then', requiring preservation in intent extraction.

Subjective Factors
Elements reflecting current thoughts or personal views of dialog participants within non-task-oriented conversations.

Speaker
The conversational participant producing an utterance, systematically substituted for first-person pronouns during annotation.

Addressee
The conversational participant receiving an utterance, systematically substituted for second-person pronouns during annotation.

Three Native Speakers
A group of annotators who performed the tagging of questions and commands to evaluate inter-annotator agreement.

Corpus Tagging Process
The annotation and labeling effort conducted by native speakers to tag directives and non-directives, achieving an IAA score of 0.85.

Directive Utterance
A speech act category encompassing questions and commands designed to convey an intention or prompt an action from the addressee.

Strong Requirement
A linguistic utterance category introduced in corpus annotation describing the co-existence of a prohibitive expression and a canonical requirement.

Prohibition
A speech act category representing an injunction, restriction, or disallowance expressed in an utterance.<SEP>An utterance category characterized by expressions that forbid or discourage an action.

Alternative Question
A question category targeted during corpus augmentation to balance utterance types for automated processing.

Wh-Question
A question utterance category requiring the abstraction of wh-related concepts to extract intent arguments.

Speaker/Addressee Classification
A five-category coreference classification scheme comprising only the speaker, only the addressee, both, none, and unknown.

Corpus Annotation
The process of tagging directives, questions, and commands, and establishing speaker and addressee coreference notations.

Corpus Augmentation
The process of expanding dataset size and balancing utterance types via human-aided sentence rewriting across defined topics.

Question
A functional utterance category tagged during corpus development to identify interrogative speech acts requiring information or confirmation.<SEP>A speech act category signifying an inquiry or information request, identified as the third most frequent speech act in entity and event topics.

Command
A speech act category representing imperative utterances and directives requesting specific actions.

Head-Final Language
A linguistic classification describing languages, such as Korean, where the syntactic head typically occurs at the end of a phrase.<SEP>A linguistic typology category classifying languages such as Korean where syntactically governing elements appear at the end of phrases or clauses, impacting tail prediction in autoregressive models.

Head-First Language
A linguistic typological category where syntactic heads precede their complements, contrasted with head-final languages.

Mail
A functional domain topic used in generating intent argument sentences for the corpus at a defined ratio.<SEP>A topic domain category utilized in constructing the smart agent corpus.

Schedule
A calendar and time management topic category used for balancing utterances in corpus construction.<SEP>A functional topic category used for calendar and agenda-related intent arguments.

House Control
A smart home device management topic category used to structure dataset sentences for smart agent applications.<SEP>A topic category encompassing smart home automation directives and queries.

Weather
A topic domain category used for weather-related intent arguments and utterance creation.<SEP>An environmental domain category used as a topical theme in corpus augmentation sentences.

Free Topics
An open-domain topic category covering diverse subjects, such as algebra concepts, used to diversify the corpus.<SEP>An open-ended topical category making up a significant portion of sentences generated during dataset augmentation.

Native Speakers
A group of three native Korean speakers who conducted the tagging process for questions and commands.

Tagging Of Questions And Commands
An annotation activity performed by three native speakers that achieved an inter-annotator agreement score of kappa 0.85.

Human-Aided Sentence Rewriting
A text expansion activity wherein human annotators rewrite sentences from intent arguments to augment and balance the corpus.

Wh-Questions
A category of utterance type focused on information-seeking questions, constructed in the dataset using nominalized intent arguments without direct wh-particles.

BERT-Based Scoring System
An evaluation metric category utilizing pre-trained language models to evaluate semantic similarity in text generation.

Participants
Human subjects requested by researchers to compose ten diverse utterances per phrase during the paraphrasing process.

Smart Agents
Automated conversational systems whose advancement is the primary objective of constructing the corpus.

Seq2seq
Sequence-to-sequence framework employed to infer intent arguments directly from input sentences.

KoNLPy
A Python natural language processing library providing a wrapper to access Mecab for tokenization.

Paraphrasing
A monolingual translation process in which single arguments are converted into multiple diverse surface utterances.

Experiments
Empirical evaluations conducted to measure solving times, scalability, and text quality between ILP models and their approximations.<SEP>The sequence of automated testing procedures assessing model formats, seq2seq architectures, and quantitative evaluation metrics.

Requirement
A speech act category indicating an instruction, mandate, or necessary action expressed within an utterance.

Wh- Question
A category of interrogative sentences evaluated as complex input utterances for speech act and argument inference.

RNN Seq2seq with Attention
A recurrent sequence-to-sequence neural model category evaluated in the experiments, which suffered from word repetition collapse during inference.

Department Store Sale Event
A commercial sale event referenced in an evaluated Korean test sentence where a person is instructed to wait in advance.

PhD Graduation
An academic milestone event mentioned as a point of comparison in an evaluated test sentence.

BERTScore
A metric category for automatic semantic similarity evaluation based on pre-trained BERT embeddings, used to measure the alignment between model outputs and gold standard data.

ROUGE-1
An evaluation metric category measuring character-level and lexical overlap against reference text, preventing bias from formatting differences.

Pre-Trained Language Models
A category of neural models trained on broad corpora that encode general linguistic common sense, utilized in semantic similarity scoring.

Out-of-Vocabulary Terms
A linguistic and computational category designating words absent from the model's training vocabulary, causing inference decoding confusion.

Loanword
A linguistic category of words borrowed from foreign languages, such as 'sale' in Korean, that often appear as out-of-vocabulary terms in test sets.

Auto-Regressive Inference
A sequence generation category in neural models where subsequent token prediction is conditioned on prior tokens, presenting challenges for clause-tail stability.

Department Store
A commercial establishment referenced in utterance (6) where shoppers are directed to arrive early.

Onsen
A hot spring bath location referenced in test sentence (7) where swimming is specified as prohibited.

Swimming in an Onsen
An activity referenced in test sentence (7) designated under a prohibition speech act.

Wedding Preparation
A personal planning event referenced in utterance (8) compared against doctoral graduation in terms of hardship.

Interpark
Interpark is a South Korean e-commerce and ticketing company referenced in an example Korean utterance regarding spam mail and ticket blocking.

An organization involved in research and development projects supporting police science and technology.

South Korea, the nation whose government ministries provided research grants and whose language is the focus of the Natural Language Processing study.
