An advisor acknowledged for providing helpful advice on the research.

Portner
A cited researcher whose 2004 work on clause types and their properties was referenced in the study.

Korean Natural Language Processing
A domain of computational linguistics focused on developing natural language understanding and generation techniques for the Korean language.

Spoken Language Understanding
A dialogue system component responsible for parsing user utterances and performing slot-filling, often modeled jointly with dialogue state tracking.<SEP>A pipeline module in spoken dialogue systems that extracts user intents and slot-value pairs from user utterances.<SEP>A subfield of natural language processing and dialog systems that handles parsing and intent understanding of spoken user utterances.

data.entity_name: Projects for Research and Development of Police Science and Technology
data.content:
Projects for Research and Development of Police Science and Technology
A research grant program focused on advancing police science and technology under grant PA-J000001-2017-101.

Technology Innovation Program
A research program under project number 10076583 targeting the development of free-running speech recognition technologies for embedded robot systems.

Semantic Web Search
An application domain that utilizes structured semantics, summarization, and paraphrasing schemes to enhance web searching.

Androutsopoulos
Androutsopoulos is a researcher who studied the generation of natural language sentences in English and Greek from OWL ontologies.

WebNLG
WebNLG is a natural language generation challenge and benchmarking event that spurred research in generating text from Semantic Web data.

OWL
A formal ontology language standard based on description logics, RDF, and RDF Schema, used to specify Semantic Web ontologies.<SEP>OWL (Web Ontology Language) is a semantic web language used to represent ontologies and formal statements, such as those extracted from the Disease Ontology.<SEP>The Web Ontology Language format used to represent underlying ontology statements and facts for natural language generation.<SEP>Web Ontology Language (OWL) is the de-facto standard ontology representation language for authoring ontologies on the Semantic Web.<SEP>Web Ontology Language, a semantic web language used for authoring rich and complex ontologies and class expressions.<SEP>Web Ontology Language, a semantic web representation standard used to model complex classes, properties, and relationships in knowledge domains.

LD2NL
LD2NL is an open-source natural language generation framework designed to verbalize RDF, OWL, and SPARQL Semantic Web data into natural language.<SEP>The system or framework responsible for generating natural language verbalizations of Linked Data, SPARQL constructs, and OWL axioms.

SPARQL2NL
SPARQL2NL is an open-source framework and predecessor verbalization system that uses rules to convert SPARQL queries into natural language, upon which LD2NL builds.

SPARTIQULATION
SPARTIQULATION is an existing verbalization system that demonstrates the generation of natural language from SPARQL and RDF data for question answering and explanation.

Gatt
Gatt is a researcher who co-authored a comprehensive 2017 survey on Natural Language Generation.

Greek
Greek is a natural language targeted for sentence generation from OWL ontologies by Androutsopoulos.

Description Logic SROIQ(D)
SROIQ(D) is a formal description logic equivalent to the expressive foundation of OWL 2 ontologies, providing automated reasoning capabilities.

Albert Einstein
Albert Einstein is a historical figure referenced as an example individual in OWL assertional axioms regarding his birth place and birth date.<SEP>Albert Einstein is a renowned physicist used as a subject in example RDF triples and natural language verbalizations.<SEP>Albert Einstein is a renowned scientist referenced as an example individual born in Ulm in an RDF triple statement.<SEP>Albert Einstein is a renowned scientist whose birthplace is Ulm, place of death is Princeton, and who is known for general relativity; he serves as an example in RDF verbalization and subject grouping.

Ulm
Ulm is a city identified as the birth place of Albert Einstein in the RDF verbalization examples.<SEP>Ulm is a city identified as the birth place of Albert Einstein in the ontology example.<SEP>Ulm is a city identified as the birthplace of Albert Einstein.<SEP>Ulm is a city referenced as the birthplace of Albert Einstein in knowledge representation examples.

Spain
A European country whose Spanish language dataset showed low annotator agreement and high performance variability.<SEP>Spain is a country referenced in an example ontology class expression describing individuals working at a university located there.<SEP>Spain is referenced in connection with the Spanish language sentiment analysis dataset examined for sentiment class ordering.

Alice
Alice is an example individual person used to demonstrate individual representation and property assignment in OWL.

Reiter & Dale
Reiter & Dale are researchers who proposed the standard architecture model for natural language generation cited in the text.

Animal
Animal is an ontological class representing the set of all animals, used to demonstrate OWL classes and taxonomic subclass relationships.

Koala
Koala is an ontological class defined as a subclass of Animal in an example of OWL terminological axioms.

Person
A named entity category representing individual people, accounting for 457 annotations in the analyzed Turkish tweet dataset.<SEP>Person is an atomic class and semantic category in OWL ontologies, used in class expressions and subclass axioms.<SEP>Person is an ontological class representing individuals, used to illustrate lexicalization into natural language terms like 'people'.

Professor
Professor is an ontological category representing an academic occupation, used in the text to illustrate class expressions where professors work at a university.

University
University represents academic institutions where professors work and which can be geographically located in countries such as Spain.

Scientist
A profession and classification category applied to Albert Einstein in the ontology and triple examples.<SEP>Scientist is a professional category referenced in an example SPARQL query targeting individuals who were born in Ulm.<SEP>Scientist is an atomic class and category used to illustrate a terminological subclass axiom.<SEP>Scientist is an occupational category attributed to Albert Einstein in the triple verbalization example.

Reiter
Reiter is a computer scientist and researcher who, along with Dale, proposed the standard model for natural language generation.

Dale
Dale is a computer scientist and researcher who co-authored the standard natural language generation architecture cited in the LD2NL framework.

Terminological Axiom
Terminological axioms are a category of ontology statements that describe domain structures, class hierarchies, and relationships between classes.

Assertional Axiom
Assertional axioms are a category of ontology statements that assert concrete facts about individual entities, their class memberships, and properties.

Object Property
Object property is an ontological category representing binary relations between individuals, such as childOf.

Data Property
Data property is an ontological category that links an individual entity to a specific data value, such as birthDate.

Query Form
Query forms represent categories of SPARQL queries used to retrieve or construct RDF graphs, consisting of SELECT, CONSTRUCT, ASK, and DESCRIBE.

Nathan Rosen
Nathan Rosen is a physicist cited in an example RDF triple as being influenced by Albert Einstein.

William Shakespeare
William Shakespeare is a famous writer used as an example subject in RDF triple verbalization and sentence ordering.<SEP>William Shakespeare is an English writer who died on 23 April 1616, used as an example in RDF triple verbalization.

Princeton
Princeton is a location identified as the death place of Albert Einstein in the RDF verbalization examples.<SEP>Princeton is a location identified as the death place of Albert Einstein.

Writer
A profession and classification category applied to William Shakespeare.<SEP>Writer is an occupational category attributed to William Shakespeare in the triple verbalization example.

LD2NL Framework
LD2NL Framework is a natural language generation framework designed to transform RDF graphs and triples into natural language text.

RDF Graph
A graph-based data model representing semantic web data through subjects, predicates, objects, and literals.

Literal
A data value in an RDF graph consisting of a lexical form and a datatype IRI, optionally including a language tag.

Triple Realization
The process of transforming individual RDF triples into grammatical natural language sentences within the LD2NL framework.

Clustering And Ordering
A stage of transformation rules in natural language generation that organizes verbalized sentences by frequency and subject coherence before grouping.

Grouping
A transformation step following clustering and ordering designed to aggregate sentences and reduce redundant information.

Benjamin Franklin
Benjamin Franklin is a historical figure born in Boston, referenced in an example illustrating object grouping.

Leonard Nimoy
Leonard Nimoy is a figure born in Boston, referenced in an example illustrating object grouping.

Boston
Boston is a city cited in the text as an example of a topic-specific entity term excluded from general n-grams.<SEP>Boston is a city identified as the birthplace of both Benjamin Franklin and Leonard Nimoy.<SEP>Boston is a major American city referenced in relation to the Boston Marathon bombings and the Boston Red Sox.

Dalianishovy
Dalianishovy refers to researcher(s) cited for defining grouping as collecting and collapsing clauses with common elements.

General Relativity
A fundamental theory in physics for which Albert Einstein is known, referenced in the natural language generation example.

People
An ontological class or category representing human individuals, referenced in an example of OWL class expressions.

OWL Class
A category and conceptual element in OWL 2 ontologies representing an abstract group or collection of individuals.

Albert Einstein's Birth
The historical event of the birth of Albert Einstein, which took place in Ulm.

Albert Einstein's Death
The historical event of the death of Albert Einstein, which took place in Princeton.

William Shakespeare's Death
The historical event marking the death of writer William Shakespeare on 23 April 1616.

Benjamin Franklin's Birth
The historical event of Benjamin Franklin being born, which occurred in Boston.

Leonard Nimoy's Birth
The historical event of Leonard Nimoy being born, which occurred in Boston.

City
City is an atomic class and category in OWL ontologies used in complex class expressions.

Assertional Axioms
Assertional Axioms (ABox Axioms) are a category of OWL axioms that state facts about individuals, such as their types and property values.

Terminological Axioms
Terminological Axioms (TBox Axioms) are a category of OWL axioms that express relationships between conceptual classes, such as subclass relations.

Power
Power is a researcher cited in the text regarding findings that most terminological axioms in ontologies are subclass axioms.

OWL Class Expressions
OWL Class Expressions are a category of description logic constructs that define concepts or complex conditions in Web Ontology Language.

Subclass Axioms
Subclass Axioms are a category of terminological axioms asserting that all instances of a subclass belong to a superclass.

Atomic Classes
Atomic Classes are basic, named concept categories in ontologies that serve as the foundational building blocks for complex class expressions.

Existential Restrictions
Existential Restrictions are a category of OWL class expressions specifying that individuals must have at least one relationship to members of a given class.

SPARQL SELECT Query
SPARQL SELECT Query is a category of graph query consisting of a body section, an optional section, and a modifier section.

Domain Experts
A group of 66 evaluation participants with specialized knowledge who evaluated OWL axiom verbalizations and RDF resource summaries.<SEP>Subject-matter specialists with knowledge in semantic web formalisms who evaluated generated natural language sentences.

Non-Experts
A group of 20 volunteer evaluators without specialized domain knowledge who participated in evaluating fluency and instance identification.

OWL Axiom Verbalization Experiment
The first evaluation experiment in which domain experts rated the adequacy and fluency of verbalized OWL axioms from the Koala ontology.

RDF Resource Summaries Verbalization Experiment
The second evaluation experiment where volunteers evaluated the verbalization of triples describing DBpedia resources based on adequacy, fluency, and completeness.

Class Instance Identification Experiment
The third evaluation experiment where human raters were tasked with identifying class instances based on verbalized OWL class descriptions and resources.

Gardent
A researcher cited for establishing the evaluation measures of adequacy and fluency used in natural language generation assessment.

Koala Ontology
A well-known benchmark ontology formulated in OWL used in the experiments to evaluate axiom verbalization.

OWL Axioms
Formal logical statements in the Web Ontology Language that express semantic relationships and restrictions within an ontology.

RDF Resources
Entities and concepts represented in the Resource Description Framework that are subject to summarization and verbalization.

Triple Patterns
Core syntactic structures in SPARQL queries composed of subject, predicate, and object elements.

Stanford Dependencies
A grammatical dependency representation framework whose vocabulary is extended and used to formulate realization rules.

Variables
The set of variable identifiers used within SPARQL queries to represent unbound terms in graph patterns.

Properties
The set of semantic relations and predicates contained in target knowledge bases that link resources.

Literals
The set of concrete data values such as strings and numbers contained in target knowledge bases.

A German federal ministry (BMWI) that supported semantic web research through the RAKI project.

The German Federal Ministry of Education and Research, which supported research through the SOLIDE project.

African Languages
A broad category of diverse, low-resourced languages that lack extensive benchmarks, datasets, and machine translation attention.<SEP>A broad group of low-resourced indigenous languages in Africa facing challenges such as low discoverability, lack of benchmarks, and limited machine translation resources.<SEP>A group of over 2,000 diverse and predominantly low-resourced languages spoken across the African continent.

Formal knowledge representation languages, including RDF, OWL, and SPARQL, evaluated for natural language verbalization.

Project OPAL
A research project funded by the German Federal Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure (BMVI) under grant number 19F2028A.

A research initiative supported by the German Federal Ministry of Economics and Technology (BMWI) under grant number 01MD19012D.

Project SOLIDE
A research project funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) under grant number 13N14456.

Experiment I
An experimental evaluation measuring the adequacy and fluency ratings of semantic web verbalizations.

Experiment II
An experimental evaluation assessing the adequacy, fluency, and completeness of verbalized resource summaries.

Linguists
Non-domain experts specializing in language who evaluated the fluency and grammatical accuracy of verbalized sentences.

SWRL
Semantic Web Rule Language, an ontology rule language targeted for future verbalization work.

SHACL
Shapes Constraint Language, a standard language for validating graph-structured RDF data targeted for future verbalization support.

Afrikaans
A South African language evaluated in the neural machine translation experiments with a comparatively larger dataset.<SEP>Afrikaans is a South African language included in the Autshumato parallel datasets and evaluated with neural machine translation models.<SEP>Afrikaans is a non-agglutinative language evaluated in the translation study that attained reasonable translation performance despite having fewer parallel sentences.<SEP>An analytic West-Germanic language descended from Dutch settlers in South Africa, addressed in machine translation experiments.<SEP>An official South African language included in neural machine translation model training from English.

isiZulu
A Southern Bantu and Nguni language, being the second most spoken language in Southern Africa, recognized for high morphological complexity.<SEP>An indigenous South African language identified in the study as having very limited, lower-quality dataset resources.<SEP>An official South African language modeled in neural machine translation experiments.<SEP>IsiZulu is an agglutinative language evaluated in the neural machine translation study, exhibiting low BLEU scores due to high morphological complexity and small dataset size.<SEP>isiZulu is a South African target language evaluated in the translation experiments, noted for having low-quality parallel corpora and morphological complexity.

Northern Sotho
A Southern Bantu language closely related and mutually intelligible with Setswana, also referred to as N. Sotho.<SEP>An indigenous South African language (also referred to as N. Sotho) identified as having exceptionally small datasets in the study.<SEP>An official South African language evaluated in neural machine translation from English.<SEP>Northern Sotho (referred to as N. Sotho) is an agglutinative language evaluated in the neural machine translation experiments.

Setswana
A South African language with a comparatively larger dataset used in the neural machine translation ablation studies.<SEP>A Southern Bantu language closely related to Northern Sotho, targeted for machine translation models.<SEP>An African language analyzed as a target language in translation models and multi-head attention visualizations.<SEP>An official South African language used as a target translation language in neural machine translation experiments.<SEP>Setswana is a South African language included in the Autshumato project's parallel corpora and translation experiments.<SEP>Setswana is an agglutinative language evaluated in the translation experiments, which achieved higher translation performance due to a larger parallel dataset.

isiXhosa
An official South African language supported by Google Translate as of February 2019.<SEP>An official South African language supported by translation tools like Google Translate.

An official South African language currently supported by tools like Google Translate.<SEP>An official South African language supported by Google Translate as of February 2019.

data.entity_name: South African Centre for Digital Language Resources
data.content:
South African Centre for Digital Language Resources
The South African Centre for Digital Language Resources (SADiLaR) is an institute providing an open platform for technologies and digital resources for South African languages.<SEP>The South African Centre for Digital Language Resources is an organization that hosts and provides public downloads for the Autshumato parallel corpora on its website.

Southern Africa
Southern Africa is a geographic region encompassing countries and indigenous languages including isiZulu, Setswana, and Xitsonga.<SEP>Southern Africa is the geographic region encompassing several low-resource languages that lack extensive machine translation research.

Mozambique
Mozambique is a Southern African country identified as the origin of the Xitsonga language.

Google Translate
A machine translation service provided by Google that supports translations for two additional South African official languages.<SEP>Google Translate is an automated translation service developed by Google used to translate Tamil sentences into English for comparative evaluation.<SEP>Google Translate is an automated translation service offering translation models for several official South African languages.

Southern Bantu Languages
A branch of the Bantu language group characterized by agglutinative structure, rich noun class systems, subject-verb-object word order, and tone, including isiZulu, N. Sotho, Setswana, and Xitsonga.

Nguni Language Family
A linguistic subgroup of the Bantu languages to which isiZulu belongs, recognized for its morphological complexity.

Vatsonga People
An ethnic group originating in Mozambique whose language is Xitsonga.

Google Scholar
Google Scholar is an academic search engine and indexing tool used by researchers, cited as an example of indexing tools that often lack coverage of African conferences and journals.

West-Germanic Languages
A branch of the Germanic language family to which Afrikaans belongs.

Bantu Languages
A major group of African languages characterized by agglutinative morphology, rich noun class systems, subject-verb-object word order, and tone.

Dutch Settlers
Historical European colonizers in South Africa from whom the Afrikaans language descended.

Autshumato Project
The Autshumato project is an initiative aimed at providing data resources to support the development of open-source translation systems in South Africa.

Southern African Languages
Southern African Languages refers to the group of languages evaluated in the study, including Afrikaans, isiZulu, Northern Sotho, Setswana, and Xitsonga.

N. Sotho
N. Sotho (Northern Sotho) is an indigenous South African language evaluated in the English translation benchmark.

ConvS2S
A convolutional sequence-to-sequence neural network architecture evaluated for machine translation on South African languages and used in the ablation study.<SEP>A convolutional sequence-to-sequence neural network architecture evaluated on machine translation across target languages.<SEP>A convolutional sequence-to-sequence neural network model architecture category evaluated as a baseline translation model across multiple languages.<SEP>ConvS2S is a convolutional sequence-to-sequence neural network architecture modeled using Fairseq for baseline machine translation benchmarks.

Byte-Pair Encoding
Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) is a subword tokenisation method and category investigated through ablation studies to optimize rare word handling in translation models.<SEP>Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) is a subword tokenisation method applied to improve vocabulary handling and model performance in translation.

WordPiece
A subword tokenisation algorithm category used by the Transformer model with token counts aligned to optimal BPE settings.<SEP>WordPiece is a subtoken encoding algorithm similar to BPE used by Tensor2Tensor to prepare training data for Transformer models.

BPE Ablation Study
The BPE Ablation Study is an empirical investigation conducted to identify the optimal number of subword tokens for ConvS2S translation models.

WMT 2014
WMT 2014 is a machine translation benchmark event and shared task referenced for standard subword token counts in English-to-German and English-to-French translation.

Agglutinative Languages
Agglutinative languages are a morphological category of languages characterized by complex word formation through affixation, making them challenging for machine translation models with limited data.

Subword-nmt
A software tool and implementation utilized to perform subword segmentation and BPE ablation experiments.<SEP>A tokenisation utility and tool category used to conduct the ablation study on Byte-Pair Encoding token counts.

TensorFlow Research Cloud
A program by Google providing Cloud TPU resources that supported the computational research for this study.

Laura Martinus
A researcher whose GitHub repository hosts the code and datasets for the ukuxhumana project.

Jason Webster
An individual acknowledged for providing assistance with the Google Translate API.

Reinhard Cromhout
An individual acknowledged for assisting with back-translations for the research evaluation.

Guy Bosa
An individual acknowledged for assisting with back-translations for the research evaluation.

Mbongiseni Ncube
An individual acknowledged for assisting with back-translations for the research evaluation.

Seale Rapolai
An individual acknowledged for assisting with back-translations for the research evaluation.

Vongani Maluleke
An individual acknowledged for assisting with back-translations for the research evaluation.

Ukuxhumana
An open-source research project and GitHub repository hosting machine translation code and datasets for South African languages.

Meta-Learning
An advanced machine learning methodology proposed for future research to tackle low-resourced African language translation.

Zero-Shot Techniques
Machine translation methods requiring no direct parallel training data, identified as potential future work to cover all official South African languages.

Concept-to-Text Generation
A specialized branch of natural language generation that transforms structured knowledge representations, such as ontologies, into fluent text.<SEP>Concept-to-text generation is a specialized natural language generation task that converts structured ontological data or conceptual representations into coherent multi-sentence text.

Integer Linear Programming
A mathematical optimization framework (ILP) used in the extended model to globally optimize sentence planning, aggregation, and natural language generation.<SEP>A mathematical optimization framework used to jointly model content selection, lexicalization, and sentence aggregation for producing compact texts.<SEP>A mathematical optimization framework utilized to jointly optimize content selection, lexicalization, and sentence aggregation in text generation to produce compact texts.<SEP>A mathematical optimization technique (ILP) widely applied in natural language processing and generation tasks to jointly optimize decisions such as content selection, aggregation, ordering, and lexicalization.<SEP>Integer Linear Programming (ILP) is a mathematical optimization approach applied to jointly solve content selection, lexicalization, and sentence aggregation in natural language generation.<SEP>Integer Linear Programming (ILP) is a mathematical optimization framework used in this context to model fact selection and sentence aggregation under specific objective functions and constraints.

Pipeline Architecture
A pipeline architecture is a traditional software and NLG architectural paradigm where components execute sequentially in separate, greedy stages.<SEP>A traditional multi-stage system architecture for natural language generation that executes content selection, text planning, lexicalization, and realization sequentially.

Linked Data
A paradigm for publishing structured, interconnected data on the Web using Semantic Web standards.<SEP>Linked Data refers to a method of publishing structured data using semantic web technologies, RDF triples, and SPARQL queries.

Description Logics
A family of formal knowledge representation formalisms that provide the logical foundation for Semantic Web ontology languages like OWL.

RDF Schema
A semantic extension of RDF providing mechanisms for describing groups of related resources and classes.

Content Selection
A stage in natural language generation pipelines that chooses the logical facts or axioms from an ontology to be expressed in the text.<SEP>A stage in natural language generation that determines which available facts from a knowledge source are selected to be communicated.<SEP>A stage in natural language generation that determines which facts from an ontology or data source should be conveyed in the output text.<SEP>A subtask in natural language generation focused on choosing which facts to express, computationally analogous to the multiple knapsack problem.<SEP>A subtask in natural language generation that determines which facts or information from a knowledge pool or database should be expressed in the output text.<SEP>Content selection is a sub-task and process in natural language generation systems that determines which facts from an ontology are chosen for inclusion in generated texts.<SEP>Content selection is a subtask in natural language generation that determines which information units or facts from the input data should be expressed in the output text.

Text Planning
A stage in natural language generation that determines the sequence of facts, sentence order, and rhetorical structure of a text.<SEP>An overarching natural language generation stage that governs the discourse structure, organization, and ordering of generated content.

Lexicalization
A natural language generation stage that selects vocabulary, phrasing, and sentence plans to express facts in linguistic form.<SEP>A stage in natural language generation responsible for choosing the vocabulary, words, and syntactic structures used to express selected facts.<SEP>A stage in natural language generation that selects the specific words and syntactic structures used to express individual facts.<SEP>A stage in text generation involving the selection of appropriate words and syntactic phrases to express chosen concepts or facts.<SEP>Lexicalization is a subtask in natural language generation responsible for choosing specific words and syntactic forms to express concepts and relations.

Sentence Aggregation
A natural language generation process that merges multiple facts or clauses into single sentences to improve text flow, compactness, and readability.<SEP>A natural language generation process that merges multiple simple sentences or sentence plans into concise, aggregated sentences.<SEP>A natural language processing technique that combines multiple simple sentences or semantic facts into complex, cohesive sentences.<SEP>A process in natural language generation that combines multiple facts or simple clauses into unified, cohesive, and compact sentences.<SEP>An NLG process that merges multiple shorter sentences into fewer, longer sentences to improve compactness and readability.<SEP>Sentence aggregation is a natural language generation process that combines multiple facts into compact subsets to produce coherent, aggregated sentences.<SEP>Sentence aggregation is an NLG subtask that combines multiple simple semantic messages or sentences into single, more complex sentences to reduce redundancy.

Referring Expression Generation
A component of NLG that generates appropriate referring forms, such as pronouns or noun phrases, to identify entities in discourse.<SEP>A natural language generation subtask focused on producing appropriate noun phrases or pronouns to identify referents unambiguously in discourse.<SEP>A natural language generation subtask focused on selecting the most appropriate names, nouns, or descriptions for entities and classes.<SEP>Referring expression generation is an NLG subtask that selects appropriate linguistic expressions to identify domain entities in text.

Surface Realization
The final natural language generation phase that converts structured linguistic representations into grammatically correct surface text.<SEP>The final stage in natural language generation that transforms abstract linguistic structures into actual strings of words according to syntactic and morphological rules.<SEP>The final stage of natural language generation that converts abstract internal linguistic representations into actual textual strings.

Over-Generate and Rank
An architectural strategy in NLG that produces multiple alternative candidates at each stage and ranks them to mitigate greedy pipeline decisions.

StEmilionRegion
A geographic region referenced in the ontology as the location where StEmilion wine is produced.

StEmilion
A class in the wine ontology defined as an intersection of Bordeaux wines, located in the St. Emilion region, possessing strong flavor, red color, and made from Cabernet Sauvignon grapes.<SEP>StEmilion (Saint-Émilion) is a renowned wine-producing region and appellation in southwestern France, featured as an individual entity in the ontology and sentence planning examples.<SEP>StEmilion refers to Saint-Émilion, a prominent wine-producing region used as an example subject in the sentence plan templates.

Bordeaux
A class of wines in the ontology under which StEmilion is defined as a subclass.<SEP>Bordeaux is a major wine-growing region in southwestern France, used in the text as both a geographic location and an ontological class.<SEP>Bordeaux is a prominent wine-producing region in southwestern France, referenced as a classification or category of wine.

Wines
A knowledge domain and ontology used to test the integer linear programming natural language generation model.

Consumer Electronics
A broad product category encompassing electronic devices like cameras, camcorders, and printers, utilized as a real-world e-commerce test domain.<SEP>A knowledge domain and ontology evaluated in the natural language generation experiments.<SEP>Consumer Electronics represents the domain and ontology category used in the second set of text generation experiments.<SEP>The domain of electronic products modeled by the Consumer Electronics Ontology.

Diseases
A medical knowledge domain and ontology used in the experiments to evaluate text generation compactness.

Naturalowl
A natural language generation system whose text planner and referring expression generation components are utilized by the experimental systems.<SEP>An open-source natural language generation system for OWL ontologies that implements typical NLG processing stages and serves as the baseline and integration platform for the ILP models.<SEP>NaturalOWL is an ontology-based natural language generation system that utilizes a pipeline architecture and domain-dependent linguistic resources.<SEP>Naturalowl is an open-source, publicly available natural language generation system designed for OWL ontologies that originally operated using a pipeline architecture.

Cabernet Sauvignon
A grape variety defined as an ingredient property value for the StEmilion wine class within the OWL wine ontology.<SEP>Cabernet Sauvignon is a grape variety and wine category used in the linguistic aggregation and text generation examples.<SEP>Cabernet Sauvignon is a grape variety identified in the ontology as the exclusive grape used to make St. Emilion wine.

Red Wine
A wine category cited as an example of common-sense or obvious knowledge in referring expressions.<SEP>Red Wine is a subcategory of wine characterized by its red color, used as an example of semantic redundancy in text generation.

St. Emilion Region
The St. Emilion Region is a geographical wine-producing area associated with St. Emilion wines.

Piemonte
Piemonte is a wine-producing geographical region in Italy referenced in ontological classification examples.<SEP>Piemonte is an Italian region referenced as a geographic location in ontology triples and generated natural language expressions.

St. Emilion Wine
St. Emilion is an ontological wine class defined as a red, strong Bordeaux wine originating from the St. Emilion region and made exclusively from Cabernet Sauvignon grapes.

Bordeaux Wine
Bordeaux wine is a broader classification of wines to which St. Emilion belongs as a subclass.

Colorado Tick Fever
Colorado Tick Fever is a medical disease condition used as an ontological example with symptoms including fatigue, headache, and myalgia.

Traditional Wine from Piemonte
Traditional Wine from Piemonte is an ontological class representing traditional wines originating from the Piemonte region.

Fatigue
Fatigue is a clinical symptom category associated with Colorado Tick Fever in ontological examples.<SEP>Fatigue is a clinical symptom characterized by extreme tiredness, listed as a symptom of Brazilian hemorrhagic fever.

Headache
Headache is a clinical symptom category associated with Colorado Tick Fever in ontological examples.

Myalgia
Myalgia is a muscle pain symptom category associated with Colorado Tick Fever in ontological examples.

Message Triple
A formal semantic representation of a fact consisting of a target individual or class, a relation, and an object, serving as the input for text generation.<SEP>A message triple is a semantic representation category comprising a subject, relation, and object used by NaturalOWL to prepare ontology facts for verbalization.<SEP>A semantic data unit composed of a subject, property/relation, and object used as input for natural language generation.<SEP>A structured semantic representation consisting of subject, predicate, and object elements (such as facts) used as input for text generation.

RDF Triple
An RDF triple is a standard Semantic Web statement category from which message triples are adapted with potential relation modifiers.

Sentence Plan
A sentence plan is a linguistic template category in NaturalOWL that dictates how a specific relation within a message triple is expressed in natural language.<SEP>A sentence plan is an intermediate linguistic structure used to verbalize facts, composed of distinct elements that contribute to the length and structure of aggregated sentences.<SEP>A structured linguistic plan consisting of distinct elements and referring expressions designed to produce natural language sentences.<SEP>A structured linguistic template comprising slots and instructions that define how to verbalize a semantic fact or message triple into a natural language sentence.<SEP>A structured sequence of annotated linguistic slots used in natural language generation to realize semantic relations into natural text.<SEP>Sentence Plan is a structural template category in NaturalOWL that defines how to construct sentences expressing ontological message triples.

Natural Language Name
A linguistic expression or designation (nl name) used to indirectly express facts or reference concepts within generated text.<SEP>A natural language name (nl name) is a structured category consisting of annotated slots used to generate noun phrases for ontology classes and individuals.<SEP>Natural Language Name (NL Name) is a structured linguistic specification category in NaturalOWL composed of annotated slots that describe an individual or class.

Ontology Verbalizer

Disease Ontology
A biomedical domain ontology characterized by facts with conjuncts and varied natural language naming lengths.<SEP>A biomedical domain ontology characterized by varied natural language name lengths and conjunctions, used to evaluate extended ILP and baseline text generation models.<SEP>Disease Ontology is a formal biomedical ontology used as an experimental dataset for evaluating concept-to-text natural language generation systems.<SEP>The Disease Ontology is a biomedical domain ontology comprising development classes used in the third set of natural language generation experiments.<SEP>The Disease Ontology is a biomedical knowledge base and ontology resource used in experiments to provide structured medical facts and vocabulary.<SEP>The Disease Ontology is a domain ontology representing diseases, referenced as a point of comparison in text generation experiments.<SEP>The Disease Ontology is a formal ontology describing diseases, containing 6,746 classes, 15 relations, and 1,545 individuals, used as the knowledge base for NLG experiments.<SEP>The Disease Ontology is a structured biomedical knowledge domain used as a dataset for evaluating natural language generation systems and sentence aggregation models.

Paralysis of the legs due to thrombosis of spinal arteries is a specific medical condition used as an individual example within the Disease Ontology.

Dry Wine

Moderate Flavor
A sensory categorization describing moderate flavor intensity within wine ontology specifications.

Constraints
A set of mathematical restrictions (such as Eq. 34 and Eq. 35) limiting the word count of subsets and regulating the selection of sentences and natural language names for expressed facts.

Computational Complexity and Approximation
A theoretical category and section topic addressing the computational difficulty and approximation techniques associated with solving the optimization model.

Fact Expression
The selection and inclusion of informational facts ($f_i$) in the output text based on their relative importance.

Sentence Generation
The mechanism of generating explicit sentences ($a_i = 1$) for selected facts when they are not expressed via natural language names.

Word Limit Constraint
A constraint bounding the maximum number of words ($W_{max}$) allowed within each subset of generated text.

Priority Weighting
Tuning parameters ($\lambda_1, \lambda_2$) balancing the trade-off between maximizing expressed important facts and minimizing text length.

Binary ILP Problems
A class of mathematical optimization problems where all variables are restricted to binary values, known in general to be NP-hard.

NP-Hard
A complexity class of computational problems that are at least as difficult as the hardest problems in NP, including binary ILP and knapsack problems.

0-1 Multiple Knapsack Problem
A combinatorial optimization problem class where items are packed into multiple knapsacks of given capacities, closely related to content selection in text generation models.

Linear Programming
A mathematical optimization framework with continuous variables used in LP relaxation to approximate integer linear programming solutions.

Consumer Electronics Ontology
A domain ontology containing product specifications with a large number of available facts per product, used to evaluate system scalability and approximation methods.<SEP>A domain ontology covering electronic products, characterized by unique product names that limit alternative natural language naming.<SEP>A domain ontology utilized in the text generation experiments that required setting the subset parameter m to 5 or greater.<SEP>A domain-specific knowledge ontology utilized to provide concepts, text plans, and sentence plans for generating longer texts in the second experiment.<SEP>A domain-specific ontology used in natural language generation experiments, containing an average of 14 facts and up to 21 facts per individual.<SEP>Consumer Electronics Ontology is a domain ontology containing knowledge about consumer electronic products, used to test solver efficiency and generation quality in NLG models.<SEP>The Consumer Electronics Ontology is a domain ontology covering product attributes and specifications, used to evaluate text conciseness and clarity.<SEP>The Consumer Electronics Ontology is a domain ontology previously used to evaluate natural language generation solver times and text aggregation models.<SEP>The Consumer Electronics Ontology is a domain ontology representing electronic products, discussed in relation to naming constraints in text generation.

First ILP Model
An integer linear programming model developed for text generation and content selection that operates effectively when the number of fact subsets is small (m <= 4).

Extended ILP Model
An expanded integer linear programming formulation for text generation that accounts for natural language name variations and whose complexity grows exponentially with the number of fact subsets.

Simplex Algorithm
A widely used optimization algorithm for solving linear programming models, specifically utilized in solving linear programming relaxations.

LP Relaxation
An approximation technique in mathematical optimization where integer constraints are relaxed to continuous values to solve ILP problems in polynomial time.

Totally Unimodular Matrix
A matrix property where every square nonsingular submatrix has determinant 0, 1, or -1, guaranteeing integer solutions to linear programming relaxations.

Pipeline Approach
A conventional multistep architecture for natural language generation against which the ILP models and approximation methods are benchmarked.

Off-The-Shelf Solvers
Standard commercial or open-source mathematical programming solvers used to solve the original binary ILP models directly.

Ontology Evaluation Experiments
A series of experiments conducted to evaluate integer linear programming (ILP) models across multiple OWL ontologies representing different domains.

Concept-To-Text Generation
The automated generation of multi-sentence natural language texts directly from formal conceptual representations, databases, or ontologies.

A natural language processing task that condenses information across multiple text documents into a unified summary, often using joint optimization ILP models.

A text-to-text generation task aimed at shortening a sentence while retaining its core grammatical meaning, frequently formulated via ILP.

Joint Optimization
An optimization paradigm where multiple interdependent subtasks or decisions are modeled and solved simultaneously rather than in a sequential pipeline.

Recurrent Neural Layers
Recurrent neural layers are deep learning architectural components used to model sequential data and fuse feature information across multiple related tasks.

Multi-Sentence Concept-To-Text Generation
Multi-sentence concept-to-text generation is a process within natural language generation focusing on converting structured ontology knowledge into fluent multi-sentence texts.

Single-Task Learning
A standard supervised learning approach where a dedicated model is trained independently on a single specific task with its own dataset and objective function.

Multi-Cardinality Tasks
A perspective of multi-task learning where tasks share similar characteristics but differ in cardinality parameters, such as sequence lengths or number of target classes.

Multi-Domain Tasks
A multi-task learning perspective involving tasks spanning different domains or subject areas, such as product reviews across varying item types.

Multi-Objective Tasks
A multi-task learning scenario where tasks are designed for distinct goals or objectives, such as sentiment analysis, topic categorization, and question type judgment.

Semantic Matching
A natural language processing task focused on determining the degree of semantic correspondence or relevance between two text units.

Recursive Neural Networks
A class of deep neural networks that process hierarchical, tree-structured inputs to compute compositional vector representations.

Neural Bag-Of-Words
A simple neural network architecture that computes continuous representations of text by aggregating word vector embeddings without sequential modeling.

Topic Classification
A text classification sub-task dedicated to organizing and categorizing documents into distinct topic-based themes.

Question Type Judgment
A classification task in natural language processing aimed at categorizing user inquiries based on expected answer types or intent.

Long Short-Term Memory Network
A variant of recurrent neural networks equipped with internal memory cells and gating mechanisms to address gradient vanishing and exploding problems and capture long-term dependencies.

Multi-Task Learning Architecture
A generalized neural network framework designed to jointly learn multiple text classification tasks in parallel using specialized intra-task and inter-task recurrent neural layers.

Single Layer
An intra-task LSTM-based recurrent neural network layer dedicated to individual task representation learning within the multi-task framework.

Coupling Layer
An inter-task architectural layer designed to model direct pair-wise interactions and information exchange between tasks via gating mechanisms.

Local Fusion Layer
A shared bi-directional LSTM layer designed to facilitate indirect pair-wise interactions between tasks through concatenated inputs.

Global Fusion Layer
A core structural component of the neural network architecture composed of a bi-directional LSTM layer that computes global fusion terms and memory storage across tasks.<SEP>A shared bi-directional LSTM layer providing global memory storage to capture shared representations across all learning tasks.

BIBREF12
A researcher or author cited for proposing the original Long Short-Term Memory network architecture.

BIBREF13
A researcher or author cited for providing the specific LSTM implementation referenced and adapted in the proposed multi-task architecture.

Bi-directional LSTM
A variant of the Long Short-Term Memory network that processes sequential information in both forward and backward directions.

Gradient Vanishing and Exploding
A mathematical challenge during backpropagation in recurrent neural networks where gradient vectors grow or decay exponentially over long sequences.

Gating Mechanism
Algorithmic control structures used to regulate, filter, and balance the flow of information and memory retention within neural layers.

Fully Connected Layer
A standard dense neural network layer connecting the hidden states of recurrent layers to the softmax output layer.

Intra-Task Learning
The process of learning feature representations dedicated to a single specific task within a multi-task learning framework.

Inter-Task Interaction
The exchange and coordination of information across different tasks, either directly pair-wise or indirectly via shared fusion mechanisms.

Pre-trained Lookup Table
A pre-trained vector embedding mapping used to transform input tokens into dense vector representations before neural network processing.

Task Oriented Sampling
An algorithmic sampling method proposed to generate multi-task sample collections specifically tailored to improve the performance of an oriented task.

Multi-Domain Scenario
An experimental evaluation setting consisting of product review datasets across different domains such as Books, DVDs, Electronics, and Kitchen.

Multi-Cardinality Scenario
An experimental evaluation setting featuring movie review datasets with varying average sequence lengths and class counts, including SST-1, SST-2, and IMDB.

Multi-Objective Scenario
An experimental evaluation setting combining datasets with divergent classification objectives, such as sentiment analysis, topic detection, and question categorization.

Bi-Directional LSTM
A recurrent neural network architecture utilized in the Global Fusion Layer to process sequential inputs across tasks.

Type-I Multi-Task Learning
A classification of multi-task learning models referenced from previous studies that process task samples through traditional formulations.

Type-II Multi-Task Learning
A classification of standard multi-task learning models used in prior literature.

Type-III Multi-Task Learning
An advanced multi-task learning model architecture requiring a 4-D tensor input to jointly learn samples from different tasks in parallel.

SST-1
A sentiment analysis benchmark dataset consisting of movie reviews with multiple class numbers and varying sequence lengths, used in multi-cardinality evaluation.

Multi-Domain Sentiment Dataset
A collection of product review datasets across diverse domains including Books, DVDs, Electronics, and Kitchen, used to evaluate multi-domain learning.

QC Dataset
A question classification benchmark dataset designed to classify questions into six categories, evaluated within the multi-objective scenario.

RN Dataset
A text classification benchmark dataset evaluated in the multi-objective experiment scenario.

Stochastic Gradient Descent
An iterative optimization algorithm paired with backpropagation used to train the parameters of the multi-task learning network.

Pair-Wise Performance Gain
A metric formulated to quantify the correlation strength and performance variation between two individual tasks when trained jointly versus independently.

Product Reviews
A domain category of customer reviews comprising domains such as Books, DVDs, Electronics, and Kitchen with shared sentiment characteristics.

Movie Reviews
A domain category of text reviews featuring varying class cardinalities and lengths represented by SST-1, SST-2, and IMDB datasets.

Shuguang Hospital
Shuguang Hospital is a medical institution from which coronary angiography clinical records were collected for evaluating joint entity and relation extraction models.

Entity And Relation Extraction
Entity and relation extraction is an information extraction task category in natural language processing aimed at identifying entities and their semantic relationships from unstructured text.

Coronary Angiography
Coronary angiography is a medical examination and procedure category, whose textual diagnostic reports serve as domain-specific text for clinical information extraction.

Relation Classification
A natural language processing task (RC) focused on determining semantic relations between identified entities in text.<SEP>An information extraction sub-task category focused on identifying the specific semantic relationships between identified entities.<SEP>An information extraction task that determines and classifies semantic relationships between recognized entities in a text.<SEP>Relation classification is a natural language processing task focused on categorizing semantic connections and relationships between identified entities in text.

Clinical Decision Making
A medical decision-making process category supported by integrated electronic health records.<SEP>Clinical decision making is a healthcare process category supported by information extracted from electronic health records to guide patient diagnosis and treatment.

Entity and Relation Extraction
A core task category in natural language processing and medical data mining aimed at extracting relational entity triples from unstructured text.

Pipeline Processing
A system architecture category that decomposes information extraction into sequential, independent sub-tasks such as named entity recognition followed by relation classification.

Joint Learning
A machine learning paradigm category in which related tasks, such as named entity recognition and relation classification, are trained simultaneously to capture joint features.<SEP>A machine learning paradigm where models for named entity recognition and relation classification are trained concurrently to share representations.

Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory
A category of recurrent neural network architectures commonly used as a shared parameter layer in sequence tagging and joint learning tasks.

Symptom
A clinical entity category targeted in medical named entity recognition, frequently serving as a central word in electronic health record entity triples.

STR-Encoder
A modified BERT language model architecture known as the shared task representation encoder that alters the attention range of the last K layers to generate task-specific representations.<SEP>STR-encoder (shared task representation encoder) is an architectural model component improved from BERT that uses dynamic range attention to produce task-specific representations.<SEP>STR-encoder is a neural encoding component in the proposed model that learns joint features of entities and relations using MASK matrices.

Focused Attention Model
A neural network model architecture proposed for jointly learning named entity recognition and relation classification using dynamic range attention.<SEP>A neural network model architecture proposed to jointly learn named entity recognition and relation classification using an integrated BERT parameter layer.<SEP>A proposed model built upon BERT to dynamically adjust attention range for joint entity and relation extraction.<SEP>Focused Attention Model is a joint learning architecture for NER and RC based on a shared parameter approach.<SEP>The Focused Attention Model is the proposed deep learning architecture designed for joint named entity recognition and relation extraction.

Dynamic Range Attention Mechanism
An attention mechanism category designed to construct task-specific MASK matrices to constrain attention ranges in transformer layers.<SEP>An attention mechanism used to transform BERT into the STR-encoder by adjusting attention ranges across entity pairs.<SEP>Dynamic Range Attention Mechanism is an attention control method that utilizes custom MASK matrices to constrain or direct word attention ranges for specific downstream tasks.<SEP>The dynamic range attention mechanism is a category of attention mechanism used to determine and constrain the attention span of words and tokens via task-specific mask matrices.

Task-Specific MASK Matrix
An attention masking matrix structure used to guide the attention range of transformer layers toward relevant words for specific tasks.

BIEOS Tagging Scheme
A standard sequence labeling category representing Begin, Inside, End, Outside, and Single tags used for formulating named entity recognition.

Presence Word
A semantic category of entities in clinical natural language processing denoting presence, absence, or status of symptoms and diseases.

Relational Entity Triples
A structured data category composed of two entities and their relationship, extracted from unstructured text.

Data Mining Algorithms
A category of computational techniques used to discover patterns in structured data, requiring text to be pre-processed into key-value pairs.

Government Health Policy Formulation
A public health administrative process category supported by aggregated electronic health record data.

Joint Entity and Relation Extraction
A combined natural language processing task that performs entity recognition and relation classification simultaneously.<SEP>An information extraction framework that simultaneously detects entities and identifies relationships between them to capture joint features.

Pipeline Methods
Approaches in natural language processing that decompose information extraction into two sequential steps: named entity recognition followed by relation classification.

Joint Learning Methods
Approaches that perform entity recognition and relation classification simultaneously, capturing joint features to improve generalization performance.

Joint Tagging
A category of joint learning that transforms named entity recognition and relation classification into sequence tagging tasks using specialized tagging schemes.

Zheng et al.
Researchers who proposed a novel tagging scheme for joint entity and relation extraction via sequence tagging.

Medical Domain
A specialized field of application where natural language processing tasks focus on clinical concepts such as diseases, symptoms, and anatomical relationships.

Conditional Random Fields
A statistical modeling method frequently used for structured sequence tagging and named entity recognition.<SEP>Conditional Random Fields is a class of statistical modeling methods and supervised machine learning algorithms used for structured prediction and sentiment analysis.

Hidden Markov Models
Statistical sequence models utilized in conventional named entity recognition systems.

Recurrent Capsule Network
A neural network architecture applied to relation classification in the medical domain.

Domain Invariant Convolutional Neural Network
A convolutional neural network variant adapted for robust relation classification across domains.

ELMo
A contextualized word representation language model trained on unsupervised text data.

GPT
A generative pre-trained transformer language model utilizing unsupervised corpora for text representations.

Self-Attention Encoder
A core structural component of the BERT model comprising an embedding layer and multiple multi-head self-attention layers.

ResNet
A residual neural network architecture integrated into multi-head self-attention layers to mitigate gradient vanishing and exploding.

ResNet Architecture
ResNet architecture is a deep neural network design applied within the multi-head self-attention layers to prevent gradient vanishing and exploding problems.

NER
NER (Named Entity Recognition) is a category of downstream natural language processing task focused on identifying entities by assigning sequence tags to words.<SEP>NER (Named Entity Recognition) is a downstream natural language processing task jointly learned with RC using the focused attention model.<SEP>NER (Named Entity Recognition) is a natural language processing task that identifies and classifies named entities in unstructured text.<SEP>Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a natural language processing task focused on identifying and classifying key entities within text.

RC
RC (Relation Classification) is a category of downstream natural language processing task designed to determine and summarize the relation between pairs of entities.<SEP>RC (Relation Classification) is a downstream natural language processing task integrated into the focused attention model alongside NER.<SEP>RC (Relation Classification) is a natural language processing task focused on identifying and classifying semantic relationships between entity pairs.<SEP>Relation Classification (RC) is an information extraction task aimed at determining semantic relationships between entity pairs.

Multi-Head Self-Attention
Multi-head self-attention (MHSA) is a neural network mechanism that computes context-dependent word representations using multiple parallel attention heads.

SA-Encoder
SA-encoder is a self-attention encoder that produces context-dependent word representations from an input sequence and a MASK matrix before passing them to downstream task layers.

MASK Matrix
MASK matrix is a parameter matrix of size T x T used to control the range of attention across word positions in self-attention mechanisms.

CLS Token
[CLS] is a special classification token placed at the beginning of an input sequence, adopted from BERT.

SEP Token
[SEP] is a special separator token appended to the end of an input sequence to denote termination.

BIEOS Tag
BIEOS tag represents a category of sequence labeling scheme utilized in named entity recognition to identify the boundaries and types of entities in a text.

Medical Text
Medical text represents a domain-specific category of textual data referenced for applying and analyzing the relation classification task.

CRF Model
A CRF (Conditional Random Field) model is a category of statistical modeling method used in the NER downstream task layer to capture transition and emission probabilities between sequential tags.

Pre-Trained Language Model
A pre-trained language model is a category of deep learning model trained on large-scale text corpora that contains prior linguistic knowledge used for transfer learning.

Single-Layer Neural Network
A single-layer neural network is a category of baseline neural architecture contrasted with CRF models due to its limitation in capturing link relations between adjacent tags.

Shanghai Shuguang Hospital
Shanghai Shuguang Hospital is a medical institution from which coronary arteriography reports were collected to create an entity and relation extraction dataset.

Shanghai
Shanghai is a major metropolitan city in China where Shanghai Shuguang Hospital is located.

Coronary Arteriography Reports
Coronary Arteriography Reports are clinical diagnostic documents from which entities and relations were extracted for the experimental dataset.

Negation
Negation is an entity category defined in the medical dataset indicating the absence or denial of a clinical condition.

Body Part
Body Part is an entity category defined in the medical dataset identifying anatomical structures.

Degree
Degree is an entity category defined in the medical dataset describing the severity or extent of a finding.

Quantifier
Quantifier is an entity category defined in the medical dataset specifying numerical values or quantitative descriptors.

Location
A named entity category designating geographical places and sites, accounting for 282 annotations in the analyzed Turkish tweet dataset.<SEP>Location is an entity category defined in the medical dataset indicating positional or spatial references in medical text.

Negative
Negative is a relation category identified in the medical dataset connecting entities with negation.

Modifier
Modifier is a relation category identified in the medical dataset linking descriptive modifiers to entities.

Position
Position is a relation category identified in the medical dataset representing location or directional associations.

Percentage
Percentage is a relation category identified in the medical dataset representing proportion or percentage relations.

No Relation
No Relation is a category denoting the absence of a meaningful relationship between entity pairs in the dataset.

Joint Entity And Relation Extraction
Joint Entity and Relation Extraction is a sub-task and research problem in natural language processing aimed at simultaneously identifying entities and their semantic relations.<SEP>Joint Entity and Relation Extraction is an integrated NLP task that simultaneously identifies entities and their semantic relations.

Adam Optimization Algorithm
Adam is an optimization algorithm used to train and update parameters in the neural network model.

Joint-Bi-LSTM
A baseline neural network model architecture used for comparison in the task of joint entity and relation extraction.<SEP>Joint-Bi-LSTM is a generic domain baseline model used for comparison in joint entity and relation extraction tasks.

RDCNN
RDCNN is a medical domain neural network model used as a baseline for named entity recognition evaluation.

RCN
RCN is a medical domain baseline neural model evaluated specifically on relation classification tasks.

Precision
Precision is an evaluation metric measuring the proportion of true positive predictions among all positive instances identified.

Recall
Recall is an evaluation metric measuring the proportion of actual positive instances successfully retrieved by the model.

F1-Score
F1-score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, serving as a primary overall performance metric for NER, RC, and joint models.

National Key R&D Program of China
A government research funding initiative in China that supported the research under the Precision Medical Research grant.

STR-encoder

A clinical domain dataset of medical texts used to verify the effectiveness and performance of the proposed extraction model.

Precision Medical Research
A national scientific research initiative and grant focus area aimed at medical text structuring and advanced healthcare intelligence.

Bigram Frequencies Calculation
A computational natural language processing task discussed for its efficiency and suitability when applied to short text corpora.

Anonymous Reviewers
Peer reviewers who evaluated the manuscript and provided valuable feedback and comments acknowledged by the authors.

Editors
Editorial personnel acknowledged for coordinating the evaluation and publication of the research paper.

Joel Nothman
Joel Nothman is a researcher or practitioner acknowledged for having a conversation with the authors and sketching a solution for calculating bigram frequencies in short texts.

Church
Church is a researcher and co-author of a widely cited paper with Hanks proposing an approximation method for calculating bigram frequencies.

Hanks
Hanks is a researcher and co-author with Church of a seminal paper on word association norms and bigram frequency approximations.

Bilingual Lexicon Induction
A natural language processing task (abbreviated as BLI) focused on mapping and translating lexical and morphological forms across languages.<SEP>An established computational linguistics task focused on inducing word translations and serving as a standard evaluation benchmark for cross-lingual word embedding models.<SEP>Bilingual Lexicon Induction (BLI) is a computational linguistics task that aims to induce cross-lingual word mappings and dictionaries from monolingual embeddings.<SEP>Bilingual Lexicon Induction (BLI) is a computational linguistics task that focuses on inducing translations between word forms across different languages.<SEP>Bilingual Lexicon Induction (BLI) is a natural language processing task aimed at inducing word translations between language pairs, particularly focusing on generalizing to rare and novel words.<SEP>Bilingual Lexicon Induction (BLI) is a task in natural language processing aimed at learning word translations between languages.<SEP>Bilingual Lexicon Induction (BLI) is an NLP evaluation task mentioned in the document's introductory fragments concerning lexical paradigms.<SEP>Bilingual lexicon induction is a natural language processing technique for extracting translation pairs across languages using comparable corpora.

Comparable Corpora
Comparable Corpora are collections of multilingual documents that share topical alignment but lack direct sentence-by-sentence alignment.<SEP>Comparable corpora are collections of texts in multiple languages that discuss similar topics without being direct sentence-by-sentence translations of each other.

Siamese Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Network
A Siamese bidirectional recurrent neural network is a deep learning architecture used to identify and extract parallel sentences from comparable multilingual articles.<SEP>A deep learning architecture featuring two identical bidirectional recurrent neural networks used to extract parallel sentences from multilingual comparable corpora without requiring pre-existing translation systems or extensive feature engineering.

Bigram Frequency Calculation
Bigram frequency calculation is a statistical natural language processing task that computes the occurrence of word pairs within specified window sizes across text corpora.

Parallel Sentence Extraction
Parallel Sentence Extraction is the methodology and pipeline used to identify and decode translation-equivalent sentence pairs from comparable bilingual text.<SEP>Parallel Sentence Extraction is the technique of identifying and extracting translation-equivalent sentence pairs from non-parallel or comparable texts.

Maximum Entropy Classifier
A statistical machine learning model utilized in prior alignment methods to evaluate and score sentence pairs extracted from comparable corpora based on surface features and word overlap.

Bilingual Lexicon
A cross-lingual dictionary or mapping between words in two languages, induced from comparable corpora to alleviate out-of-vocabulary challenges in translation systems.

Out-Of-Vocabulary
A machine translation challenge where words appearing in source documents are absent from training corpora, resulting in untranslated tokens and reduced translation quality.

Workshops on Machine Translation
Collaborative academic gatherings and shared evaluation tasks that provide crowd-sourced parallel datasets to advance translation research on various language pairs.

Lucene
An open-source search engine software library whose Levenshtein distance implementation and indexing capabilities were utilized for string matching and token resolution.<SEP>An open-source text search engine software library used to execute information retrieval queries over entire comparable corpora based on characteristic domain vocabularies.

Wikimedia
Wikimedia is the organization that hosts Wikipedia and provides the data dumps utilized to collect bilingual English-Tamil and English-Hindi articles.

Moses
Moses is an open-source statistical machine translation system and toolkit that includes scripts like multi-bleu for model evaluation.<SEP>Moses is an open-source statistical machine translation toolkit and research community project used for training phrase-based translation models and evaluation.

Siamese Network
Siamese Network is an artificial neural network architecture using shared or twin sub-networks to map candidate sentence pairs into continuous representations for similarity estimation.

Bidirectional RNN
Bidirectional RNN is a recurrent neural network architecture that processes text sequences in both forward and backward directions to encode sentence representations.

Sequence-to-Sequence
Sequence-to-sequence (Seq2seq) is a neural architecture paradigm that maps an input sequence to an output sequence, commonly used in machine translation.<SEP>Sequence-to-sequence is a neural network architecture paradigm that maps an input sequence to an output sequence, widely used in translation and question answering.

Negative Sampling
Negative Sampling is a training method in machine learning where non-parallel sentence pairs are generated randomly to teach classifiers to discriminate non-translations.

Greedy Decoding
Greedy Decoding is a sequence inference strategy used during decoding and sentence alignment to extract high-precision parallel sentences.

Workshop on Machine Translation
The Workshop on Machine Translation (WMT) is an academic conference event featuring shared tasks such as the Parallel Corpus Filtering task in its 2018 edition.

Parallel Corpus Filtering
Parallel Corpus Filtering is a competitive shared task introduced at the 2018 Workshop on Machine Translation (WMT) focused on filtering noisy web-crawled text into high-quality parallel sentence pairs.

OpenNMT
OpenNMT is an open-source neural machine translation framework and research ecosystem utilized for training sequence-to-sequence and transformer models.<SEP>OpenNMT is an open-source project and generic deep learning framework specialized in sequence-to-sequence neural network models for NLP tasks.

TensorFlow
TensorFlow is an open-source machine learning and deep learning framework developed by Google used here to implement OpenNMT models.

English-Tamil
English-Tamil (en-ta) is a low-resource language pair evaluated in the parallel sentence extraction and translation experiments.

English-Hindi
English-Hindi (en-hi) is a language pair evaluated in the translation experiments to assess BLEU score improvements.

ConceptNet
ConceptNet is a semantic knowledge graph project used to identify and expand relationships between words and entities.

Extractive Question Answering
A task within question answering where the answer is directly extracted as a segment or span from the source context.

FastQA
An RNN-based baseline neural system designed for extractive question answering that incorporates question-word awareness.

Gated-Attention Reader
A multi-hop neural architecture featuring a multiplicative gating mechanism designed for answering cloze-style questions over documents.

Dependency Parsing
A natural language processing technique that analyzes grammatical structure to determine relationships between words in a question or sentence.

Conversational Modelling
The subfield of NLP and AI focused on generating multi-turn dialogues and responses for conversational agents.

Summarisation
Summarisation is a natural language processing task focused on producing a concise and fluent summary of a longer text document.

Speech Processing
Speech processing is an area of computer science and signal processing dealing with the analysis, synthesis, and recognition of spoken language.

Character-Based Neural Model
Character-based neural models operate on individual characters rather than whole words to bypass vocabulary limitations and handle out-of-vocabulary tokens.

N-Triples
N-Triples is a line-based, plain text format for encoding Resource Description Framework (RDF) graphs, representing subject-predicate-object knowledge facts.

DBpedia Infobox Properties
DBpedia Infobox Properties is a structured knowledge dataset extracted from Wikipedia infoboxes, providing semantic property triples used to form question-answer pairs.

METEOR
METEOR is an evaluation metric based on the harmonic mean of precision and recall that incorporates stemming, paraphrasing, and synonymy matching.

chrF
chrF is a character n-gram F-score evaluation metric used to assess generated text quality without heavily penalizing differences in word inflections.

QA System Experiment
The QA system experiment is the scientific evaluation and empirical training conducted to test seq2seq neural networks on question-answer pairs extracted from DBpedia and subtitles.

Science Foundation Ireland
A statutory body in Ireland that provides financial support for scientific research, funding the presented QA research under Grant Number SFI/12/RC/2289.

Insight
A research centre associated with Science Foundation Ireland involved in the funded research project.

Sequence-to-Sequence Neural Model
A deep learning architecture category used for mapping sequences to sequences, applied to question answering and dialogue modeling.

Dialogue Agents
Intelligent conversational agents designed to produce natural responses in human-computer interaction.

Imagine-Then-Arbitrate Model
A neural dialogue model architecture designed to predict conversational turn-taking and decide whether an agent should wait or reply.

METEOR Metric
An automatic evaluation metric based on the harmonic mean of precision and recall with stemming, paraphrasing, and synonymy matching.

BLEU Metric
An automatic n-gram precision overlap evaluation metric used to evaluate the hypothesis answers against gold standard answers.

chrF Metric
A character n-gram evaluation metric that correlates well with human judgment, especially for morphologically rich languages.

Imaginator Module
A sub-component of the ITA neural dialogue model designed to learn the user's and agent's speaking styles and generate possible future utterances.<SEP>A submodule of the Imagine-then-Arbitrate neural dialogue system tasked with simulating conversational continuations.

Arbitrator Module
A component of the ITA model that combines conversation history with generated hypothetical utterances from imaginators to decide whether the agent should wait or reply.<SEP>A decision-making component of the Imagine-then-Arbitrate dialogue model that arbitrates whether to wait or generate an immediate response.<SEP>A text classification and response selection module designed to evaluate predicted dialogue paths and determine whether an agent should respond or wait.

Imagine-then-Arbitrate
A dialogue modeling framework that uses dialogue history, ground truth labels, and simulated future utterances to determine agent turn-taking actions.<SEP>A novel neural dialogue model framework consisting of two imaginator modules and an arbitrator module, designed to decide whether an agent should wait or reply directly.

Dialogue System
A human-computer interaction system or agent used in applications like personal assistants, customer service, and chitchat, focused on generating responses and managing conversational flow.

Seq2Seq
A sequence-to-sequence neural model framework used in deep learning for dialogue response generation and natural language processing.

TextCNN
A convolutional neural network architecture built on pre-trained word vectors used for sentence-level text classification tasks.<SEP>A convolutional neural network architecture category for text processing, utilized as a base structure for the arbitrator module.<SEP>A convolutional neural network architecture trained on pre-trained word vectors for sentence-level classification tasks.

Task-Oriented Dialogue Models
A category of dialogue systems designed to assist users in accomplishing specific tasks by incorporating external knowledge.

Personal Assistant
