Intelligent Customer Service
An automated business application of dialogue agents designed to interact with clients and address service inquiries.

Chitchat Companion
An open-domain conversational agent designed for casual social interaction and entertainment.

Emotion Recognition
A classification task in dialogue systems aimed at detecting human emotional states from conversational text.

Gender Recognition
A classification task used within conversational analysis and natural language processing to identify speaker gender.

Semantically Controlled LSTM
An extension of LSTM that incorporates semantic control for data-driven language generation.

SEQ2SEQ
A sequence generation model architecture often implemented with encoder and decoder networks for utterance generation.

Dialogue Manager
A system component in dialogue architectures responsible for selecting communication goals to be converted into natural language by generation modules.

Dialogue Agent
An automated conversational participant or chatbot designed to decide the appropriate timing to reply rather than responding to every message.

Human User
A conversational participant interacting with the dialogue agent across multiple conversation turns and subturns.

Rule-Based Approach
A traditional NLG methodology relying on hand-crafted templates, rules, and heuristics designed by domain experts.

Retrieval Method
A dialogue response approach that selects existing candidate responses, distinct from generative natural language generation.

Imaginator
A generative module designed to predict potential agent and user responses based on prior dialogue history.<SEP>A sequence generation component within the ITA framework that learns conversational styles to simulate prospective future dialogue utterances.

User's Imaginator
A specialized imaginator module trained on conversational history to learn the human user's speaking style and generate anticipated user utterances.

Task-Oriented Dialogue
A category of conversational systems and datasets focused on assisting users to accomplish specific tasks, exemplified by MultiWOZ 2.0 and DSTC 2.<SEP>A functional category of conversational AI systems and corpora oriented toward completing specific tasks using slots and ontology values.

Chitchat
A category of informal, open-domain conversational interaction, represented in the text by datasets such as DailyDialogue.

Human-Computer Interaction
A domain and category of interactive communication between humans and computational systems that the proposed conversational approach targets.

DSTC 2

Bi-GRU

KVR

Agent Imaginator

User Imaginator

Bi-GRUs
Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units, an established recurrent neural network architecture utilized as an experimental baseline.

TextCNNs

LSTM-Attention

ITA
A proposed conversational framework comprising imaginators and arbitrators, evaluated against several baseline models.

GLOVE
Global Vectors for Word Representation, a pretrained word embedding method integrated with LSTM-attention imaginators.

Arbitrator

Accuracy Score

Multi-Turn Dialogue
A conversational format consisting of multiple exchanges between dialogue participants, characterizing both task-oriented and daily datasets.

Utterance Splitting

Drop Slots And Values

Morphological Generalization is an evaluation framework assessing how well cross-lingual models translate rare and unseen inflected word forms.<SEP>Morphological Generalization is the capability of models or human translators to generate and understand rare inflections of words based on general morphological rules.<SEP>The ability of a language model or translator to understand, produce, and map rare or unseen inflectional forms of lexemes accurately.<SEP>The ability of bilingual lexicon induction models to accurately translate rare, inflected, or previously unseen morphological variants of words.

Open-Vocabulary BLI
A setting in bilingual lexicon induction that tests a model's capacity to translate out-of-vocabulary and rare morphological variants rather than just closed-vocabulary words.<SEP>A variant of bilingual lexicon induction that evaluates word translation models on rare and out-of-vocabulary inflected word forms.

Wiktionary

UniMorph
A project providing inflectional word paradigms and morphological schema across dozens of languages, utilized for generating morphological dictionaries.<SEP>UniMorph is a collaborative morphological project providing grammatical inflections used to construct out-of-vocabulary evaluation data.<SEP>UniMorph is an open collaborative project and database that provides morphological data and gold standard morphological tags for word forms across languages.

MUSE

fastText
An open-source library and project providing large-scale word representation models and embeddings.

Digital Stylometry

Iterative alignment algorithms used in bilingual lexicon induction to learn cross-lingual mappings without exhaustive supervision.

Standard BLI Task

An experimental evaluation setting designed to measure morphological generalization in bilingual lexicon induction independently of lexeme frequency.

Social Networks

Wincenty Lutosławski

Agence Nationale de Sécurité du Médicament et des Produits de Santé
The official French regulatory agency (ANSM) responsible for the safety of health products and medicines, funding the DRUGS-SAFE platform.

Dictionary-Based Approach
A natural language processing and text matching methodology that uses structured vocabularies, dictionaries, and token trees to assign medical codes to clinical text.

Levenshtein Method
A string metric and fuzzy matching algorithm used to calculate edit distance and identify compound or split words such as medical terms.

Pharmacoepidemiology
The study of the uses and effects of drugs in populations, which forms the core focus of the DRUGS-SAFE platform.

Sentiment Classes
A three-tier categorical classification system consisting of negative, neutral, and positive sentiment labels, perceived as ordered by human annotators.<SEP>Discrete, ordered categories—specifically negative, neutral, and positive—used to quantify emotional perception in text.<SEP>The ordered sentiment classification categories (negative, neutral, and positive) evaluated by human annotators in Twitter sentiment analysis.

Inter-Annotator Agreement
A measurement category assessing the consistency and reliability of labels assigned to identical tweets by two different annotators.<SEP>A metric and quality criterion measuring consistency between different human annotators when labeling the same texts for sentiment.<SEP>A metric quantifying consensus among multiple human annotators labeling the same data, serving as an upper bound benchmark for automated classification performance.<SEP>A performance benchmark and reliability metric quantifying the consensus between different annotators labeling identical tweets.<SEP>A statistical measure used to quantify the consistency and quality of annotations produced by human coders on training datasets.<SEP>A statistical metric used to measure agreement between different human annotators and to establish an upper bound for classifier performance.<SEP>An evaluation metric calculated from multiple annotations of the same tweet by different annotators, used to assess the objective difficulty of the sentiment annotation task.

Dodds
A researcher, cited alongside collaborators, who conducted a massive study collecting millions of human sentiment assessments for common words across multiple languages.

Lexicon-Based Approach
A methodology in sentiment analysis where the sentiment of a text is determined using a predefined set of sentiment-bearing words.<SEP>A sentiment classification method utilizing precompiled dictionaries of sentiment values to categorize text polarity.

SentiWordNet
A widely known semi-automatically constructed sentiment lexicon containing over 100,000 English words.

Self-Annotator Agreement
A metric measuring the internal consistency of an individual annotator over time, used to monitor and improve dataset quality.

Twitter Sentiment Classification
The specialized task of automatically classifying sentiment in Twitter posts using machine learning or lexicon-based methods.

Evaluation Measures
Statistical metrics employed to evaluate annotator agreement and compare the performance of machine learning classifiers.

Emojis Dataset
A dataset covering emoji sentiment annotations, which is subsumed by the 13 language datasets analyzed in the study.<SEP>An application dataset analyzed in the study, characterized by having an exceptionally low self-annotator agreement compared to inter-annotator agreement due to Spanish annotations.<SEP>An application dataset focused on emojis where inter-annotator agreement was exceptionally higher than self-agreement.<SEP>The Emojis Dataset is an application dataset composed of tweets containing emojis extracted across multilingual sentiment corpora.

Facebook(it) Dataset
An Italian-language application dataset from Facebook exhibiting high self-agreement and inter-annotator agreement, yet leaving a gap to classifier performance.<SEP>An application dataset within the study originating from Facebook, exhibiting both high inter-annotator agreement and high self-agreement.

TwoPlaneSVMbin
A machine learning classifier explicitly designed for ordered classes, ranked among the top performers and chosen for interpreting study results.<SEP>A machine learning classifier used to evaluate sentiment classification performance across incrementally sized labeled datasets.<SEP>A specific SVM-based sentiment classification model selected for subsequent analyses due to its consistent placement among the top-performing classifiers.<SEP>TwoPlaneSVMbin is a refined version of TwoPlaneSVM that partitions the feature space around both hyperplanes into bins to determine majority classes and prediction confidence.

Albanian Dataset
A language-specific sentiment dataset analyzed in the study that exhibited low self-agreement and low inter-annotator agreement (below 0.2), indicating low annotator quality.<SEP>A sentiment dataset in the Albanian language that exhibited low annotator self-agreement, inter-annotator agreement below 0.2, and classifier performance barely above random.<SEP>A specific language dataset analyzed in the sentiment study, observed to have very low annotator agreement and poor annotation quality.

Spanish Dataset
A language-specific sentiment dataset analyzed in the study with low agreement values below 0.2, pointing to lower-quality manual annotations that also influenced the Emojis application dataset.<SEP>A sentiment dataset consisting of over 250,000 tweets in Spanish characterized by very low self- and inter-annotator agreement and poor annotation quality.<SEP>A specific language dataset analyzed in the sentiment study that exhibits poor annotation quality and atypical agreement behavior.

English Texts
The dominant linguistic category in previous related work on automated sentiment classification of Twitter posts.

10-Fold Cross-Validation
10-Fold Cross-Validation is a model evaluation technique, specifically applied here in a blocked and stratified form suitable for time-ordered data.<SEP>A standard machine learning evaluation procedure where the labeled dataset is partitioned into ten folds to iteratively train and evaluate classification models.

Friedman-Nemenyi Test
A standard non-parametric statistical test applied to evaluate and compare the performance differences among six machine learning sentiment classifiers.<SEP>A statistical post-hoc test used to determine significant differences in performance among multiple classifiers.<SEP>The Friedman-Nemenyi Test is a statistical evaluation test used to rank multiple classifiers and determine if differences among them are statistically significant.

Bootstrapping
A statistical resampling method used to estimate confidence intervals for annotator agreement measures.<SEP>Bootstrapping is a statistical resampling method used to approximate sampling distributions and compute 95% confidence intervals for agreement metrics.

Self-Agreement
A measurement category assessing the consistency of annotations when the same annotator labels the same tweet multiple times.<SEP>A metric assessing how consistently an individual annotator labels duplicate items, used to filter out low-quality annotations.<SEP>A metric measuring the internal consistency and reliability of an individual annotator labeling duplicate tweets over time.<SEP>A quality evaluation metric measuring the consistency of a single annotator when labeling the same sample of tweets multiple times.<SEP>An evaluation metric calculated from repeated annotations of the same tweet by the same annotator, serving as an indicator of individual annotator quality and consistency.

Financial Markets
A specialized topical domain noted as an example where domain-specific vocabulary and task difficulty (such as predicting stock movements) cause annotator disagreement.<SEP>An application domain for sentiment classification models focusing on stock movements, financial terms, and Dow Jones commentary.

Environmental Issues
A domain covering topics such as climate change, fossil fuels, and fracking, utilized to evaluate domain-specific sentiment classification.<SEP>A topical domain cited as contrasting with financial markets, illustrating how different domain vocabularies contribute to annotator disagreement.<SEP>An application domain encompassing topics such as climate change, fossil fuels, and fracking evaluated via sentiment classification.

Language Datasets
A collection of 13 multilingual tweet datasets totaling 1.6 million tweets annotated by 83 native speakers to study sentiment classifier performance and agreement limits.

English Dataset
A sentiment analysis dataset of English tweets that demonstrated a persistent performance gap between the classifier and inter-annotator agreement.

Polish Dataset
A sentiment analysis dataset of Polish tweets that reaches peak classifier performance at approximately 150,000 labeled tweets, achieving performance close to its inter-annotator agreement.<SEP>A sentiment dataset of over 200,000 Polish tweets where classifier performance plateaued and approached the inter-annotator agreement upper bound at around 150,000 tweets.

Russian Dataset
A sentiment dataset of approximately 90,000 tweets labeled by a single annotator where classifier performance continued to rise with larger training sets.

Slovak Dataset
A sentiment dataset containing around 60,000 labeled tweets from a single annotator exhibiting continuing classifier performance improvements.<SEP>A specific language dataset analyzed in the study where normalized agreement exhibited exceptional behavior regarding class distinction difficulty.

DJIA30 Dataset
An application dataset related to the Dow Jones Industrial Average 30 where sentiment classifier performance approached its inter-annotator agreement limit.

Environment Dataset
An application domain sentiment dataset characterized by a notable gap between classifier performance and inter-annotator agreement.

Bulgarian Dataset
A sentiment analysis dataset of Bulgarian tweets reaching peak classifier performance at 40,000 tweets, but characterized by a very low inter-annotator agreement.<SEP>A sentiment dataset in the Bulgarian language characterized by inter-annotator agreement between 0.3 and 0.4 and relatively low classifier performance around 0.4.

German Dataset
A sentiment analysis dataset of German tweets where over 90% of annotations were performed by two annotators with high disagreement and disparate annotation quality.<SEP>A sentiment dataset in the German language showing inter-annotator agreement between 0.3 and 0.4 and classifier performance around 0.4.

Ser/Cro/Bos Dataset
A joint sentiment analysis dataset combining Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian tweets, characterized by low inter-annotator agreement and high classifier performance variability.<SEP>A sentiment dataset covering Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian languages with inter-annotator agreement between 0.3 and 0.4 and relatively low classifier performance around 0.4.<SEP>The Ser/Cro/Bos Dataset is a multilingual language dataset split into Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian constituent language files for sentiment analysis.

Portuguese Dataset
A sentiment analysis dataset of Portuguese tweets annotated by a single annotator, which exhibits an initial performance peak at 50,000 tweets followed by high performance variability.<SEP>A sentiment dataset in Portuguese with a single annotator, lacking inter-annotator agreement metrics and having classifier performance around 0.4.

Slovenian Dataset
A sentiment analysis dataset of Slovenian tweets whose classifier performance peaks at 70,000 tweets, with an inter-annotator agreement nearly 10 percentage points lower than Polish.<SEP>A sentiment dataset in the Slovenian language where classifier performance in the range 0.4–0.6 approached the upper bound set by inter-annotator agreement.

Swedish Dataset
A sentiment dataset in Swedish labeled by a single annotator without measured inter-annotator agreement.

Hungarian Dataset
A sentiment dataset in Hungarian labeled by only one annotator, preventing direct calculation of inter-annotator agreement.

Application Datasets
A group of four application-specific sentiment datasets, including Facebook(it), DJIA30, Environment, and Emojis, analyzed alongside language datasets.

83 Native Speakers
A pool of 83 native speaker annotators hired to label 1.6 million tweets across 13 languages, totaling an estimated effort of 38 person-months.

Annotator A
Annotator A is one of the two primary annotators for the German tweet dataset, characterized by a lower self-agreement score of 0.590 and dataset performance peaking at 30,000 tweets.

Annotator B
Annotator B is one of the two primary annotators for the German tweet dataset, characterized by a higher self-agreement score of 0.760 and consistently increasing classifier performance.

Serbian Dataset
A component dataset comprising 73,783 Serbian tweets annotated by 11 annotators with low inter-annotator and self-agreement scores.

Croatian Dataset
A component dataset comprising 97,291 Croatian tweets annotated by a single annotator with high self-agreement (0.781) and strong classifier performance peaking at 50,000 tweets.

Bosnian Dataset
A component dataset comprising 44,583 Bosnian tweets annotated by a single annotator with high self-agreement (0.722) and steadily increasing classifier performance.

Croatian Annotator
The sole human annotator who labeled the entire Croatian tweet dataset, exhibiting high self-agreement across repeated annotations.

Bosnian Annotator
The single annotator responsible for labeling all tweets in the Bosnian dataset, showing strong annotation consistency and high self-agreement.

Portuguese Annotator
The single annotator engaged to annotate the Portuguese dataset, resulting in an absence of inter-annotator agreement metrics.

Serbian Annotators
A group of 11 annotators who labeled the Serbian dataset, where two annotators accounted for over 40% of annotations but exhibited poor overall agreement.

Sentiment Classifier
A machine learning model trained on sentiment-labeled tweets whose performance ceiling is closely related to annotation agreement.

Joint Ser/Cro/Bos Model
A unified classifier trained on a merged dataset of Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian tweets, marked by high performance variability.

Croatian Classifier
An individual sentiment model trained solely on Croatian tweets, achieving peak performance at 50,000 tweets.

Bosnian Classifier
An individual sentiment classifier trained solely on Bosnian tweets, demonstrating continuous performance growth up to 40,000 tweets.

Serbian Classifier
An individual sentiment classification model trained solely on Serbian tweets, converging to a relatively low agreement plateau at 70,000 tweets.

Serbian Language
A South Slavic language analyzed in short Twitter posts, closely related to Croatian and Bosnian.

Croatian Language
A South Slavic language analyzed in sentiment classification, structurally similar to Serbian and Bosnian.

Bosnian Language
A South Slavic language evaluated in the study, displaying high linguistic similarity to Serbian and Croatian.

Portuguese Government
The Portuguese Government is the governing body that approved additional austerity measures in November 2013 affecting the public sector to prevent an international bailout.

Dow Jones
Dow Jones refers to the financial market index and entity whose related stock discussions on Twitter were analyzed for domain-specific sentiment.

Austerity Measures Approval
An event in November 2013 where the Portuguese government approved additional public sector austerity measures to avoid a second international bailout, causing significant social media backlash.

Second International Bailout
An impending financial bailout that the Portuguese government worked to avoid through the implementation of austerity policies.

Public Sector
The sector of the Portuguese economy composed of government-controlled enterprises and public services, primarily affected by the 2013 austerity measures.

Spanish Dataset Annotator
The primary individual who annotated over 95% of the Spanish Twitter dataset, exhibiting low self-agreement and poor annotation quality.

Albanian Main Annotator
The primary human annotator who labeled over 22% of the Albanian Twitter dataset, showing low self-agreement and inter-annotator agreement.

Stock Price Prediction
An application area where domain-specific sentiment classification models are deployed to forecast market trends and financial performance.

Elections Monitoring
An application area where sentiment classification models are applied to monitor public opinion and electoral dynamics on social media.

Climate Change
An environmental issue examined within the domain-specific sentiment classification dataset.<SEP>An environmental subject studied as part of domain-specific sentiment classification research.

Fossil Fuels
A specific environmental subject included in the domain-specific tweet analysis for sentiment scoring.<SEP>An energy and environmental topic evaluated within the domain-specific sentiment analysis dataset.

Fracking
A specific industrial extraction process analyzed as a distinct topical component of environmental sentiment analysis.<SEP>An environmental issue cited as part of the domain-specific sentiment analysis dataset.

Emojis
Ideograms and smileys used in digital messages, studied to evaluate how contextual tweet sentiment is attributed to them.

Spanish Language Dataset
A subset of approximately 20,000 Spanish tweets containing emojis, noted for having very low self-agreement among annotators.

General English Sentiment Classification Model
A classification model trained on 90,000 general English tweets used to compare against domain-specific models.

Three-Class Sentiment Problem
An ordered sentiment classification framework categorizing text into negative, neutral, and positive classes.

Training Data Quality
A key research dimension evaluated via annotator self-agreement and inter-annotator agreement that strongly impacts model performance.

Twitter Acquisition
The collection process during which over 3 million tweets were gathered, exhibiting sampling distribution differences between training and application sets.

Gama System
A company that collected most of the tweet datasets analyzed in the study.<SEP>Gama System is an organization that collaborated on collecting tweets in European languages using its PerceptionAnalytics platform.

Sowa Labs
A company that provided the Goldfinch platform used for sentiment annotations in the study.<SEP>Sowa Labs is an organization that developed and provided the Goldfinch platform for sentiment annotation of short texts.

Dodds et al.
Dodds et al. refers to researchers who published multilingual sentiment data that can be used to construct sentiment lexicons.

Sentiment Categories
Sentiment categories are basic classification labels consisting of negative, neutral, and positive attitudes assigned to text.

Emotion Categories
Emotion categories are finer-grained emotional states such as joy, sadness, and anger used in advanced text analysis.

Joint Project with Gama System
A collaborative data collection initiative conducted between April 2013 and February 2015 to gather tweets across thirteen European languages using PerceptionAnalytics.

Human Annotators
A collective group of 83 native-speaking annotators recruited to evaluate, resolve, and label over 1.6 million tweets with sentiment values.

Entity-Based Sentiment Analysis
A fine-grained sentiment analysis technique that determines attitudes directed toward specific entities or topics rather than whole posts.

Figurative Language
A linguistic category encompassing forms of expression such as irony and sarcasm found in social media posts.

CLARIN.SI
CLARIN.SI is a public language resource repository where the 15 language sentiment annotation datasets are hosted and made publicly available.

Annotator Agreement
Annotator Agreement is a statistical and evaluation framework used to measure consensus among human annotators as well as between automated model outputs and gold-standard annotations.

Krippendorff's Alpha-Reliability
Krippendorff's Alpha-reliability is a generalized statistical measure of inter-rater agreement applicable to different metric types and numbers of annotators, measuring observed against expected chance disagreement.

F Score
The F score is an effectiveness metric from information retrieval and machine learning, defined as the harmonic mean of precision and recall and adapted for 3-class sentiment classifier evaluation.

Coincidence Matrix
A coincidence matrix is a symmetric square contingency matrix that tabulates pairable annotation values from different annotators to compute observed and expected disagreements.<SEP>A symmetric matrix structure used to compute evaluation measures and annotator agreement from pairs of sentiment labels.

Gold Standard
A gold standard is a benchmark reference dataset constructed from high-agreement human annotations used to train and evaluate automated classification models.<SEP>The benchmark reference dataset of ground-truth sentiment labels against which model predictions and agreement are evaluated.

15 Language Datasets
The 15 language datasets comprise public sentiment annotation corpora containing labeled tweets partitioned across 15 distinct languages.

Negative Sentiment
Negative sentiment is an extreme classification category representing unfavorable sentiment, positioned at one end of the ordered sentiment scale.

Neutral Sentiment
Neutral sentiment is the intermediate classification category positioned between the negative and positive classes, presenting higher distinction difficulty for annotators.

Positive Sentiment
Positive sentiment is an extreme classification category representing favorable sentiment, positioned opposite negative sentiment in the ordered scale.

Sentiment Values
Sentiment values represent the three-class ordered categorical scale (negative, neutral, positive) used in annotating and evaluating sentiment.

Accuracy Within 1
A relaxed accuracy evaluation metric that assumes ordered sentiment classes and treats classifications between adjacent categories as acceptable, penalizing only extreme misclassifications.

Annotator
A human judge responsible for reading tweets and assigning sentiment labels, whose pairwise decisions determine agreement metrics.

CrowdFlower
CrowdFlower is a crowdsourcing company offering the 'Data for Everyone' collection, which includes publicly available Twitter sentiment datasets.

SemEval-2015
SemEval-2015 is an international natural language processing competition that featured a task on Sentiment Analysis on Twitter.

Saif
Saif is a researcher who, with colleagues, described multiple Twitter sentiment datasets and introduced a dataset with entity-level sentiment labels.

Rosenthal
Rosenthal is a researcher who provided statistical overviews for the 2013–2015 SemEval datasets.

Haldenwang
Haldenwang is a researcher who co-presented a publicly available Twitter dataset labeled with positive, negative, uncertain, or spam sentiment.

Vornberger
Vornberger is a researcher who co-presented a publicly available Twitter dataset labeled for sentiment and spam.

Pak
Pak is a researcher who studied Twitter sentiment classification comparing Naive Bayes, SVM, and Conditional Random Fields.

Paroubek
Paroubek is a researcher who co-authored a study demonstrating that Naive Bayes outperformed SVM and Conditional Random Fields.

Asiaee
Asiaee is a researcher who explored dictionary learning, weighted SVM, k-Nearest-Neighbor, and Naive Bayes for sentiment analysis.

Jiang
Jiang is a researcher who applied SVM models for subjectivity and polarity classification of Twitter posts.

Davidov
Davidov is a researcher who applied k-Nearest-Neighbor models for Twitter sentiment classification.

Kouloumpis
Kouloumpis is a researcher who employed AdaBoost.MH and SVMs for Twitter sentiment classification.

Maximum Entropy
Maximum Entropy is a machine learning classification algorithm commonly applied to text and sentiment analysis.

K-Nearest-Neighbor
K-Nearest-Neighbor is an instance-based supervised learning algorithm applied to text and sentiment classification.

Decision Trees
Decision Trees is a non-parametric supervised learning algorithm used for classification and regression tasks, evaluated in sentiment analysis studies.

AdaBoost.MH
AdaBoost.MH is a multi-class boosting algorithm tested for sentiment classification of Twitter posts.

NeutralZoneSVM
NeutralZoneSVM is an extension of the binary SVM classifier that identifies neutral sentiment by detecting tweets close to the decision hyperplane.<SEP>NeutralZoneSVM is an extension of the two-class Support Vector Machine classifier that assumes neutral tweets fall between positive and negative tweets.

LATINO Library
An open-source software library for text mining in which classification algorithms and evaluation procedures were implemented by Sašo Rutar.<SEP>LATINO Library is an open-source software project providing a lightweight suite of components for text mining and machine learning applications.

TwoPlaneSVM
TwoPlaneSVM is an ordinal classification approach consisting of two SVM classifiers separating negative, neutral, and positive classes using two hyperplanes.

CascadingSVM
CascadingSVM is a two-stage classifier that first separates neutral objective tweets from subjective tweets, and then classifies subjective tweets into negative or positive.

ThreePlaneSVM
A machine learning classifier evaluated in the study that placed among the top group of indistinguishable classifiers.<SEP>ThreePlaneSVM is a multi-class SVM classifier operating in a one-vs-one setting with three binary classifiers treating sentiment classes as nominal and unordered.

NaiveBayes
NaiveBayes is a standard supervised probabilistic machine learning classifier based on Bayes' theorem used as a baseline.

Friedman Test
The Friedman test is a non-parametric statistical ranking test used to detect significant performance differences across multiple classifiers on multiple datasets.

Nemenyi Test
A post-hoc statistical test that computes the critical distance to evaluate pairwise performance differences between all classifiers.<SEP>The Nemenyi test is a post-hoc statistical test used to compute critical distances and perform pairwise comparisons between multiple classifiers after the Friedman test.

ANOVA
ANOVA is a standard statistical method for testing significant differences among multiple classifiers, of which the Friedman test is a non-parametric counterpart.

Latinolib
Latinolib is an open-source software library or suite of text mining and machine learning applications hosted on GitHub.

Bonferroni-Dunn Test
The Bonferroni-Dunn test is a post-hoc statistical test used to compare a set of classifiers against a single control classifier after a null hypothesis rejection.

Delta TF-IDF
Delta TF-IDF is a feature weighting and vectorization scheme applied to pre-processed text data to construct feature vectors for sentiment classification.

ARRS
The Slovenian research agency whose Knowledge Technologies programme partially supported this study.

Sašo Rutar
A developer and researcher acknowledged for implementing classification algorithms and evaluation procedures in the LATINO text mining library.

Mojca Mikac
A researcher acknowledged for computing Krippendorff's confidence intervals for the study.

Dragi Kocev
A researcher acknowledged for providing assistance with the Friedman-Nemenyi statistical test.

SIMPOL
A European Union-funded research project (no. 610704) that supported the study.

MULTIPLEX
A European Union-funded research project (no. 317532) that supported the study.

DOLFINS
A European Union-funded research project (no. 640772) that provided funding and support for the research.

Knowledge Technologies Programme
A Slovenian ARRS research programme (no. P2-103) that provided partial support for this research study.

Goldfinch
A sentiment annotation platform provided by Sowa Labs used to annotate tweets in the study.

Bonferroni-Dunn Post-Hoc Test
A statistical post-hoc test used to compare a control classifier against other classifiers when the null hypothesis is rejected.

Krippendorff's Alpha
A statistical measure of inter-annotator and self-agreement as well as classifier performance used across datasets in the study.

Slovenia
A European nation associated with the ARRS research programme and the Slovenian language tweet dataset.

Bulgaria
A European country whose Bulgarian language tweets were analyzed to evaluate sentiment classifier performance.

Poland
A European country whose Polish language tweet dataset was evaluated, reaching peak classifier performance at 150,000 labeled tweets.

Serbia
A South Slavic nation whose Serbian language dataset was evaluated both jointly with and separately from Croatian and Bosnian datasets.

Croatia
A South Slavic nation whose Croatian language dataset showed higher quality when evaluated separately from the Serbian dataset.

Bosnia
A South Slavic nation whose Bosnian language dataset was evaluated in joint and separate settings alongside Croatian and Serbian data.

Portugal
A European country whose Portuguese tweet dataset exhibited two performance peaks and an intermediate drop due to topic shift.

Albania
A European nation whose Albanian language dataset exhibited very low annotator agreement values.<SEP>Albania is referenced in connection with the Albanian language sentiment analysis dataset evaluated for annotator agreement.

Statista
Statista is a market and consumer data company that produced a report documenting global photograph volume and the proportion of food pictures.

YouGov
YouGov is an international research data and analytics company that conducted a poll regarding Americans taking pictures of their food.

Instagram
Instagram is a prominent photo- and video-sharing social media service that facilitates user food photography sharing.<SEP>Instagram is a social media platform used to source user-specific food images for image processing and classification.

MyFitnessPal
MyFitnessPal is a nutrition and fitness tracking application that requires users to manually input meal data to log food intake.

Han Su
Han Su is a researcher who studied whether recipe cuisines can be predicted from their ingredients and identified common ingredients across cuisines.

Ueda
Ueda is a researcher who proposed a personalized recipe recommendation method based on users' food preferences derived from browsing and cooking history.

Yang
Yang is a researcher who proposed a method for food item recognition using spatial relationships between ingredients and soft pixel-level image segmentation.

S Jayaraman
S Jayaraman is a researcher who examined cultural diffusion among cuisines and tested the performance of various classifiers under unsupervised learning methods.<SEP>S Jayaraman is a researcher who, along with colleagues, explored the performance of various classifiers for cuisine datasets under unsupervised learning methods.

H Holste
H Holste is a researcher whose work focuses on predicting the cuisine of a recipe based on ingredients and assessing model performance with and without tf-idf scoring.<SEP>H Holste is a researcher whose work focuses on predicting the cuisine of a recipe based on its ingredient list.

Cuisine Preference Modeling
Cuisine Preference Modeling is a research category focused on deducing individual culinary preferences and cuisines from food images and ingredients.

Personalized Recommendation Systems
Personalized Recommendation Systems is a technological domain aimed at tailoring suggestions to individual users based on extracted profiles and preferences.

DJIA30
DJIA30 refers to the Dow Jones Industrial Average 30 index or its associated sentiment analysis dataset used without merging in classifier training.

Linear Support Vector Classifier
Linear Support Vector Classifier (SVC) is a machine learning classification algorithm whose performance on recipe datasets was explored by S Jayaraman et al.<SEP>Linear Support Vector Classifier is a supervised machine learning classification algorithm evaluated on cuisine and recipe datasets.

Random Forest Classifier
Random Forest Classifier is an ensemble learning method evaluated in cuisine prediction studies by both S Jayaraman et al. and R M Kumar et al.<SEP>Random Forest Classifier is an ensemble learning method that constructs multiple decision trees for classification tasks.

R M Kumar
R M Kumar is a researcher who utilized Tree Boosting algorithms, including Extreme Boost and Random Forest, to predict recipe cuisines from ingredients.

Teng
Teng is a researcher who analyzed substitutable ingredients through recipe reviews by creating substitute ingredient graphs and ingredient clusters.

Clarifai
Clarifai is an AI and computer vision company whose image recognition models (General Model, Food Model, and General Embedding Model) are used in the data processing pipeline.<SEP>Clarifai is an artificial intelligence company providing an image recognition API used to identify food dishes and ingredients from images.

Yummly
Yummly is a digital recipe and food platform whose recipe dataset was utilized to train the cuisine classification model.<SEP>Yummly is a recipe and food platform whose dataset of 39,774 recipes across 20 cuisines is analyzed to determine cuisines from ingredients.

Italian Cuisine
Italian cuisine is a culinary category heavily represented in the dataset and identified as a primary preference of the user.<SEP>Italian cuisine is a culinary category that overshadows the Yummly dataset with 7,383 associated recipes.

Mexican Cuisine
Mexican cuisine is a culinary category into which specific native dishes, such as tacos identified by image models, are classified.<SEP>Mexican cuisine is a food classification category identified by native dishes such as tacos and found to be one of the user's primary preferences.

Extreme Boost
Extreme Boost is a tree boosting machine learning algorithm utilized by R M Kumar et al. that demonstrated superior performance over Random Forest in predicting cuisines.

Clarifai General Model
The Clarifai General Model is an image recognition model recognizing over 11,000 concepts, used to distinguish food images from non-food images and detect people.

Clarifai Food Model
The Clarifai Food Model is a specialized vision recognition model identifying more than 1,000 food items down to the ingredient level.

Clarifai General Embedding Model
The Clarifai General Embedding Model maps input images into a 1024-dimensional vector space to detect and remove visually duplicate food images.

Porter Stemmer Algorithm
The Porter Stemmer Algorithm is an algorithmic process used for removing morphological and inflectional suffixes from ingredient words during natural language preprocessing.

Kaggle
Kaggle is an online data science platform that hosts datasets and competitions, including the Yummly dataset used in the study.

Filipino Cuisine
Filipino cuisine is a culinary category analyzed by the model, showing decreased classification rates at higher K values due to dataset imbalance.

Vietnamese Cuisine
Vietnamese cuisine is a culinary category evaluated within the cuisine classification model.

Cajun_Creole Cuisine
Cajun_Creole cuisine is a regional culinary category analyzed within the ingredient-based classification system.

Tacos
Tacos are a native Mexican dish used as an example of a meal that Clarifai can identify directly without requiring ingredient-level classification.

KNN Model
The K Nearest Neighbors Model is a machine learning classification algorithm trained on recipe ingredients to predict cuisine preferences across various k-values.

Rudimentary Method
The rudimentary method is a baseline classification approach that maps high-probability ingredients directly to unique cuisine ingredients.

Radar Chart
A radar chart is a data visualization format used to plot and depict the user's cuisine preferences and model predictions across different k-values.

Data Pipeline
The data pipeline is an automated workflow that processes user food images, applies natural language and image processing, and feeds data into classification models.

Recommendation System
A proposed future suggestive system that combines determined user cuisine preferences with contextual factors such as weather and physical activity.
